News.title: Mum finds out fertility doctor is her child’s DAD & ‘fathered 9 other kids after using his own sperm instead of donors’
News.content:
'BETRAYAL OF TRUST' Mum finds out fertility doctor is her child’s DAD & ‘fathered 9 other kids after using his own sperm instead of donors’

A MUM was horrified to learn her fertility doctor is the real dad of her son, a bombshell lawsuit claims.

Mary Ellen Lukezick, 71, was promised a “healthy young medical student” would be the father of her child more than 40 years ago.



But she is now suing Dr Federick Dettmann, now 91, amid fears he used his own sperm for insemination of her son, who is now 43.

It comes after Mary’s son, Joseph Laedtka Heider, was shocked to find out he had nine half-siblings through an ancestry DNA result in December 2024.



Joseph said: “Words cannot fully express what it feels like to learn that your entire identity is built on a lie.”

According to NBC News, Mary was a patient of Dettmann in 1982 and after struggling some time with her fertility, he recommended she try artificial insemination.

In December 2024, Joseph submitted his DNA to Ancestry.com and made the shocking revelation that Dettmann was his biological father, the lawsuit alleges.

The suit said: “Upon tracing these DNA connections, Joseph identified a direct genetic link to Dr Dettman’s family; that upon information and belief, this genetic information established that Dr Dettmann is Joseph’s biological father.”



In 1982 after struggling some time struggling with her fertility, Dettmann recommended Mary try artificial insemination.

For over four decades, the family remained unaware of the alleged switch until Joseph received an email from Ancestry.com about his biological connections.

He said: “What he did was incomprehensible and it was such a betrayal of trust that I just wanted to make sure that if I have the opportunity to hold him accountable for the pain that he caused my mom and the things he put her through, that maybe she didn’t even know at the time.”

Mary says she feels “violated”, saying she feels like she has been raped.

She said: “It’s not right. And I want other women to feel ok about coming forward with this.”



The lawsuit was filed on August 6 on behalf of the mother and son by their attorney Al Foeckler, with the Wisconsin Health Care Liability Insurance Plan and ABC Insurance Co also listed as defendants.

At a news conference announcing the suit, Foeckler said: “These families come to fertility doctors at their most hopeful and their most helpless time.

“Trusting completely in the physician who holds their dreams of parenthood in their hands. Dr Frederick Dettmann preyed on that desperation. He exploited that trust.”

Foeckler revealed multiple women have come forward to share with own uncomfortable experiences with the Dr, dating as far back as the 70’s.

He said: “There is no question in my mind that this man was a serial predator of women.”



Dettmann is now retired and denies any wrongdoing in a statement submitted by his legal team on his behalf.

In a statement to NBC News, attorney Sean Gaynor said Dettmann is aware of the allegations but is unable to speak about patient care because of privacy laws.

He said: “The events referenced are alleged to have occurred almost 50 years ago.

“Dr. Dettmann has no independent recollection of the individuals making these allegations and is unaware of any evidence supporting the claims being asserted.”

According to Whitefish Bay police records, Dettmann had previously been accused of assaulting a woman during a gynaecological exam in 1985, TMJ 4 reported.



No charges were issued, citing that proving the assault would be “too difficult”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson for the Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services told NBC News it does not have records of closed complaints from that long ago.

Gaynor has since noted that Dettmann was “never sued, disciplined, investigated, had his licensure challenged, nor were any ethical complaints ever made against him.”

News.title: Who really killed Tupac? Suspect Orlando Anderson’s gang shooting death left case cold for years before Keefe D’s arrest
News.content:
THE death of the primary suspect in Tupac Shakur’s drive-by shooting left the rapper’s case cold for decades before the high-profile arrest of a Compton street gang leader.

Duane “Keefe D” Davis, 63, is the only person criminally charged in connection with the infamous shooting of Shakur, 25, near the Las Vegas Strip on September 7, 1996.



Davis has boasted about his involvement in the shooting, including admitting in interviews to being one of the four people inside the white Cadillac that opened fire at the BMW Shakur and Death Row Records founder Suge Knight were driving.

Over the years, retired law enforcement officials have stated that the four individuals inside the Cadillac were Davis, Terrence “Bubble Up” Brown, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, and Deandre “Freaky” Smith.



All four were members associated with the Southside Compton Crips, a rival street gang to the Compton Bloods set linked to Knight.

Investigators have long suspected Anderson, Davis’ nephew, as the triggerman who opened fire at Shakur from the back seat.

The drive-by was allegedly a retaliatory gang hit against Shakur and Knight after the two and their entourage jumped Anderson in the hotel lobby of the MGM Grand following Mike Tyson’s heavyweight boxing fight.

Anderson was once named a suspect in Shakur’s murder, however, he was never charged due to lack of evidence.

Two years after Shakur’s death, Anderson also fell victim to gang violence when he was fatally shot at a car wash in Compton in May 1998.

Investigators said Anderson, who was 23 years old at the time of his death, and another man – both members of the Southside Crips, drove up to a car wash where several members of a rival gang had gathered.



An altercation ensued and then quickly escalated into a shootout, according to police.

Four people were injured, while Anderson and another man died from their injuries a short time later.

Michael Dorrough was arrested and convicted of the murders in October 1999.



Now, decades after his nephew’s killing, Davis is finally set to stand trial for the murder of Shakur.

Ahead of his trial, Davis has repeatedly sought to distance himself from the shooting and claimed he was seeking royalties from the interviews he conducted where he bragged about being the shot caller in Shakur’s murder.

“I wasn’t in Las Vegas. They can’t prove it,” Davis told Fox affiliate KVVU.

Davis also detached himself from his memoir, Compton Street Legend, claiming he never wrote the book and only told a ghostwriter aspects of his life.

“I never wrote that book. I just gave him things about my life and I gave him some pictures,” Davis said in a prison interview, referring to the book’s co-author Yusuf Jah.



“He just did research and some stuff like that. He and my lawyer did. My lawyer died, and signed on to it with him. I never read it or nothing.”

Davis was arrested outside his home in Henderson, Nevada, in September 2023 and has maintained his innocence.

The prosecution’s case against Davis will rely heavily on his own self-incriminating remarks, where he portrayed himself as the gang’s ringleader and orchestrated the shooting on the night of September 7, 1996.

Prosecutors have a list of 45 potential witnesses that they plan to call to the stand, including Knight, Reggie Wright Jr., the former head of security of Death Row Records, former Las Vegas Mayor Oscar Goodman, Republican Governor and former Las Vegas Metro officer Joe Lombardo, and several of Shakur’s relatives.



However, Knight, who is serving a 28-year sentence after pleading no contest to voluntary manslaughter in 2018, is refusing to cooperate with prosecutors.

“This trial has nothing to do with me and if somebody brings me there, it’s gonna hurt whoever brings me there. I promise you that,” Knight told ABC News.

“They make me come there against my will, if Keefe D’s lawyers bring me there, it don’t look good for him.

“If the prosecution brings me there, it don’t look good for them. Leave me out of it.”



A defiant Knight, who has long ties with the Compton Bloods street gang, called taking the stand and testifying against someone worse than killing them.

“My loyalty to Tupac can never be compromised,” he told the outlet.

“Me as a man, what I believe in, can’t be compromised. I’m not there to help [Davis], and I’m damn sure not there to hurt him.

“To actually get on the stand, and point somebody out, it’s worse than taking a gun and shooting that man in the head.

“Because if you shoot a person in the head, they die once. If you get on the stand and you snitch on that person, they die a million times.



“I am not going to be responsible for sending another man to prison for the rest of his life. If God’s forgiving, who am I to think I’m bigger than God and don’t forgive? Because I’m not.”

Knight believes his testimony does not matter because Davis already “told on himself” after spending years conducting interviews about his involvement in Shakur’s murder.

“He felt he was untouchable,” Knight told the outlet.

“He wanted to talk bad about ‘Pa, he wanted to just talk, talk, talk, talk. He kept talking until they put handcuffs on him.

“Everything he said and talked about, he already told on himself. So what are you going to do?



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Erase all the recordings of the interviews he did?”

Davis’ trial is expected to last four weeks.

News.title: Ukraine ‘destroys air defences’ around Putin’s £1billion Black Sea palace leaving tyrant’s retreat ‘unprotected’
News.content:
UKRAINE has obliterated air defences systems guarding Vladimir Putin’s £1bn Black Sea fortress, where he is holed up with his family.

Volodymyr Zelensky‘s long-range strikes have downed the dictator’s defences and are “systematically destroying” electronic warfare capability protecting the palace.



Ukraine has blasted electronic warfare systems and S-400 air defence systems near Gelendzhik, the Moscow Times reported.

A Volna Kupol Garant electronic warfare system, used to jam signals of attacking drone was destroyed on Friday.





Two days later, Ukrainians blasted the S-400, less than half a mile away.

The anti-aircraft missile system had fired six missiles on Saturday.

It then was left “ablaze and sputtering for three hours” after Sunday’s strike, the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ Unmanned Systems Forces said.

The powerful defence system was just 12miles from the Russian president’s Black Sea palace.



The strikes bring Putin’s war closer and closer to the raving Russian leader’s own front door.

Paranoid Putin is thought to be hiding out in the £1billion clifftop mega-mansion, terrified of a Ukrainian drone strike or a coup from his own war-weary inner circle.

The sprawling complex is said to include a restaurant, a helipad, an ice rink, a church, an amphitheatre and even its own petrol station – a real luxury as Russians fight it out on foregrounds over dwindling oil supplies.



It comes as Russia burned today with Ukrainian drones blasting key industrial targets.

And unexplained fires raged across the country, deepening the Kremlin krank’s pain.

Another Wildberries – Russian’s Amazon equivalent – warehouse was destroyed by a raging fire after a drone attack in Voronezh.

Zelensky’s drones also struck nearly 1,000miles into southern Russia where they set the Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery in Orsk ablaze.

The huge facility close to the Kazakhstan border is one of the country’s largest.



Long-range drones also reportedly targeted a strategic mechanical plant in the same city that produced artillery cartridge cases for Mad Vlad’s army.

A mystery fire raged at Rosneft oil refinery in Komsomolsk-on-Amur, more than 4,000 miles east of Ukraine.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Last night, Russia killed six and injured 19 in strikes on Zaporizhzhia.

And three Ukrainians were killed, with five injured, in the Dnipropetrovsk region.

News.title: Pubs, shops and cafes forced to close in English village as hundreds told to ‘boil their tap water’
News.content:
PUBS, shops and cafes, in an English town were forced to temporarily close down due to a burst pipe.

A water main burst in Chagford, Devon over the weekend which led to supply problems and hindered business operations.

Up to 900 properties were told they would have to boil their water as a precautionary measure due to the incident.



But the issue also meant that a number of businesses could not open.



That includes the historic Three Crowns pub, with owner Simon Court telling BusinessLive he was unable to serve food without food and drink without running water.

“We spent yesterday (Sunday) afternoon phoning and cancelling quite a few people who were due to check in as we didn’t know when the water was coming back on,” he explained.

“We also had bookings for lunch and evening meals that had to be cancelled. It’s had a major effect on our turnover for yesterday and today.”

Elsewhere, Chris Mount of Blacks Delicatessen, was also forced to shut his shop.

“Some of the shops are open, which is great, but you can’t eat anything in town at the moment,” he told the BBC yesterday.

“It has had a huge impact… We should be bustling, we would have tables out and it would be full of people.”

News of the outage came less than 24 hours after residents were hit by a hosepipe ban imposed by South West Water.



A notice by the water company, published today, Tuesday, August 11, said that “all customers should now be back in supply.”

It continued: “Our teams will remain in the area to complete the permanent repair on the main.

“As a precaution a Boil Water Notice remains in place until further notice,” it continued.

A bottled water station at Chagford Primary School will also remain open until 10pm tonight.

News.title: Disturbing twist in desperate hunt for son, 27, after bodies of his missing parents are found buried in Arizona backyard
News.content:
A DISTURBING twist has emerged after a mother and father were found buried in their backyard.

Arizona authorities have named a suspect in the case after discovering a “large amount of blood” appeared to have been cleaned up at the home when following up on a welfare check on August 4, police said.



The Avondale Police Department was called to a home in Litchfield Park, a city west of Phoenix, for a welfare check after relatives said they could not reach the parents who lived there and their son.

Officials found that the house was empty, but then discovered “indications that foul play may have occurred.”



Department spokesperson Daniel Benavidez said “a large amount of blood” was found in addition to evidence indicating someone tried to clean it up.

Homicide detectives were then called to the home, and discovered clues that led them to the backyard.

Officials brought in a mini excavator, and on August 6, recovered the remains of two people buried in shallow graves.

Police named the victims’ son Matthew Flores, 27, as the prime suspect in the investigation.

“All I can say is that he fled the country,” Benavidez said, per Fox affiliate KSAZ.

Officials have not said what country they believe the son fled to.



The FBI and US Marshals Service have since joined the investigation efforts as an international manhunt unfolds.

Police could not confirm whether Flores has a criminal history or mental health history, or if he lived with his parents, saying only that he was expected to be at the home at the time the welfare check was conducted.

“At the family‘s request, we are not releasing the names of the husband and wife at this time,” officials said in a statement to KSAZ.

Neighbors who spoke with local outlets said the family always seemed pleasant, and two recalled hearing a disturbance near the home on the morning of August 4.



“The dad there, we see him every once in a while, he’s very, very friendly but we don’t talk too much just whenever we see him, we say hello,” neighbor Alec Rogers told KSAZ.

“There was a little bit of yelling and I don’t know exactly who from,” Rogers said of what he heard on that morning.

A neighbor who spoke with AZFamily said she saw a car circling the neighborhood before she heard a disturbance.

She recalled hearing a person scream “please stop,” the day before, but didn’t think much of it at the time.



“I was on the other side of the sidewalk and I definitely heard it come from that direction. But I was like, ‘Okay, we live by a middle school, it might be nothing’, so I didn’t think more of it.”

“I was so confused and I’m honestly still so confused just seeing all this because our neighborhood is super quiet,” she said.

“I don’t even really see my neighbors for the most part. I don’t really see them come home. I don’t see them leave. It’s a super, super quiet neighborhood.



“So this is a shock to all of us. We’re all just trying to figure out what the heck is going on. And hopefully everything is good and I hope everyone’s OK.”

Officials have yet to say how long the family had been missing or how long the remains were in the yard.

“What I can say is that the bodies are in a state of decomposition,” Benavidez told AZFamily.



One neighbor told KSAZ they were “pretty spooked” by investigators digging in the yard of a nearby home.

“I never thought anything like this would go on around here,” the neighbor said.

Officials have said this was an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anyone with information about where Flores might be has been asked to contact the Avondale Police Department at 623-333-7001.

The U.S. Sun has reached out to the Avondale Police Department for comment.

News.title: Remains of lost UK village demolished & flooded 50 years ago to create reservoir re-emerges after drought
News.content:
BRITAIN’S brutal drought has uncovered the remains of a lost village which was demolished and flooded to create a reservoir almost 50 years ago.

Stonework from Nether Hambleton has emerged from the depths at Rutland Water in the East Midlands as water levels continue to plunge.



The village was among a number of small communities cleared in the 1970s before the Gwash valley near Empingham was dammed to create the vast reservoir.

Residents of Nether Hambleton and nearby Middle Hambleton were relocated before cottages, farms and farmhouses were demolished and the area flooded.



Construction of the reservoir was completed in 1976, with flooding taking a further three years, according to the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust.

More than 3,000 acres of land were submerged to create one of the largest man-made bodies of water in western Europe, covering more than four square miles.



At its deepest, Rutland Water reaches around 34 metres.

Falling water levels have now exposed stonework left behind after Nether Hambleton was demolished.

The eerie remains offer a rare glimpse of the village which disappeared beneath the water more than half a century ago.

The remarkable discovery comes as England‘s drought continues to worsen.

Rainfall across the East Midlands has been below average for five consecutive months, the Environment Agency said.



The spring and summer period has been the driest in the region since 1995, while July was the driest on record.

The East Midlands, Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire, Kent and East Sussex, and Solent and the South Downs were among the latest areas to be officially moved into drought status on Monday.

And now the country is bracing for another blast of extreme heat, with temperatures set to rocket towards 38C on Thursday.

The Met Office has issued an amber extreme heat warning for London and parts of the South East, East Midlands, East of England, West Midlands and South Yorkshire.

The warning will run from 9am until midnight on Thursday, with temperatures expected to reach 37C or 38C in some areas.



The heat is expected to add further pressure to already parched landscapes, with officials warning that drought conditions will continue until there is significant and sustained rainfall.

Tony Grayling, strategic drought lead at the Environment Agency and chairman of the National Drought Group, said: “Drought conditions are worsening and will continue to do so until we see

significant and sustained rainfall.

“We know the hot and dry weather is taking a real toll on farming and there will be long-lasting impacts on our environment.



“We want everyone to stay safe and hydrated over the summer, but we need everyone’s help in using a little less water to make sure our current water reserves last.”

He added: “Every drop we can save is a drop more for your local farmers, local wildlife and local rivers.”

The extreme heat warning comes as the UK faces its fifth heatwave of the summer, with the mercury expected to climb day by day before peaking on Thursday.

But the combination of heat and bone-dry ground has sparked growing fears over wildfires.

Firefighters have been battling blazes across the UK, including a major fire in the New Forest in Hampshire, while crews in South Wales have tackled multiple wildfire incidents.



There could finally be some relief next week, with early signs of showers moving across the country on Sunday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The rain could bring the first proper downpours to parts of southern England in two months.

But for now, the drought is continuing to drain reservoirs and uncover extraordinary glimpses of the villages lost beneath Britain’s waters

News.title: Mega-dinghy carrying 230 migrants ‘originally had 260 before nearly sinking’… as 3,000 arrive since Burnham became PM
News.content:
SOME 260 migrants crammed onto the “mega-dinghy” as it left French shores – but 30 were flung into the Channel as the vessel nearly sunk.

Despite this, a record-breaking 230 passengers reached the UK – bringing the total crossings to more than 3,000 since Andy Burnham became PM.



The 49ft craft carried more passengers than an average EasyJet flight – and cost British taxpayers an estimated £25million.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp declared it a “full-blown Burnham borders crisis” as arrivals in the PM’s first 22 days reached 3,003.



As the numbers continue to soar, the under-fire Prime Minister today promised to “change tactics” to tackle the gangs behind the crossings.

Onlookers have since described the shocking scenes as the packed vessel attempted to embark on the perilous journey on Sunday afternoon.

Passengers had all been hiding in sand dunes after paying people smugglers for the journey, before boarding the so-called “mega-dinghy”.

Members of the SNSM, the French equivalent of the RNLI, described how hundreds boarded from a beach between Berck-sur-Mer and Merlimont.



The flimsy boat, designed to carry a maximum of 40 people, was then battered by choppy waters as it entered the English Channel.

As the overloaded boat hit the waves, it sent dozens of migrants flying into the sea – forcing gormless French cops into action.

A photo released by SNSM shows dozens of young men floundering in the Channel shortly after 5pm.

Issuing a statement, the group said: “A veritable tide then rushed the approximately 15-meter (49ft) inflatable boat.

“Due to overloading, several people were thrown from the vessel – around thirty ended up in the water as the craft continued on its way.”



An SNSM boat tracked the “mega-dinghy” from 5.15pm until 7.45pm, along with two French rescue boats.

Its statement continued: “The mass movement during boarding posed a major risk, especially given that many of those present could not swim.

“With the rising tide, part of the group quickly became cut off.



“Gendarmes and firefighters intervened to bring these individuals to safety.

“Coordinating all the deployed resources helped avert a tragedy during this particularly dangerous phase.”

Gendarmes watched on as the China-made PVC boat began to buckle in the sea, but still managed to reach open waters.

Mr Philp slammed the hapless French authorities for “standing around and doing nothing”, despite receiving more than £1billion from Britain.

And Reform UK leader Nigel Farage branded the record crossing further proof of a “national security emergency”.



Mr Farage said: “At 2.30am this morning a boat carrying 230 people was taken into Dover. This is a record number in a single vessel.

“It’s yet more proof that this illegal invasion is a national security emergency.”

The mega-dinghy was eventually escorted to Dover, arriving at 2.30am today, by the UK Border Force, HM Coastguard and RNLI crews.



Larger vessels are increasingly being used as careless smugglers attempt to boost their profits.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham today vowed to “keep going at this issue”, despite previously insisting his “plan is working”.

He told GB News: “People will say to me, ‘we don’t want any crossings’. I understand that concern.

“There are further things that we are doing and we will keep going at this issue until we deliver that eradication that people are looking for.

“It would be wrong, I think, for me to make a prediction now based on a timeline.”



The record-breaking 230 figure smashes the record for the most migrants on one boat — beating the 165 total set just last month.

Last week, 173 people were packed on to a single boat, but it disintegrated off the French coast after catching fire.

The Egyptian people smuggler who piloted the boat has since been sentenced to a year in prison.

The 25-year-old man, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was beginning his sentence in France on Saturday.

It follows a fast-track trial held on Friday for “facilitating the illegal entry, movement, or stay of foreign nationals in France”.



A judge ruled that these acts were committed “under circumstances directly exposing the foreign nationals to an immediate risk of death”.

Such crimes are punishable by up to five years behind bars and a £26,000 fine.

The man was told he would be deported from France after serving his sentence, while his mobile phone was confiscated permanently.

He continually denied any wrongdoing, arguing that he was a legitimate asylum seeker who wanted to settle in the UK.

Smugglers are said to have charged at least £1000-a-head for a place on the boat, ensuring a massive profit.



At least 15 UK-bound migrants have died in the Channel this year, either by drowning or suffocating in a small boat because of overcrowding.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Three women and a man were found dead on the beaches close to Calais the week before last.

The worst tragedy of this kind came in November 2021, when 27 migrants died after a dinghy sank while heading to the UK.

News.title: Attacking JK Rowling makes Amnesty International just as bad as the rotten regimes it used to fight
News.content:
WHEN I was growing up in the 1980s, Amnesty International’s emblem of a candle burning inside a coil of barbed wire said it all.

The charity stood out like a beacon in a world riddled with malignant dictators and military juntas.



It never had the direct power to topple an authoritarian government, of course, but its stringent letter-writing campaigns were a constant reminder to world leaders: if you abuse your citizens’ human rights you will never belong in the civilized world.

Who could have imagined that 40 years later Amnesty would come to emulate some of the rotten regimes it once campaigned against.



Last month, it published an astonishing attack on 117 organisations which it claimed form a growing ‘anti-rights movement in the UK’.

Nearly half of them on its blacklist were charities and other bodies condemned for possessing ‘gender-critical’ views. It even called on the Charity Commission to remove their charitable status.

If you are not familiar with the language used by left-wing activists, being ‘gender-critical’ means you believe that biological sex actually means something, and that men should not be allowed to access women-only spaces just because they feel they are female.

Amnesty International might like to think this is an unacceptable, fringe opinion, but others might call it plain common sense. It is, after all, scientific fact that humans are divided into two biological sexes, defined by our chromosomes, not just our inner feelings.

Moreover, the majority of the British public believe that society should recognise this truth. In a YouGov poll in January 2025 74 percent said they opposed trans women from taking part in women’s-only sports events while only 11 percent were in favour.

It is also the law of the land. Last year, the Supreme Court ruled that when equality legislation refers to ‘women’ it means biological women. Thus a male rapist cannot claim the right to be placed in a women’s prison, for example.



Fortunately, the silent majority have a champion when it comes to resisting the extreme ideology of noisy trans activists. Over the past few years Harry Potter author JK Rowling has pushed back bravely against militant trans campaigners and defended the right of women to have their own, protected spaces.

She has a personal reason for doing so, having suffered abuse during her first marriage.

A Edinburgh-based charity she founded for women who are victims of sexual violence, Beira’s Place, was one of those organisations which appeared on Amnesty’s blacklist. Or at least it was until Rowling threatened to take legal action.

Not only that, she invited other organisations which appeared on the list to apply for financial support if they, too, wanted to challenge Amnesty’s description of them.



She described Amnesty as having become “a tyrant that persecutes those who don’t espouse what it decrees acceptable beliefs”.

Once Amnesty realised the possible consequences for its fundraising efforts, it rapidly withdrew its report, claiming that it was published by mistake before it had gone through its internal review process.

However, its website still carries a similar, earlier attack on pro-life campaigning groups.

In Amnesty International’s warped worldview it is apparently unacceptable to believe in any restriction on abortion rights, even though a quarter of the UK public, according to a YouGov poll, believe that the current 24 week limit for abortion is too high and should perhaps be reduced to 12 weeks, as is common in many countries.



Amnesty also raised hackles by rushing out a report in December 2024 accusing Israel of ‘genocide’ in Gaza, while failing properly to condemn Hamas for the murderous attacks which had sparked Israel’s reaction.

Hamas-run Gaza was the sort of brutal regime which Amnesty would once have condemned, so why does it find to so hard to do so now?

The charity has already lost some of its most staunch supporters. Back in the 1980s, Monty Python star John Cleese helped organise the Secret Policeman’s Ball: an annual comedy show which raised money for Amnesty International, which at that time was engaged in fighting torture.

More recently, Cleese has said: “I renounce the mob who have taken over Amnesty.”

The charity has also lost the support of Iseult White, granddaughter of Sean MacBride, the former Irish Foreign Affairs minister who was one of Amnesty’s co-founders in 1961.



She said last month that her grandfather would be ‘appalled’ by what Amnesty has become, saying “they want to go against the laws of the UK – a western democracy.

“They are now acting like the types of authoritarian regimes that they have always sought to expose.”

The decline of Amnesty is so sad to watch because the world is still riddled with regimes which torture and imprison their opponents.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

We need an organisation which brings to public attention what is going on in countries where political dissidents are routinely ‘disappeared’.

In allowing itself to be captured by extreme trans activists Amnesty has relinquished that role. We must now look to, and give our money to, other campaigning groups which are prepared to focus on the world’s real human rights abuses.

News.title: Massive fire erupts near Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport as two runways closed
News.content:
Massive fire erupts near Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport as two runways closed

Two runways at Charles de Gaulle Airport in Paris have been closed after the huge fire broke out near the transport hub

Paris: Huge plume of black smoke rises from fire near airport

A massive fire has broken out near Charles de Gaulle Airport near Paris, forcing the closure of two runways.

‌



French media reports the fire broke out near the railway tracks of Louvres train station, close to the airport, with a towering plume of smoke is visible for miles around.

‌



The blaze is believed to have started at around 3pm in a car park near Louvres, a town in Val-d’Oise in the north of the capital. Some 80 firefighters have been mobilised.

‌



View Image Aerial footage showed black smoke pouring into the sky near Paris Charles De Gaulle airport (Image: X/flabrouillere)

There has been no impact on air traffic at this time despite the closure of two runways at the airport, local reports say.

‌



French media, M6info, also reported that the car park where the fire broke out is the one used by passengers flying through Charles De Gaulle. Footage taken from a passing train shows cars ablaze in the parking lot which is on an industrial estate near the train station.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Emergency services have warned the public to stay away while they battle the inferno.

News.title: Aldi to sell £150 'garden baths' from Sunday August 16
News.content:
Aldi to sell £150 'garden baths' from Sunday August 16

The weekend brings a unique item on sale in the middle aisle

View 3 Images Aldi is selling the bath in stores across the UK from Sunday, August 16 (Image: Matt Cardy/Getty Images)

Aldi shoppers are used to all sorts of items being featured in the middle aisles of the supermarket, but the supermarket very rarely sells baths. However, Aldi shoppers won't be getting their hands on the typical tubs that go in the bathroom. The store will start selling a bath you put outside instead, which could help people with certain medical conditions.

‌



The Crane Premium Ice Bath will be arriving in Aldi stores this weekend as part of the newest SpecialBuy refresh. On offer for £149.99, customers can bring home a tub that claims to be big enough for two people to use.

‌



Describing the bath online, Aldi said: "Refresh your body. Refocus your mind. Experience the power of cold water immersion." The discount supermarket claims that the bath is "suitable for two people" and is "perfect for a winter ice bath".

‌



The £150 set, available later this week, includes the bath itself as well as a pump, filter pump with lid, carry bag and repair patch. Previously, Aldi sold a single Ice Bath for £24.99 - so this new option serves as an upgrade for those who take their ice baths seriously.

View 3 Images The Crane Premium Ice Bath

‌



What are the benefits of an ice bath?

Ice baths offer a way for people to practice cold water immersion. According to health experts at Bupa, plunging into water that is colder than 15°C has been linked to easing sore muscles, lowering swelling, speeding up physical recovery after hard exercise, and boosting mental alertness by releasing endorphins.

People should be aware that cold water immersion can trigger some dangerous side effects, such as cold water shock, arrhythmias (heart rhythm disorders) and hypothermia. It is important for anyone wanting to include this in their health and wellness routine to build up sessions gradually to help the body adapt to the cold and lessen the risk.

Cold water therapy won’t be suitable for everybody, despite what the internet may claim. If you’re concerned about how cold water therapy may affect you, discuss it with your GP before trying it.

News.title: Brits urged to avoid 3 specific drinks this week as heatwave returns
News.content:
Brits urged to avoid 3 specific drinks this week as heatwave returns

There are three drinks that should be avoided

View 2 Images You should avoid three drinks in the heat (Image: Uma Shankar sharma/Getty)

Everyone in the UK has been urged not to consume three different drinks this week as another heatwave continues. The fifth heatwave of the summer is taking hold across much of the UK, and people need to stay safe.

‌



The NHS has listed three drinks that can cause damage in the heat as they promote dehydration and raise body temperature. It is important to stay hydrated and remain as cool as possible as temperatures are set to reach 37 °C.

‌



The NHS said: "Many of us welcome hot weather, but when it's too hot, there are health risks. During heatwaves, more people than usual get seriously ill or die. When hot weather hits, make sure it does not harm you or anyone you know."

‌



Heatwaves pose a risk to people when they do not drink enough water, overheat, and develop heat exhaustion or heatstroke. To cope with the hot weather, it is advised not to consume three drinks.

What drinks to avoid in the heatwave

View 2 Images Avoid alcohol, caffeine and hot drinks (Image: EMS-FORSTER-PROUDUCTIONS/Getty)

The NHS has recommended that people do not have alcohol, caffeine or hot drinks. It said: "Cool yourself down. Have cold food and regular cold drinks. Drink extra fluids but avoid alcohol, caffeine and hot drinks, and have a cool shower or put cool water on your skin or clothes."

‌



To treat dehydration, the NHS added: "You should drink fluids if you have symptoms of dehydration. If you feel sick or have been sick, you may find it hard to drink, so start with small sips and then gradually drink more. Avoid caffeinated drinks and alcohol as both will dehydrate you."

You should try to avoid:

Caffeine

Alcohol

Hot drinks

‌



UK weather this week

The Met Office has issued an amber extreme heat warning through much of Thursday. It covers the southern and eastern parts of England, as well as the Midlands.

Met Office Chief Forecaster Chris Bulmer said: “While the peak heat will be more short-lived than recent heatwaves, temperatures widely into the mid-30s Celsius on Thursday brings the potential for impacts for some, which is why a Met Office warning has been issued.

“High pressure is now becoming dominant and temperatures will build day-by-day. Southerly and southeasterly winds will also tap into the hot conditions over Europe, which helps develop this further notable heat in what has been a hot and dry summer so far for many in the south of the UK.”

‌



There are likely to be impacts on health, potential water safety incidents and travel disruption. The UK Health Security Agency has also issued a heat health alert.

William Spencer, climate and first aid expert at the British Red Cross, said: “While periods of hot weather have become more familiar in recent years, they can still pose serious risks to health. In fact, after prolonged dry and warm conditions, it is more important than ever to follow heat safety advice.

“Simple steps such as wearing sunscreen, drinking plenty of fluids, seeking shade during the hottest parts of the day and taking regular breaks from the sun can help protect you and those around you. It’s also important to look out for the signs of heat exhaustion and heatstroke, particularly among people who may be more vulnerable to the effects of extreme heat.

Article continues below

“Many communities are also experiencing drought conditions or are in areas at increased risk of wildfires. We encourage everyone to follow advice from local authorities and visit our website for practical guidance on staying safe and supporting anyone who may be at greater risk during periods of extreme heat.”

News.title: Putin frees Ex-US Marine Robert Gilman who is 'near to death' after years in Russian prison
News.content:
Putin frees Ex-US Marine Robert Gilman who is 'near to death' after years in Russian prison

Former US Marine and English teacher Robert Gilman, 32, was arrested in January 2022 in Voronezh after he was accused of assaulting a police officer

View 2 Images Robert Gilman is a former US Marine (Image: Family Handout)

A former US Marine and English teacher imprisoned in Russia has been freed after his family said he was “near death”.

‌



Robert Gilman, 32, was arrested in January 2022 in Voronezh, about 340 miles south of Moscow, after an incident in which he was accused of assaulting a police officer.

‌



Vladimir Putin has approved a pardon for the ailing American for humanitarian reasons, US officials said.

‌



A court sentenced him to two years in prison in October 2022 but in December a judge handed him an additional eight-year sentence for allegedly attacking guards at the jail where he was being held.

The exact circumstances of his health are unclear but his family have previously appealed to the Russian authorities for his release, stating he was “near death” following months of alleged torture.

View 2 Images Vladimir Putin has approved a pardon, reports say (Image: Family Handout)

‌



Now US officials have said that Gilman is on a plane today, headed from Russia to Washington Dulles Airport. Officials said Gilman was walking and talking.

He was accompanied on the State Department plane by four doctors, who will evaluate his health. His mother, Nina, is also on board.

US envoy Steve Witkoff is due to meet Gilman upon arrival at Dulles, along with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and other officials.

‌



He will then board another flight to San Antonio, Texas, where he is due to enter a rehabilitation centre for medical treatment. Moscow has not commented on reports of his release.

In June it was reported that he had been transferred to a psychiatric ward at a civilian hospital in Voronezh after he fell into a “dissociative stupor” following abuse at the hands of prison guards.

During his time at the ward he was hooked up to a feeding tube and handcuffed to a bed, according to Eric Lebson, chief strategy officer of Global Reach, a group that's been working to free him and other American detainees abroad.

Article continues below

Gilman was one of at least eight Americans who remain in Russian custody after a series of high-profile prisoner exchanges with the US in recent years.

News.title: Anyone suffering from headaches and tiredness issued disease 'overlap' warning
News.content:
Anyone suffering from headaches and tiredness issued disease 'overlap' warning

GP has shared a health alert for anyone suffering common symptoms this summer to not mistake them as 'normal'

View 3 Images The doc tor says headaches, fatigue, feverishness, and muscle discomfort can occur with both conditions (stock image) (Image: Getty)

With more people spending time outdoors in the ongoing hot weather, a GP is urging them not to automatically put headaches, fatigue or feeling feverish down to the heat. The health expert warns that some of the same symptoms can 'overlap' and occur in the early stages of Lyme disease.

‌



The two conditions can share some early symptoms, making Lyme disease easier to overlook during the summer, particularly when someone has recently spent time outdoors. Dr Rupa Parmar, GP and Medical Director of Midland Health, is sharing her tips on the key differences between heat exhaustion and Lyme disease and when symptoms after time outdoors may need medical attention rather than simply being put down to the heat.

‌



What is the difference between Lyme disease and heat exhaustion?

Dr Rupa Parmar said headaches, fatigue, feverishness, and muscle discomfort can occur with both conditions. However, the circumstances in which symptoms develop can help people decide when to seek medical advice.

‌



"Some early symptoms of Lyme disease overlap with those people may experience after spending too long in the heat," she said. "A headache, tiredness, a raised temperature and aching muscles can occur with both, so it’s important to consider when the symptoms began and what else you are experiencing.

"Heat exhaustion normally develops during or soon after exposure to hot weather or strenuous activity. Excessive sweating, pale or clammy skin, intense thirst, dizziness, nausea, muscle cramps and a fast pulse or breathing rate are all signs that the body may be struggling to cool itself."

View 3 Images Some early symptoms of Lyme disease overlap with those people may experience after spending too long in the heat

‌



The GP added that if someone is experiencing possible heat exhaustion, it’s important to move to a cool place, remove unnecessary clothing, cool the skin, and drink fluids. They should begin to feel better within around 30 minutes.

She also said that if someone remains unwell after 30 minutes, or develops confusion, very hot skin, a very high temperature, a seizure or loss of consciousness, call 999, "as these can be signs of heatstroke". An improvement in symptoms after cooling down and drinking fluids means it’s more likely to be heat exhaustion.

What is the timeline of Lyme disease?

She continued: "Lyme disease follows a different timeline. Symptoms may not appear until days or weeks after a walk, picnic, gardening, or other time spent around vegetation. It’s easy not to connect feeling unwell with where they have been, which can make the infection easier to overlook"

‌



A circular or oval rash that gradually spreads can be an early sign of Lyme disease. It’s commonly called a bullseye rash. The rash may be evenly coloured, and it can be harder to see on brown or black skin.

View 3 Images A circular or oval rash can be an early sign of Lyme disease

The doctor said: "It’s also important to remember that not everyone develops or notices a rash. Ticks can be extremely small, and their bites are not usually painful, so some people with Lyme disease have no memory of being bitten.

‌



"Ticks generally attach in warm, hidden areas, including behind the ears and knees, around the hairline, under the arms, around the waist and groin, and between the legs. So, check skin, but also clothing and belongings after spending time outdoors, particularly after walking through long grass or wooded areas."

How do symptoms of both conditions overlap?

Headaches: Caused by dehydration and strain in heat exhaustion, and by inflammatory immune responses in Lyme disease.

Caused by dehydration and strain in heat exhaustion, and by inflammatory immune responses in Lyme disease. Fatigue: Low electrolytes and fluid in the heat, and from the body fighting a bacterial infection in Lyme disease.

Low electrolytes and fluid in the heat, and from the body fighting a bacterial infection in Lyme disease. Feverishness: Higher body temperature caused by either hot weather or a fever/chills from the immune system.

Higher body temperature caused by either hot weather or a fever/chills from the immune system. Muscle discomfort: Cramps or weakness from heat strain and generalised aches or joint pain from Lyme disease.

What are the distinguishing signs?

Indicators of heat exhaustion include Heavy sweating, pale, clammy skin, extreme thirst, and a direct correlation with hot environments or intense exertion. Indicators of Lyme disease include: History of a tick bite, development of a characteristic expanding circular or "bullseye" rash (erythema migrans), and chills without necessarily being in a hot environment.

‌



What should you do if you find a tick on your skin?

Dr Parmar says that if you find an attached tick, remove it as soon as possible using a tick-removal tool or fine-tipped tweezers. Grasp it as close to the skin as you can and pull slowly and firmly upwards, taking care not to squeeze or crush its body. Clean the bite area afterwards with antiseptic or soap and water.

"Do not try to burn the tick or cover it with petroleum jelly, alcohol or nail varnish," she stressed. "These methods may irritate it and could increase the chance of infected material passing into the skin.

Article continues below

"Finding a tick does not mean you will develop Lyme disease, as not every tick carries the infection. However, you should monitor the area and pay attention to how you feel over the following weeks."

She added: "If you develop a spreading circular or oval rash or experience persistent flu-like symptoms, fatigue, headaches, muscle pain or joint discomfort after possible tick exposure, contact your GP. Tell them where you have recently spent time, even if you didn’t see a tick or notice a bite.

"Most symptoms after a hot day outdoors will not be Lyme disease, but any that persist after cooling and hydration shouldn’t be automatically blamed on the weather. Being aware of the timing and checking for ticks can help people seek the right support sooner."

News.title: Rubbish collectors wade through sea of plastic after monsoon creates 'trash trap' in Manila
News.content:
Rubbish collectors wade through sea of plastic after monsoon creates 'trash trap' in Manila

Rubbish collectors in Metro Manila, the Philippines, have been pictured combing through a sea of rubbish after it was thrown into a 'trash trap' following heavy rain

View 4 Images Workers in Manila have been combing through a vast sea of rubbish (Image: ROLEX DELA PENA/EPA/Shutterstock)

Workers have been deployed into a sea of rubbish and tasked with freeing one of the world's most populous cities from a tidal wave of refuse.

‌



Rubbish collectors are wading through nearly shoulder-deep waters in Paranaque City, in Manila, the Philippines, following nine days of torrential rainfall that has caused the deaths of at least 16 people. Monsoon season has left the major city, which is the seventh most populous in the world and home to 27.1 million people, awash with mishandled refuse, which has accumulated in waterways.

‌



Brave city workers have plunged ankle first into the depths of those waterways in a bid to free those rubbish-choked rivers and streams as the Philippine government mulls tougher penalties for would-be litterbugs.

‌



Bin £5,000 fine warning for putting 24 banned electrical items in household waste READ MORE :

Binmen will never collect rubbish bags if it's left in 1 common area outside READ MORE :

View 4 Images Workers have been going waist deep to clear the rubbish (Image: ROLEX DELA PENA/EPA/Shutterstock)

The more than week-long downpour across the city had a significant impact, causing landslides and flooding across the north of the flood-prone metropolis. It has also seen personnel rush to waterways across the city, backed by cranes, boats and huge containers in which to stash the rubbish.

City workers who have taken up the unenviable job of clearing through the mess have been pictured wading in a sea of debris, with a vast number of plastic bottles, and even a lone croc shoe seen amongst the collection of rubbish.

‌



The worst hit area is believed to be the Redemptorist Water Channel in Barangay Baclaran, where refuse collectors were submerged up to their necks and visibly caked in dirt. Pictures show that while a huge amount of water has poured across the city, it is barely visible under the sheer extent of the waste.

View 4 Images Water was barely visible through the thick layer of rubbish covering the water (Image: ROLEX DELA PENA/EPA/Shutterstock)

As the cleanup operation gets underway, the surge of rubbish has prompted conversations about rubbish disposal in the city, with the country's national leadership at Malacañáng Palace backing proposals for harsher littering penalties.

‌



Local Government Units (LGUs) have been blamed for the surge after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr learned about the situation, according to local media, with Palace officials saying the situation was "truly shocking". Palace press officer Claire Castro said on Tuesday: "This is not what the government wants to happen. We want proper waterways where water can flow freely."

Rubbish has been a sticky issue in the Manila, which has been dealing with excessive littering for years. A 2021 study estimated that the city's major Pasig River contributed up to six percent of plastics from rivers leaking into the ocean.

View 4 Images The cleanup operation has seen Philippine authorities employ heavy machinery alongside cleaners (Image: ROLEX DELA PENA/EPA/Shutterstock)

Article continues below

The staggering total was more than rivers like India's notoriously messy Ganges, which despite its global reputation is shorter than the Pasig. Thousands of families live in makeshift houses along the major waterway, once a vital food source and transportation route for the city's workers.

The Parañaque City Government said in a post on social media that the latest dramatic images were the product of a "trash trap" which had caused rubbish to pile up.

Officials said: "The CENRO Task Force continues its waterways clean-up operations to remove accumulated garbage and debris from the Redemptorist Water Channel in Barangay Baclaran. This is after garbage from the Manila Bay entered the water channel." They added the concentration of rubbish was being removed from what it called a "trash trap" formed following heavy rainfall.

News.title: Solar eclipse weather forecast as 23 counties have 'excellent' view but others miss out
News.content:
Solar eclipse weather forecast as 23 counties have 'excellent' view but others miss out

Met Office forecasters have revealed where in the UK should have the best view of the solar eclipse as a weather front moving in means other areas may miss out

UK weather: Largely clear and hot as UK set for partial solar eclipse

The Met Office has released a map showing which parts of the UK will have the best view of tomorrow’s solar eclipse.

‌



Although the eclipse should be visible across the UK, cloud cover could obstruct the view for people in some regions.

‌



A weather front is expected to push into the northwest tomorrow, with rain on the cards in Northern Ireland and Scotland.

‌



The Met Office has published a map showing where is likely to have clear skies between 6pm and 8pm, when the eclipse is due to take place. The event will peak at just after 7pm, although the exact timings vary depending on location - and can be seen here.

View 2 Images The Met Office's map showing where will have the best view of the eclipse (Image: Met Office)

Solar eclipse glasses sell out on Amazon for Wednesday – four other ways to view READ MORE :

Next solar eclipse in UK after August 12 is in 2027 - every eclipse date listed READ MORE :

The map shows southern parts of England and Wales should have an “excellent” view of the eclipse.

‌



North Wales, northern England and southern Scotland can expect “good” conditions, whereas visibility will likely be “low to moderate” in Northern Ireland and the rest of Scotland.

In total, there are 23 counties in the “excellent” region. They are all in either England or Wales.
