BBC Weather forecast for Wednesday

BBC Weather forecasters say there should be "very little cloud" for most tomorrow. However, the BBC forecast does identify northern areas as where showers and "patchy cloud" could come.

It states: "Dry and sunny for most with very little cloud around. Patchy cloud and a few showers for northern England and Northern Ireland. Heavier spells of rain for north-western Scotland, possibly thundery."

Article continues below

Warning ahead of solar eclipse

Wednesday will bring the first near-total eclipse to the UK since 1999, and will be the last chance to see one until 2081.

Safety-approved solar eclipse glasses have been selling out online. And consumers have been warned against using “knock-off” glasses instead. Eye doctors have also urged people to avoid looking directly at the Sun, with even brief exposure causing lasting vision damage.

Only special solar eclipse glasses that are ISO 12312-2 certified for the safest eye protection should be used, experts say. Glasses that do not carry the safety standards, or ordinary sunglasses, should never be used as they reduce glare, making it feel more comfortable to look at the Sun for longer, but still allowing harmful solar radiation to reach the retina.

News.title: Police probe if man charged with Ann Widdecombe's murder involved in Nigel Farage 'break in'
News.content:
Police probe if man charged with Ann Widdecombe's murder involved in Nigel Farage 'break in'

Counter terrorism officers investigating Ms Widdecombe's death have reopened an inquiry into an incident at Mr Farage's home in April 2025 after possible links were found

View 3 Images Police are examining whether Joshua Kerry was involved in Farage incident

Counter terrorism police are investigating whether the man charged with the murder of Ann Widdecombe is linked to an attempted break-in at Nigel Farage's home.

Joshua Kerry, 28, is accused of killing Ms Widdecombe last month at the bungalow where she lived alone in Devon.

Devon and Cornwall police first ruled out any potential political motivation for the Reform UK politician's death, but the case was transferred to counter terrorism police.

On Friday, officers investigating Ms Widdecombe's murder said that they had reopened an inquiry into what had been described as an attempted burglary of Mr Farage's home in April 2025. Detectives are reportedly studying fingerprints taken from the scene, as well as CCTV footage from devices such as video doorbells.

The investigation, by the Metropolitan Police and Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London, was closed and no arrests were made. Counter terrorism police now say they have identified a line of inquiry that "was not identified and pursued by them at the time" and which "may have been relevant". The force has referred itself to the police watchdog, the Independent Office for Police Conduct.

View 3 Images Ms Widdecombe was murdered in her kitchen (Image: Lucy North/PA Wire)

Police are reportedly examining whether there is a connection between Kerry and the incident, and that Farage has been informed.

At a press conference on Monday after a meeting with counterterrorism police, Farage said: "This is directly linked to the murder of Ann Widdecombe."

Farage said he believed counterterrorism officers had "made some mistakes" in the original case but that he still had confidence in them.

The Reform leader said of CTP’s decision to refer itself to the IOPC: “The fact they’ve done that shows you they’re not trying to cover up, they’re not trying to ignore, and I have to say I have met Laurence Taylor [the head of CTP] and I did feel a great, great confidence in it.”

View 3 Images Reform UK leader Nigel Farage (Image: Dinendra Haria/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

Reform UK spokeswoman and former Tory minister Ms Widdecombe, 78, died on July 8 after she was hit over the head with a hammer 21 times at her home in Haytor on Dartmoor, Devon. Kerry was charged with her murder on July 20.

At the time of the incident at his home last year, Mr Farage said: "It was an outright arson attempt. I wasn't at home at the time, but when I came back and opened the door I found the damage."

Counter Terrorism Policing said on Friday: It said: “As part of the ongoing investigation led by Counter Terrorism Policing South East into the murder of Ann Widdecombe, officers have reopened an investigation into an incident reported to police last year.

“In April 2025, the Metropolitan police received a report of an attempted burglary at an address in the Greater London area. Enquiries were carried out by the Metropolitan police, supported by Counter Terrorism Policing London. No arrests were made and the investigation was subsequently closed, pending any new lines of inquiry.

Article continues below

“Following the reopening of the attempted burglary investigation, Counter Terrorism Policing London identified a line of enquiry which was not identified and pursued by them at the time, which may have been relevant.

"As a result, to ensure their support to the initial investigation is thoroughly reviewed, Counter Terrorism Policing London made a mandatory conduct referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct today.”

News.title: Summer 2026 on course to be UK's hottest on record, says Met Office
News.content:
This summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began, according to the Met Office.

Only average conditions are needed for the remainder of August to surpass the record set just last year.

Provisional Met Office statistics show that the UK's mean temperature for meteorological summer so far (1 June to 10 August) currently stands at 16.48C, which is 1.88C above the 1991-2020 average.

In summer 2025, the mean temperature across the country - which includes overnight lows as well as daytime highs - was 16.10C (60.98F).

It is in line with evidence that summers are getting hotter and are likely to become drier because of climate change.

News.title: Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low
News.content:
At a bakery in central London, stock has been flying off the shelves.

"I've sold, like, 100 this morning," a staff member tells the BBC. But it's not baked goods driving queues out of the door - customers are here to buy eclipse glasses.

They are among those hoping to catch a safe glimpse of Wednesday's solar eclipse - the UK's most significant since 1999 - but struggling to get their hands on the right gear.

Experts have urged eclipse enthusiasts not to look directly at the Sun - with even brief exposure causing lasting damage - and to seek out specialist glasses instead.

But online, pairs that meet safety specifications have all but sold out. Those still available either require a hefty next-day delivery fee or simply cannot arrive on time.

Even the Royal Museums Greenwich - recommended as a reputable retailer by UK health officials - has sold out, citing an "unprecedented volume" of orders.

Meanwhile, eclipse glasses have been turning up for sale in unexpected places as retailers try to capitalise on the demand.

"I Googled 'where can I get eclipse glasses but not through the post', because I realised I was too late," one customer waiting to buy three pairs at the bakery on Monday tells BBC Radio 4's PM programme.

"People have been struggling to find them all over," says another.

News.title: Watch: Family narrowly escapes home during Colombia earthquake
News.content:
A family captured video of the moment they fled their home during an earthquake in Colombia.

Liliana PÃ©rez Ocampo and her family escaped moments before their home was rocked by a 7.4 magnitude quake on Monday.

"At first, we thought it was just a mild tremor like the ones that usually happen in Colombia, but when more than 30 seconds passed and everything was shaking harder, we realised it was an earthquake," the mother-of-four told the BBC World Service.

Her family, including two young children at school, are safe.

"In the end, material things can be replaced," she said. "The most important thing is life, and we have that."

With at least 169 people killed, this has been the strongest earthquake to hit Colombia in the 21st Century, according to the country's Geological Service.

More on this story.

News.title: Anne Hathaway pokes fun at 'fake baby bump' theories
News.content:
Anne Hathaway has poked fun at those who suggested her baby bump didn't look real after a recent film premiere, telling them she had "fake hair, real bump".

The US actress turned heads in an outfit that showed off her bare bump at the launch of her new film, The End of Oak Street, in Los Angeles on Sunday.

It sparked a flurry of comments on social media, external from people saying "Why does it look fake?" and "Oh come on. That is not real."

But others came to her defence, with one writing: "A lot of people in these comments have never seen a pregnant belly on someone who has abs." Another questioned: "Can women exist, damn," while someone else posted: "People always commenting about women is insane."

Hathaway, 43, announced in June that she is expecting her third child with husband Adam Shulman.

Celebrities are often judged on their choice of red carpet wear, but Hathaway's outfit at the premiere for The End of Oak Street has attracted particular attention.

Her bump was partially exposed in the custom Atelier Prabal Gurung crop top, which the designer described as a "sculptural high-low halter top with a cascading train". Hathaway paired the top with low-rise La Ligne jeans and red Aquazzura stilettos.

News.title: Russia releases former US Marine reported in poor health
News.content:
Russia has released a former US Marine who was jailed in 2022 and was reportedly in extremely poor health.

Robert Gilman, from Massachusetts, was freed "from detention for humanitarian reasons" and flying on a US plane to Washington, DC, on Tuesday, according to Kirill Dmitriev, special envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Massachusetts Senator Ed Markey posted on social media that Gilman had been "essentially catatonic" and battling a "severe case of pneumonia" before he was released.

Gilman was 28 when he was arrested for kicking a police officer while drunk aboard a train to Moscow.

"Approximately 50 days ago, Robert was diagnosed with a dissociative stupor - a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat," Markey said, adding that the details of Gilman's current condition were unknown.

Reuters reported that multiple doctors were tending to Gilman as he returned to the US and that a US official said "he seems to be in good shape".

His family is awaiting his arrival at a military hospital in Texas, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

"I am so grateful to President Trump for saving my brother's life," Lexie Hudson, his sister said in a statement. "There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action."

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and for many people, the high streets they grew up with are "unrecognisable".

He said the plans were "shaped" by a series of BBC News investigations which exposed organised crime on high streets, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes, vapes, cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco for up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham told the BBC that the changes would make it "easier for police to close a vape shop and have it closed for longer".

He said: "At the same time we're changing the planning regime... which should stop the proliferation of vape shops on our high streets."

The prime minister added that Operation Vulcan in Cheetham Hill, Greater Manchester, cleared the area of counterfeits and crime and "proved" what could be achieved.

"When I look at police reform across England, I will be asking for a similar approach to be taken," he said. "I want the strongest possible neighbourhood policing, with all agencies involved, to rip out criminal behaviour that is pulling places down."

Burnham said he did not accept the decline of the high street as "inevitable".

"I don't see why anywhere should have to accept they have empty shops, vape shops and the challenges that come with that."

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday that many people were frustrated at vape and gambling outlets "popping up even near schools and some of them are linked to illegal activity and crime".

News.title: England set to be one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

News.title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak: When and where to catch a glimpse
News.content:
The best annual meteor shower has once again returned to our skies, and the Perseids dazzling display is set to peak on Wednesday night.

But skywatchers will be treated to not one, but two, impressive astronomical events within just a few hours of each other.

A deep partial solar eclipse will be also visible in the UK in the early evening before the Sun sets and the stars emerge. While the two events are unrelated, their timing makes for an exceptional night of stargazing.

Astronomer Dr Becky Smethurst said it was "the perfect cosmic coincidence of events".

Here is when to look up and where you will have the best views of the meteor shower.

News.title: London Heathrow no longer Europe's busiest airport
News.content:
Heathrow has lost its position as Europe's busiest airport to Istanbul, new figures show.

The west London airport said 7.86m passengers passed through its four terminals in July, whereas Istanbul Airport in Turkey's largest city recorded 8.15m passengers.

The US-Israel conflict with Iran has had an impact on Heathrow's passenger traffic with Middle East routes in July down 20.2% year-on-year.

Annual figures from trade body Airports Council International show Heathrow was Europe's busiest airport from 1996 to 2019. It lost that title in 2020 amid coronavirus travel restrictions before regaining it in 2023, holding it ever since.

Heathrow continues to operate its two runways at near-full capacity and is seeking government permission to build a third.

News.title: Fourth ex-police officer arrested over child abuse
News.content:
A fourth former South Yorkshire Police officer has been arrested on suspicion of non-recent child exploitation and abuse.

A total of 10 victims have now come forward to allege sexual abuse by former South Yorkshire Police officers in Rotherham.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) earlier issued an update to the National Crime Agency's (NCA) investigation into alleged child sexual abuse by former officers of the force.

The BBC reported in July 2025 that five women who were exploited by grooming gangs as children said they were also abused by police officers in the town in the 1990s and early 2000s.

South Yorkshire Police initially investigated its own former officers before the NCA took over the inquiry.

Among the witness accounts reported by the BBC was the testimony of one woman who said she was raped from the age of 12 by a serving police officer in a marked police car.

She said he would threaten to "hand her back to the gang" if she did not comply.

A former South Yorkshire Police officer in his 60s was arrested in June by the NCA on suspicion of non-recent child sexual abuse offences.

He was taken into custody and later released on conditional bail pending further investigation.

Three other former officers have been arrested since December 2024 on suspicion of historical sexual offences - including attempted rape, indecent assault and misconduct in a public office.

The crimes are alleged to have taken place between 1995 and 2004 while the officers were on duty as constables. None has been charged.

At least 1,400 children were abused by men in Rotherham between 1997 and 2013, the landmark report from Prof Alexis Jay into the town's grooming gangs found in 2014.

News.title: Former army translator jailed for raping woman in private hire car
News.content:
A former translator for the British Army who raped a woman after becoming a private hire driver in Scotland has been jailed for seven years.

Abdul Nabizada attacked the 19-year-old after failing to take her home from a night out in Edinburgh in 2021.

The 36-year-old, who previously worked as an interpreter for the British, Danish and American militaries in Afghanistan, denied the charges and claimed to be suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) from an explosive device detonating near him.

Judge John Morris KC told Nabizada he had committed an "appalling betrayal of trust" during sentencing after he was found unanimously guilty at a High Court trial last month.

Nabizada, a father of four who lived in the Pilton area of Edinburgh, had applied for British citizenship after coming to the UK in 2016.

He had been a tailor in Afghanistan, but also worked with military personnel, translating his native Farsi alongside Dari, Pashto, Urdu and Arabic.

News.title: Antisemitism towards Jewish children 'shocking', government expert tells BBC
News.content:
Headteachers of some Jewish schools are spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than on educational matters, a review into antisemitism in schools and colleges has found.

Sir David Bell, speaking for the first time about his ongoing government-commissioned independent review, told the BBC he had been struck by how many leaders of Jewish faith schools had told him security was their main concern - and that "sometimes education takes second place to that".

The extent of antisemitism directed at children and young people was "shocking" he said.

The report, due ithis autumn, examines experiences of Jewish pupils and staff in faith and secular schools and colleges in England.

Sir David said he found that pupils were "subject to regular harassment and abuse".

He said Jewish children and young people "are facing a pressure - and indeed one might say even a crisis - that is not the experience of other communities in this country".

The review is likely to recommend dedicated training for all teachers and improved education about antisemitism for pupils, the BBC has been told.

The BBC has spoken to several headteachers and staff at Jewish schools. All asked not to be named because of concerns over their security and that of their schools.

One headteacher said: "In recent years [security] has become an overwhelming priority and increased a significant amount. There have been weeks where approximately 90% of my time has been spent on security-related matters.

"Security concerns can become one of the many things that headteachers carry with them beyond the school day and, quite literally, can be among the things that keep me awake at night."

News.title: Girl, 6, dies and another child hurt in A12 crash
News.content:
A six-year-old girl was killed and another child was injured in a collision that shut part of the A12 on Monday, police have said.

The crash, involving a lorry and a car, happened at about 10:30 BST on the northbound carriageway near the Colchester United football stadium.

The road was shut in both directions and an air ambulance landed, while vehicles caught in the closure were turned around.

Det Insp Mark Fraser, of Essex Police, said the lorry driver had passed all road-side tests and was due to be interviewed in the coming days.

The injured child suffered a leg injury and was recovering in hospital, the force added.

The collision led to parts of Colchester being gridlocked throughout the day, while A12 queues stretched back to Marks Tey.

News.title: Golfer left shaking by 411-yard hole in one
News.content:
An amateur golfer was left "frozen" and "could not stop shaking" after hitting a hole in one from 411 yards (376 metres) - a one-in-six-million chance, according to one estimate.

Matthew Vigurs, from Droitwich in Worcestershire, narrowly missed out on claiming a Guinness World Record when he sank the shot during a league match at Great Barr Golf Club on 25 July in Sandwell near Birmingham.

The record sits with Robert Mitera, external who in 1965 at Miracle Hills Golf Course in Nebraska, USA,, external hit a hole in one from 447 yards (408 metres).

But despite being 36 yards (33 metres) short, 32-year-old Vigurs said: "I got married last year so obviously that's number one but this is definitely up there as a close second best moment of my life."

England Golf, external, the national governing body for amateur golf, believes Vigurs' achievement could be a national record, but that is yet to be confirmed.

But for any golfer a hole in one is a moment to remember and due to its rarity, Vigurs admitted he felt "stupid" even looking for his ball near the hole.

"We all hit good shots but I didn't expect it to go anywhere close to the green and I didn't know it had until we got up there," he said.

"We were looking for the balls but mine was missing.

"Everyone else was about 40 yards short of the green and we even had a look over the back of the green.

"I just double checked the hole and unbelievably I froze for about 10 seconds when I noticed the ball in the bottom.

"I rolled it over and saw my markings and we all went mad. It was surreal."

News.title: Charlotte Church's forest school set up without permission on pig farm faces closure
News.content:
A forest school set up by singer Charlotte Church on a former pig farm might have to close because of environmental fears.

The Awen Project opened in 2024 without planning permission in Wenvoe, Vale of Glamorgan.

The singer, who appeared on series one of Celebrity Traitors, applied for retrospective permission in October 2025, but that was refused.

The council raised concerns over the noise, impact on residents, and dangers to pedestrians because of insufficient parking. It also said the project failed to show how it would "conserve and enhance green infrastructure".

Church refused to comment, but has appealed to the Welsh government's Planning and Environment Decisions Wales (PEDW).

The Awen Project aims to give children an environment "where they feel championed to be themselves and follow their passions as active participants in a democratic community".

The school is free and accepts donations.

It was originally based in Cwm George and Casehill Woods, near Dinas Powys, with permission from the Woodland Trust.

But, in 2023, the charity revoked the license agreement because of "multiple breaches" of the permission granted which "posed health and safety concerns" for "visitors and wildlife".

In response, the project posted on social media that it had given its "best efforts to salvage" the partnership.

A council spokesperson said the application was refused because of "concerns regarding the sustainability" of the site's location and the "potential impact on neighbouring residents was another consideration".

There was also "insufficient supporting evidence to satisfy concerns around the potential impact of the proposal on biodiversity and the natural environment", the council said.

PEDW confirmed it had received the appeal, but said no date has been fixed for the hearing.

News.title: Murder accused X Factor singer gets legal deadline
News.content:
A former X Factor finalist accused of murdering a woman by running her over with a car in central London has been given seven days to confirm who will represent her at her trial.

Gabrielle Carrington, 29, denies killing Klaudia Zakrzewska outside the Inca nightclub in Soho on 19 April. Zakrzewska, 32, died from her injuries six days later.

It is alleged a woman got into a car before it lurched forward and hit Zakrzewska.

Carrington, from Manchester, appeared at the Old Bailey and told the court it would be "crazy" to represent herself and said she would confirm her chosen legal firm by 17 August. She was not represented in court by a barrister on Tuesday afternoon.

The Office star Lucy Davis has “incurable” breast cancer, according to a post on her Instagram page.

The 53-year-old actress, who is the daughter of comedian Jasper Carrott, is best known for playing Dawn Tinsley in the BBC sitcom.

A post on Instagram said: “I wanted to share something with you all that I’ve kept to myself for a while but for various reasons would like to share now.

“A year-and-a-half ago I was diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer, which has metastasized to my bones. Specifically to my spine, right hip and my ribs. The cancer is incurable, and too late for chemo.

“The initial lump that I felt, wasn’t a ‘lump’ as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny. I almost didn’t bother getting it checked. So I guess I’m saying don’t ignore anything – get everything checked out.“

As of now, I’m trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can. I always like to find the teachable moments in anything negative that happens. And cancer has not disappointed in that regard; there’s a lot I have learned from it, and I’m grateful for that.”

She added: “I’m not scared of whatever comes next. I’m at peace with it. I’ll see my Gracie sooner than expected, and for me, leaving my physical body just means going home. Any and all grieving is for my family; it’s far harder for them than for me.”

Beautiful famous women have something new in common beyond the same aesthetician: all of them are “looking for a man in finance”. Nicole Kidman has been seen with Michael Reinstein, founder of a private equity firm based in LA; Olivia Rodrigo has been spotted with Julian Croonenberghs, an investor with Hg Capital; and Reese Witherspoon has been dating financier Oliver Haarmann for the last two years.

A few years ago, dating a man in finance would've been something women felt compelled to confess in, say, a dark room where nobody could possibly overhear them. The act itself was almost a source of shame, one that reflected superficial values and cast you into a gold-digging caricature. Well, now it’s more like a badge of honour that can be worn with pride, a trend to follow if you want to be like one of the cool girls.

Two years on from 29-year-old Megan Boni’s viral TikTok jingle (“I’m looking for a man in finance. Trust fund. 6ft 5in. Blue eyes…”) it seems that the brainwashing was successful – did I mention that all of the aforementioned men are rather tall? – and whatever negative connotations we once associated with finance bros have long been forgotten. Cold, obsessive, ruthless, and almost always bordering on alcoholism or sociopathy, the stereotypical finance guy is hardly someone that appeals.

So, have we had it wrong this whole time? It’s a fascinating pivot when you consider the trajectory of the aforementioned celebrities’ love lives; Kidman’s most recent ex was a musician (Keith Urban). Rodrigo’s? An actor (Louis Partridge). And Witherspoon was married to Ryan Phillippe for eight years. Creative men have long been the de facto partners for famous heterosexual women, the thesis being that they were the cool, smart, forward-thinking feminists with kind eyes and good hair. Everyone else was inferior debris.

open image in gallery No more drama: Olivia Rodrigo and her ex-boyfriend, the actor Louis Partridge – she’s recently been spotted with a man in private equity ( Getty )

Now, the tide has turned. It would be myopic to say it’s all about the money, though arguably there’s a pretty strong case to be made for high net worth women wanting to be with high net worth men. For Michelle*, 33, who has been dating a lovely, kind and generous financier for several months, it marks a surprising change from the string of emotionally unavailable, non-committal creatives she’d dated previously.

“We spend a lot of time talking about stocks and shares and where they’re at today and where he hopes they're going,” she admits. “I know how much he earned last year, how much he invested yesterday and so on. I’ve never had that happen with someone at this early-ish stage in the dating cycle. But, I suppose it’s like dating a graphic designer and him sharing his latest work.” The negativity tends to stem from other people, who are quick to judge Michelle’s new partner before having even met him based on his career.

Creative men have long been the de facto partners for famous heterosexual women, the thesis being that they were the cool, smart, forward-thinking feminists. Now, the tide has turned

“Some smirk, some snark and others go ‘of course’,” she says. “And I think some of my friends are a bit intimidated by it. But that’s their issue with their own situations.” When it comes to dates, he also pays for everything. “I can’t decipher if it’s because he’s a very traditional gent or because he can and wants to. I have paid for some smaller things and he’s been really grateful and quite shocked – I think a lot of people take him for granted and as a result he’s quite scarred from the way previous partners have approached him and ultimately his wealth. I haven’t told him how much I earn.”

For Jenny*, 33, the finance bro offers a refreshing alternative to the flaky, lethargic, and unreliable f*** boys she has dated in the past. “They’re up at 5.30am, they’re off to Third Space, and they look annoyingly good,” she says. They’re also extremely proactive, booking dates in advance, making reservations, choosing good restaurants and sending links to menus. “They also let you know that they like you and take charge, so you really know where you stand with them and don’t have to mind-read as you do with other guys,” Jenny adds. “But I never have the feeling these men are going to be my soulmate. They’re mostly just nice, organised robots that look good and pay for dates.”

Typically, these men also have a deals-first mindset, which can colour the dating experience with a unique, financial-hued shade. “I tend to be quite avoidant, and I’ve noticed that the finance bros sense that and their competitive nature comes out. They really want to win the deal, and they see dating someone as a way of winning. So, they come on really thick and fast at the beginning. But then they do tend to get bored once they’ve broken me down or I start liking them.”

open image in gallery Reese Witherspoon has been dating Oliver Haarmann for years – he’s a private equity financier and a minority owner of the New York Islanders ( AFP/Getty )

Working in finance requires a fast pace: money moves quickly, and so must you. Perhaps, then, it makes sense that men in these industries will have a particularly focused and slightly ruthless approach to dating. It’s the way they’re built to operate. That has certainly been my experience; while I’ve never dated anyone in finance for a long period of time, I’ve gone on the odd date here and there with men in the sector: investment bankers and venture capitalists, mostly. On the whole, they have not been good experiences.

There was the very tall man who told me he wanted to buy a Ferrari because of the “status” it offered him. The curly-haired VC who called his female boss a psychopath and made sexist remarks over cocktails. And the French banker who bailed on a second date with an hour to spare because he wanted to take drugs at a music festival instead. If I was going to find commonalities between these men, it would be that all of them valued money a little too much, aligning it with their self-worth to mask some other kind of inadequacy. Forget about men in finance; it’s the ones trying to hide their low sense of themselves you need to really watch out for. It just so happens that many of them happen to work in the same sector.

There are other risk factors, too. “I dated two finance bros in my twenties, both until we hit the two- to three-month mark, which I think came down to their inability to commit,” says Yasmin*, 36. “Their careers were so full of high-risk, volatility and speed, that I think their personal lives became quite similar. I didn't get the sense that they were really looking for something stable; from the chats we had, that always seemed quite boring to them.”

I never have the feeling these men are going to be my soulmate. They’re mostly just nice, organised robots that look good and pay for dates *Jenny, 33

Of course, the wealth was a nice perk. “I did love the fact that they could take me to nice restaurants and I could accept them paying for the bill without feeling guilty, but that quickly wore off,” adds Yasmin. “In the end, I found them quite superficial. Their careers were so focused on money and image that it made their conversations a bit dull. Personally, I wouldn't do it again. I'd much rather connect with people I can have deep chats with and I think with the nature of their jobs and lives, that just wasn't something they were able to do.”

There are risks, however, to becoming embroiled with someone in such high net worth circles, particularly where marriage is concerned. Consider Belle Burden, who confessed to having little knowledge of her husband’s financial career in her memoir, Strangers: A Memoir of Marriage, and was subsequently left dealing with myriad losses after he unexpectedly abandoned the family home. As a descendant of the American dynasty, the Vanderbilt family, Burden had her own wealth, too, so it’s a unique case, but one that speaks to the high stakes of marrying someone in a sector you aren’t a part of.

How do the men in finance themselves feel about any of this? Well, Andreas, 35, says assumptions can obviously be grating: “The supposition from 80 per cent of women I meet is that I’m a f***-boy for being a banker,” he explains. “I’ve found that frustrating and felt like I was sometimes pushing water uphill.” Equally vexing are the high expectations on dates in terms of cost. “I had a few instances where I pitched going to The Toucan or French House for a relaxed Soho drink with dates and had their noses turned up,” Andreas adds. “The strong implication was that they expected better because I could afford more. In the end, I decided that it was a red flag if anyone turned their nose up at a relaxed boozer.”

Ultimately, everyone knows that a person’s job cannot dictate their character. While I’ve had negative experiences with men in finance, I’ve arguably had more with those in creative careers. How someone behaves in a romantic relationship hinges on so much more than their CV could possibly declare, like their childhood, their attachment style, and the nature of their relationship with their mother. It would be all too easy to dismiss every man in finance as a walking red flag, just as it would be too simple to give them a green one because of this newfound celebrity endorsement.

The best any of us can hope to do is judge a person based on who they are, not what they do. But for those who are dating finance bros, they may want to watch out for a lack of commitment – and beware their ruthless sides making their way into their romantic relationships.

*Names have been changed

News.title: ‘Aggressive and abusive’ man found guilty of harassing Stella Creasy MP on Tube train
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

An “abusive and aggressive” man has been found guilty of harassing MP Stella Creasy after he blocked her from leaving a Tube train.

Clifford Wilby, aged 63 of east London, saw the Labour MP for Walthamstow on 15 July last year on a Victoria Line train between Walthamstow Central and Finsbury Park railway station, Westminster Magistrates’ Court heard on Tuesday.

Wilby saw the MP, blocked her ability to leave the Tube carriage and started talking to her about knife crime and her “failings as a Member of Parliament”, then filmed her, before members of the public intervened, the court heard.

Other passengers were asking him to stop and got in between them, before Ms Creasy left the carriage.

Other passengers were asking him to stop and got in between them, before Ms Creasy left the carriage.

Wilby and Ms Creasy first met on a Zoom meeting in 2024 in Ms Creasy’s capacity as an MP, which was ended due to Wilby’s behaviour, Sarah Madden, prosecuting, said.

open image in gallery Clifford Wilby, of east London, saw the Labour MP for Walthamstow on 15 July last year on a Victoria Line train between Walthamstow Central and Finsbury Park railway station ( House of Commons )

Ms Creasy, giving evidence from behind a screen, said during the online meeting he “made a series of very serious allegations”, became abusive and “referred to the fact he had been diagnosed as a psychopath”.

She said he started to make a complaint about a constituent and she reminded him that she could not discuss somebody else’s case.

He became “abusive, aggressive” and they terminated the conversation, Ms Creasy said.

On July 15 last year, she boarded a Victoria line train, and was intending to move further down the train at the next stop, and looked up to get off the train and made eye contact with the defendant, Ms Creasy said.

She said: “He said ‘are you Stella Creasy?’, at that point my memory kicked in and I made the connection because I knew his face, he then confirmed he was Clifford Wilby.

“He stood up and blocked my ability to leave the carriage, he began talking to me about his concerns about my constituent, he was shouting although the tube train is a loud environment.”

Ms Creasy said it was not entirely clear what he was saying to begin with, it was about knife crime and how dangerous London is and “my failings as a Member of Parliament”, and his views on her constituent.

open image in gallery Clifford Wilby and Stella Creasy first met on a Zoom meeting in 2024 in Ms Creasy’s capacity as an MP, which was ended due to Wilby’s behaviour, Sarah Madden, prosecuting, said ( PA )

She added: “Obviously I was concerned that I was in an enclosed space with him. He was very close.

“I stated very clearly this wasn’t an appropriate conversation to be having.”

The MP said by this point she was backed up against the door of the carriage and was holding her hands out as a gesture “to say stop”.

People on the train could see what was happening and knew she was the local MP and came up to intervene because of their concerns, the court heard.

One man came up and said “she’s saying leave her alone” and was trying to get in between her and the defendant, Ms Creasy said.

She said he was becoming more agitated and was “much taller than me and he was looming over me”, then began to film.

“I was worried that because Mr Wilby was escalating, he could turn his attention and his aggression to the other people on the train trying to protect me,” she said.

Ms Creasy said she kept repeating that it was not appropriate and that she would not discuss the matters and that she wanted him to leave her alone.

open image in gallery Clifford Wilby, of east London, saw the Labour MP for Walthamstow on July 15 last year on a Victoria Line train between Walthamstow Central and Finsbury Park railway station ( AFP/Getty )

A woman was telling Wilby to stop, telling him it was harassment, and encouraged Ms Creasy to sit next to her, she said.

Another man came and stood between her and the defendant and Ms Creasy said she began discussing with the people nearby how to get off the train and raise the alarm safely.

She got off the train at Finsbury Park by exiting through another door further up the carriage, adding that she believed the men distracted him long enough for her to get off.

Deputy chief magistrate Tan Ikram found Wilby guilty of using threatening, abusive, or insulting words or behaviour to cause harassment, alarm, or distress and adjourned sentencing until September 8 for reports.

He said: “The defendant says I did not intend to cause her harassment, alarm or distress.

“The prosecution have persuaded me that I can infer and the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence is that he wanted her to feel threatened in the circumstances, that he intended to cause her alarm or distress.

“She made her own position very clear, she said that ‘I repeatedly asked him to stop, he didn’t, he was abusive and aggressive’ and it’s clear from the defendant’s own words, he did not care.

“In relation to the conduct of the two members of public who intervened, the situation must’ve been such that there was concern for her safety, otherwise they would clearly not have intervened as they did.

“His actions clearly were such that were not only causing alarm to Stella Creasy but his actions also demonstrated clearly that the was his intent, his intent by not desisting knowing that she wanted him to stop.

“For all these reasons I find the defendant guilty of the offence before the court.”

News.title: Ex-fraternity member pleads guilty to hazing pledge to death in Arizona
News.content:

A former leader of a fraternity in Arizona has pleaded guilty to hazing and causing a pledge’s death.

Carter Eslick, 20, entered the plea to a felony hazing charge after the death of Colin Daniel Martinez, 18, in Coconino County Superior Court in Flagstaff.

Eslick was accused of making Martinez drink excessively at an off-campus rush event for Northern Arizona University.

Martinez, who was pledging to the now-defunct Delta Tau Delta fraternity chapter at NAU, was found unresponsive on Jan. 31. An autopsy found his blood-alcohol level was 0.425%, which is considered life-threatening.

Under an agreement with prosecutors, Eslick would serve no more than four years of probation. A judge will determine the length and could also impose up to a year in jail at a Sept. 30 sentencing hearing.

Coconino County Attorney Ammon Barker said the plea doesn't diminish the “profound harm caused or the sorrow of Colin's death.”

Eslick was serving as the fraternity's pledge master at the time, responsible for welcoming new members. He's no longer a student at NAU.

Martinez was among four men pledging to Delta Tau Delta who shared two bottles of vodka to ensure they vomited, according to court documents.

Another pledge told police that he and three other pledges were brought to the party with pillowcases over their heads, Arizona’s Family reported.

Eslick purchased the alcohol for the rush event and explained the drinking game that led to Martinez’s death, state prosecutors said.

Witnesses reported adjusting Martinez's sleeping position and checking his pulse and breathing to look for signs of alcohol poisoning throughout the night, the documents said.

The university suspended the Delta Tau Delta fraternity after Martinez's death, and the national organization closed the NAU chapter.

The world is set to see one of the most beautiful and unnerving celestial spectacles this week, as the Moon moves in front of the Sun and forms a solar eclipse.

In many of the places where it can be seen – including the UK and Ireland – it will be the most total eclipse that has been seen in decades, and there won’t be another chance to see it for a similarly long period of time.

It has led to excitement across the country, with eclipse glasses selling out and people rushing to find the best place to see it.

But knowing exactly when it will arrive in the sky is not straightforward, and varies substantially depending on where you are. That is both because it will pass over the Earth at different times, and because timezones mean that working out exactly when that happens adds an extra complication.

Helpfully, this map explains exactly when it will arrive above your head, wherever you are.

And this shows exactly where the eclipse will be visible – and how much you will see.

Whatever time it arrives, experts have urged anyone looking up to make sure they do so safely. That includes using special equipment – and not looking at it with the naked eye, or through normal sunglasses.

“During an eclipse, the sun appears dimmer than usual. This makes it easier to look at directly – and that's precisely the problem,” the UK Health Security Agency said.

“The reduced brightness can override the body's natural reflex to look away, allowing intense sunlight to reach and damage the retina.

“This damage happens without causing any pain, so you may not realise harm is occurring until it's too late.”

After the 1999 solar eclipse, the Royal College of Ophthalmologists reported about 70 cases of vision problems among viewers. About 40 per cent of those had looked at it for less than a minute.

Ordinary sunglasses do not provide adequate protection for viewing a solar eclipse – no matter how dark they may be, the UKHSA said.

For those without eclipse glasses, the UKHSA said the eclipse can be safely viewed through a pinhole viewer or by projecting the sun’s image onto a sheet of paper using a pinhole projector.

News.title: A summer Covid surge is happening even though many have moved on from the virus
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

While overall respiratory illness activity remains very low across the U.S., there are signs of another summer Covid spike.

Emergency department visits for the disease are increasing, according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data, rising from 0.1 percent of visits to 0.3 percent of visits between July and August.

While most states have a very low level of activity, four are seeing moderate to high activity and nearly all states are seeing growing cases, according to the agency. California, Kentucky and Hawaii are reporting moderate levels in wastewater data and Alaska is seeing high activity.

Wastewater data has become the most reliable tracking method, because people have stopped testing as much as they did during the height of the pandemic.

“As of August 5, 2026, we estimate that Covid-19 infections are growing or likely growing in 43 states, declining or likely declining in 0 states, and not changing in 7 states,” the CDC wrote in a summary of current trends..

open image in gallery Covid emergency visits are seeing an uptick this month and infections are growing or likely growing in dozens of states, CDC data shows ( AFP/Getty )

Data from the infectious disease-monitoring and university-led WastewaterSCAN Dashboard also shows high activity levels in the past 21 days in the majority of the western and southern U.S. The highest levels were in cities in coastal states, including California and Florida.

The new trends come after the CDC recorded a similar increase in activity last August.

"If you look back over the last few years ... the lowest rates across the country are usually late June, early July, and then in August you start to see this increase in rates," Dr. Susan Kline, a professor in the division of infectious diseases and international medicine at the University of Minnesota, told HuffPost.

"And last year there was actually a peak in late August, going into mid-September. And we don't know for sure if that's going to be replicated this year, but it is a possibility," she said.

Experts say Covid may have fallen into a seasonal pattern, similar to the flu.

open image in gallery Covid vaccines can reduce the risk of serious illness from Covid infections ( AFP/Getty )

Although, the Covid pattern is likely more variable than the traditional flu. That is because fewer people are getting Covid shots than flu shots - largely due to vaccine hesitancy - and variants continue to emerge.

The number of adults who said they probably would not or wouldn’t get a Covid has been rising since last fall, the CDC says.

People who have Covid have a wide range of symptoms, but infections can result in death for both healthy and unhealthy individuals. More than 1.1 million Americans died during the height of the pandemic, according to a tracker from Johns Hopkins University of Medicine.

Covid vaccines can reduce the risk of serious illness and past research has shown they helped save millions of lives.

Harrods has rebounded to a profit after compensation payments linked to alleged abuse by former owner Mohamed Al Fayed had driven it to loss last year.

Latest accounts show the historic London department store reported an £84.9 million pre-tax profit for the year to January 31.

It bounced back into the black from a £34.3 million loss a year earlier.

Harrods’s previous loss was linked to tough trading conditions and £62.5 million of compensation payments to victims of Al Fayed.

The retailer said it has paid compensation to more than 100 victims from his 25-year ownership of Harrods, with more than 260 people having engaged with its redress scheme.

The latest accounts come after the company was hit by two cyber attacks last year, although the group indicated there was “limited” financial impact.

open image in gallery Harrods’s historic store is in London’s Knightsbridge (James Manning/PA) ( PA Archive )

Harrods reported that turnover increased by 1.2% to £1.1 billion for the year.

Finance chief Geoff Weaver said it represented “further stabilisation and modest growth” for the business, amid headwinds on the global luxury sector.

The group has been buoyed by strong spending from international tourists and wealthy regular shoppers.

Mr Weaver added: “While global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty continues to shape the operating environment, Harrods remains cautiously optimistic.

“Driven by our iconic brand, long-term vision, and unwavering commitment to quality, we are uniquely positioned to navigate market shifts and drive sustainable long-term growth.”

Elsewhere in the sector, rival Harvey Nichols has warned in its latest accounts that it would need to “cease trading” within a year if it fails to secure fresh investment.

It comes as an auction process to buy Harvey Nichols nears its conclusion, with Frasers group and Next understood to be vying to buy the brand.

News.content:

The neoclassical Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni sits directly on the shore of Lake Como, oozing opulence and grandeur – from the period decor to the white-glove service

Location

Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni is found in the popular Lake Como town of Bellagio. While this pretty little lake town is heaving with tourists in the summer, and gets incredibly busy even in the shoulder season, Villa Serbelloni feels like an oasis. Set at the edge of the town, once you walk through the gates and into the hotel’s gardens, you can exhale and relax. If you venture into Bellagio, you’ll find plenty of little stores, restaurants, ice cream shops and bars. The town is best visited in the evening when the day trippers leave for the day, or early in the morning. The city of Como is just over an hour’s drive (33km) from Villa Serbelloni, and Milan – with its two airports and train station – is between 1 hour 30 minutes and 2 hours by car (roughly 75km) along the lake.



The vibe

open image in gallery Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni has a prime lakefront position in the town of Bellagio ( Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni )

Opulence and extravagance are the order of the day at Villa Serbelloni. We’re talking chandeliers, neoclassical architecture, period furniture, lots of velvet and gold, and ornate furnishings. It was initially a private home for Italian nobility before it became a hotel, and it has been owned by the Swiss Bucher family for over a century now – having been passed down through four generations. Villa Serbelloni is certainly grand and has a strong sense of history, but it also feels a little tired and would perhaps benefit from an update.

Service

Service at Villa Serbelloni is certainly old-school, with staff in suit jackets and waiters in bow ties. The overall feel is slightly stuffy, but may appeal to guests who enjoy a more old-fashioned take on service. It is not quite as slick as you’d expect from a hotel of this stature. The staff member who welcomed me at breakfast answered his phone while seating me, a menu had to be requested several times at lunch, and then there was confusion over an in-room dining menu (eventually we were brought a QR code printed on an A4 sheet of paper).

Bed and bath

Every room at Villa Serbelloni is unique, with much of the decor reflecting the hotel’s 1840s roots. You’ll find gilded headboards, gold detailing, hand-sewn silk bedspreads, ornate furniture and ostentatious furnishings – this is certainly not a hotel that holds back. High ceilings make even the smaller rooms feel airy and spacious. The views over the lake are spectacular, but rooms facing the garden or towards the mountains are also very lovely. At the highest level, the suites are jaw-dropping – including the Kennedy Suite, which has a separate living area with silk-covered armchairs and a study with a view over the lake, and the expansive Franz Liszt Imperial Suite, made up of four adjoining rooms.

open image in gallery Decor combines gold detailing, silk bedspreads and ornate furniture ( Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni )



Food and drink

Restaurant Goletta has a stunning lakefront location, looking out across the water towards the mountain Monte Tremezzo above the town of Griante. Here you’ll find casual dining with burgers, focaccia sandwiches, fresh salads and pastas.

open image in gallery Restaurant Goletta overlooks Monte Tremezzo above the town of Griante ( Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni )

Fine dining can be found at the Mistral Restaurant, which also enjoys those beautiful lake views. The seven-course tasting menu is standout, and dinner here is a full experience. While the spaghetti with wild blue lobster made tableside is impressive, the liquid nitrogen ice cream emerging from a fog of ice crystals is a true spectacle.

There’s also a cosy bar with a snacks menu and a good selection of cocktails. Breakfast is a grand affair, served in the hotel's royal ballroom complete with dazzling chandeliers, orchids and a buffet offering that includes pastries, cereals, fruits, cold meats and cheeses, as well as eggs, bacon, beans and other hot options.

Facilities

Villa Serbelloni’s outdoor swimming pool sits right in front of the lake, and there is a private beach club with sun loungers, umbrellas and a swimming area with a diving board and swim platform.

open image in gallery The indoor pool at the spa ( Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni )

The hotel’s Luce del Lago spa stretches across 1,500 square metres and features a blue marble hammam, a private spa suite and relaxation areas with chromotherapy. There is a wide selection of treatments, including massages and facials, as well as a hair stylist and nail salon. In the subterranean spa you’ll also find an indoor swimming pool and a separate children’s pool.

The focus at Villa Serbelloni is relaxing activity rather than rigorous exercise. Excursions can be organised by the concierge, including boat tours, Nordic walking and a visit to the nearby Gardens of Villa Melzi, while Villa Serbelloni’s own beautiful gardens are very pleasant to stroll around. For those keen for a bit of a runaround, there is both a tennis and squash court.



Accessibility

The ground floor suites are designed for guests with restricted mobility.

Family friendly?

Yes. There is an indoor children’s swimming pool, along with a playground in the gardens with a climbing frame, slide and swings, as well as a basketball net. Babysitting can be arranged upon request.

Pet policy

Dogs and other domestic pets are allowed at Villa Serbelloni in some rooms with prior arrangement. There is a fee of €60 per pet, per night. A maximum of one pet per room is allowed, and animals are not allowed in some public areas, including the spa, private beach, and swimming pool areas.

Check-in/check-out

Check-in is at 2pm, check-out is 12 noon.

open image in gallery Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni’s outdoor pool sits right in front of the lake ( Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni )

At a glance

Best thing: The privileged Bellagio location – without the crowds.

Perfect for: Travellers who enjoy extravagance.

Not right for: Anyone who prefers their luxury to be understated.

Instagram from: The gardens looking out over the lake.

Address: Via Teresio Olivelli, 1, 22021 Bellagio CO, Italy

Phone: +39 031 950216

Website: villaserbelloni.com



Annabel was a guest of Villa Serbelloni.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football launched on August 10, 2026. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.
