Palace are also finalising a deal to sign Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise for £21m. The Israel right-back had his medical on Sunday and is expected to sign a five-year contract. The 21-year-old’s move to Internazionale broke down last month after he failed a medical.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 3: Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

It was the day after the final game of last season at Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base and, before clearing his belongings on his last day in the building, the departing head coach, Andoni Iraola, spent a couple of hours in his office chewing the fat with his successor, Marco Rose, talking players, pubs and tactics. The story goes that, with time moving on, Tiago Pinto, the club’s sporting director, knocked on the door to advise them there were other things to tackle.

It was an interesting scenario that speaks volumes of the respect between the pair. Long before joining Bournemouth, Iraola cited Rose’s Borussia Mönchengladbach side as one of his favourite teams to watch, the German’s “vertical football” helping them qualify for the Champions League in Rose’s first season in charge.

Rose accepts that Iraola, in absorbing the sales of key players totalling more than £250m last season and qualifying for Europe for the first time, has set a high bar. Remarkably, Bournemouth did not lose a game after the sale of Antoine Semenyo in the second week of January. Rose put it succinctly during pre-season in Austria. “Andoni didn’t leave a lot of space to improve,” he said. “Pressure’s on.”

In his first session, Rose told the players he loved the way they attacked the Premier League last season. Playing in the Europa League, however, represents uncharted territory for a team in the second tier as recently as four years ago. It is why Bournemouth’s hierarchy contacted peers at Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest to understand the realities of juggling the Thursday-Sunday rhythm the competition will bring. Rose is close friends with Oliver Glasner, who is now at Forest, but won the Conference League last season with Palace. “We are not going to Europe just to enjoy, we want to be competitive,” Rose said. “We are not there just to watch.”

Unlike last summer, so far they have retained all key players, chiefly Alex Scott, Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, the 20-year-old forward who breezed into double figures in his debut Premier League season and the club consider a generational talent. Kroupi attracted serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, among other European superpowers, but a freak foot injury during a pre-season drill means he is sidelined for at least three months.

At the end of the season, Bournemouth earmarked a centre-back to replace Marcos Senesi and a striker to compete with Evanilson as key priorities and by the start of August the club had recruited Álvaro Rodríguez, whom Rose wanted to sign at Leipzig, and António Silva from Elche and Benfica respectively. Juanlu Sánchez joined from Sevilla to provide competition for Adam Smith, the evergreen 35-year-old into his 14th season at the club, and will also fill the void left by Álex Jiménez, who has joined Fiorentina on loan with an option to sign permanently because he remains suspended in England while under investigation by the Football Association.

Off-field picture

The smallest stadium in the Premier League has been a building site this summer, with the club working to ensure their 11,357-seater ground complies with Uefa regulations. There has been a wider facelift, too, with every seat being replaced, while they are filling in two corners to increase the capacity by 800 this season. Playing in Europe brings the challenge of meeting Uefa’s squad-cost ratio (SCR) rules, which caps on-pitch spending at 70% of a club’s revenue. Bournemouth finished the 2025-26 season at 82% and they continue to work towards meeting the threshold. Last month the academy was awarded category one status, four years after being category three.

Owner-fan relationship

The American billionaire Bill Foley described himself as a dictator upon buying the club approaching four years ago, but supporters are grateful for his naked ambition. Foley, who made his fortune in insurance, is forthright and somewhat prophetic. In 2023, he said the club would play in Europe within five years – and achieved it in three. It was a similar story with Vegas Golden Knights, whom he vowed would win the Stanley Cup within six years of him launching the ice hockey franchise in 2017 – they won it in their sixth season. Foley recently added rugby union’s Exeter Chiefs to his sporting stable, which extends to Lorient, Auckland FC and Moreirense. Not every decision is universally popular but Foley, who turns 82 in December and predominantly splits his time between California and Vegas, puts his money where his mouth is.

The manager

As a defender, Marco Rose was schooled by Jürgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel at Mainz, and Ralf Rangnick at Hannover, so had quite the education before beginning his coaching career at home town club Lokomotive Leipzig. Klopp told Rose, after promotion to the Bundesliga in 2004, that he would excel in the dugout and he has since managed some of the biggest names: Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham at Borussia Dortmund, Dominik Szoboszlai and Dani Olmo at RB Leipzig. Rose has been compared to Klopp and, naturally, Iraola, given his appetite for high-energy tactics. Bournemouth routed Genoa 10-1 in pre-season so, could his style be even more aggressive than Iraola’s? “I would say [to be] even more aggressive than Andoni is quite difficult,” came the reply. His grandfather, Walter Rose, represented Germany in 1937.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen António Silva has all the attributes to be a bargain buy for Bournemouth. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

These days, £50m is about the going rate for an elite defender. Tottenham paid £52m to sign Jan Paul van Hecke. Chelsea paid the same fee to take Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace. Bournemouth pocketed £50m when Dean Huijsen joined Real Madrid last year, though that price was set by a release clause. They are deals that make Bournemouth’s £25.7m purchase of António Silva, a 22-year-old who has been a regular at Benfica since breaking into the team and has experience in the Champions League, Europa League and 20 caps for Portugal, appear a snip. Silva, who is right-footed but prefers to play as a left-centre back, is a direct replacement for Senesi.

Stat attack

Bournemouth scored nine goals from Opta-defined counterattacks last season, the joint most in the Premier League. But their threat was varied; in only two of their preceding eight top-flight campaigns did they score more set-piece goals than the 14 they managed in 2025-26. It is very rare for a team to be so productive on both fronts.

Set for a breakthrough

It was a November night of ecstasy when Scotland qualified for the World Cup for the first time in 28 years, but for Ben Gannon-Doak it was a bittersweet evening and one that curtailed his club season. The 20-year-old was forced off after 21 minutes, replaced by Kenny McLean who capped the scoring in style. A £25m arrival from Liverpool last August, Gannon-Doak featured in all three of Scotland’s World Cup matches, starting the first and last, and has impressed in pre-season. After being limited to 113 minutes in eight league appearances as a substitute last campaign, there is optimism Gannon-Doak will make his mark.

World Cup impact

Rayan became the first Brazilian teenager to start a World Cup match since Marco Antônio in 1970 when he was named in Carlo Ancelotti’s starting XI for their Group C game against Scotland. The then 19-year-old, signed from Vasco de Gama in January, set up Vinícius Júnior for Brazil’s opener in the 3-0 win and afterwards swapped shirts with Gannon-Doak. Tyler Adams enhanced his reputation, impressing for the USA en route to the last 16. Two new members of Bournemouth’s coaching staff, the set-piece coach, Nicolas Gagnon, and goalkeeping coach, Frederic de Boever, worked with Canada and Belgium respectively. Alex Scott’s inclusion in Tuchel’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida spoke volumes of the Guernsey-born midfielder’s wider standing.

Sports.title: Ronald Araujo likened to loan signing involved in epic Liverpool transfer mistake
Sports.content:
Liverpool's surprise deal for Uruguay centre-back Ronald Araujo has shades of a deal the club did over 20 years ago for Nicolas Anelka.

The Barcelona captain has completed a season-long loan to Anfield in a move which carries an element of risk for both the club and player.



5 Liverpool are not paying Barcelona a loan fee but will cover the entirety of Araujo's salary Credit: Getty

The Merseyside switch represents a fresh start for Araujo, who agreed to take a pay cut to facilitate his exit from the Nou Camp.

The 27-year-old voiced his struggles with his mental health last campaign, which led to him taking an enforced break from football.

Following his red card in Barcelona's 3-0 loss to Chelsea in the Champions League on November 25, Araujo did not play again until the Spanish Super Cup final on January 11.



The defender's temporary stint in England does carry an option to make the transfer permanent for around £47.14million (€55m).

However, Liverpool's new No.33 must first vindicate the calculated gamble which the Reds have taken on him to solve their injury crisis.



Before Araujo's arrival, Andoni Iraola only had Virgil van Dijk as his only fit senior centre-back just two weeks before the opening game.

The club captain is now 35-years-old, and has played more minutes for club and country than any other player in Europe's top five leagues since June 2025.



His former defensive partner Ibrahima Konate joined Real Madrid, with Joe Gomez sustaining another injury in pre-season last month.

Giovanni Leoni is still not available after he suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament on his Liverpool debut last September.

New signing Jeremy Jacquet is yet to make his first appearance due to being hampered by a knee problem, having missed the bulk of the second half of last season with a shoulder issue.

5 Araujo only made 11 league starts last season as Barcelona were crowned LaLiga champions Credit: Getty



Young defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe has impressed in pre-season, but failure to secure a UK work permit means he'll have to be loaned.

Liverpool also remain short at right-back, with Conor Bradley a long-term absentee, which led to calls for defensive reinforcements.

Araujo can play at centre-back or right-back - which suggests that Iraola won't be tipping back into the market for more defenders.

Araujo to Liverpool deal like Anelka

The Telegraph's Merseyside Football Reporter Dom King told talkSPORT Breakfast duo Andy Townsend and Jeff Stelling: "I've been sort of trying to look for reference points back in Liverpool's past and what sort of does this chime with?



"And the one that I've come closest to is Nicolas Anelka back in 2001. I remember when Liverpool got him on loan. They signed him at Christmas, the same day as they signed Milan Baros.

5 Danny Murphy believes that Liverpool would have won the league if they signed Anelka permanently Credit: Getty

"I remember the stories of why had Liverpool signed Anelka?" King continued on talkSPORT.

"He'd obviously gone from Arsenal to Real Madrid, things hadn't worked out there, he had a reputation.



"But he came in, and he was absolutely fantastic for six months. And it was one of [Gérard] Houllier's biggest mistakes that he didn't sign him permanently when he could have done it.

"He allowed Nicolas Anelka to go to Manchester City.

"But the point I'm making is Anelka arrived at Liverpool with a pedigree of playing at the top, of knowing what quality football is.

"And he showed that in the right surroundings. Now, Araujo has had difficulties at Barcelona, but I don't think anybody would dispute the quality that he's got there.

"He was captain of a Barcelona team that's won the league. Now, that says everything about him. He can clearly play football."



5 Anelka made a real impression during his time at Liverpool Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Gerrard says Liverpool made transfer mistake with Anelka

As mentioned, Liverpool had the opportunity to sign Anelka after the forward spent the second half of the 2001/02 season on loan from Paris Saint-Germain.

The Frenchman had previously spent two-and-a-half seasons with Arsenal, where he scored 23 Premier League goals from 65 matches.

Even though Anelka netted just four times for the Reds, talkSPORT's Danny Murphy believes Liverpool would have gone on to win the title had they turned the loan into a permanent stay.



Instead, then-manager Houllier chose to sign El Hadji Diouf in a decision Steven Gerrard claimed summed up the poor recruitment at the club during his time as captain.

Diouf arrived at Anfield in June 2002 off the back of a stellar World Cup for Senegal.

5 Diouf was not a popular figure in his time at Liverpool Credit: AFP via Getty

The striker began his tournament with a man-of-the-match display for the Lions of Teranga in their shock 1-0 win over reigning champions France.



Yet he scored just six goals from 80 appearances across all competitions for Liverpool and was famously involved in a bust-up with iconic skipper Gerrard.

Diouf, who failed to find the net in 33 appearances during his second and final season for the club, was then shipped off to Bolton.

Sports.title: Where to watch Arsenal vs Como: Gunners legend returns as Bruno Guimaraes looks set for debut
Sports.content:
Where to watch Arsenal vs Como: Gunners legend returns as Bruno Guimaraes looks set for debut

Arsenal will reunite with Cesc Fabregas when they welcome Como for one final pre-season friendly.

World Cup, Euros and Premier League winner Fabregas will appear at the Emirates Stadium for the first time as a manager this week.



3 Fabregas is on his way back to his old stomping ground Credit: Getty

The Spain legend made 303 appearances for Arsenal during his playing career before successful spells at Barcelona and Chelsea.

Now in the dugout, Fabregas is excelling at Italian outfit Como having progressed from their youth side to the first team.

A fourth-place finish in Serie A last season granted them qualification for the Champions League for the first time in their history.



Fabregas will therefore be up against Europe's best, and what better way to prepare than playing his former club.

Where to watch Arsenal vs Como

This pre-season friendly will take place on Wednesday, August 12, and kick-off is scheduled for 7:30pm.



Fans in the UK and United States can watch the match for free on the Arsenal YouTube channel.

For those unable to watch, you can follow the latest news of the clash on talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com.



You can tune into talkSPORT via our website, on DAB digital radio, a smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

On the talkSPORT app, you can download and listen to all of our live commentaries this summer and beyond.

The talkSPORT YouTube channel, Facebook and X account will also provide the latest news, views and analysis.

3 Guimaraes could bank his first minutes as an Arsenal player Credit: Getty



What is the Arsenal v Como team news?

Arsenal fans could be set to get a first glimpse of Bruno Guimaraes after his £75million move from Newcastle United.

The Brazilian midfielder was unveiled to fans before their defeat to Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, but did not play.

Guimaraes could make his debut against Como, although Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke may still be rested.

Trevoh Chalobah has just signed for Como from his boyhood club Chelsea in a move worth around £31m.



However, like the aforementioned Arsenal quartet, he may remain out of action following his World Cup participation with England.

Arsenal may also rest key players ahead of the Community Shield against Manchester City on Sunday, live on talkSPORT.

3 Arsenal are just days away from their Premier League title defence Credit: Getty

Arsenal's pre-season results

Two months after their Champions League final heartbreak against Paris Saint-Germain, Arsenal made a strong start to their summer.



New signing Christos Tzolis was among the scorers as they thrashed Girona 4-1, with starlet Max Dowman also netting.

However, a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis followed before the lost 3-2 at home against Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

After facing Como and City, Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence at home to Coventry City on August 21, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Dusan Vlahovic told the Premier League club he should join after two months unemployed
Sports.content:
Dusan Vlahovic told the Premier League club he should join after two months unemployed

Chelsea have been told that Dusan Vlahovic would have been a good signing for them.

The Serbian striker is a free agent, having left Juventus at the expiry of his contract earlier this summer.

4 Vlahovic's decline is hard to pinpoint why, but he was once one of the most highly rated forwards in the world Credit: Getty

Vlahovic has long been linked with a Premier League transfer, with Arsenal missing out on him before he decided to join Juventus.

However, with only his wages to cover, we could eventually see the striker in the English top flight.

But numerous reports suggest that the 26-year-old is now on the cusp of joining Turkish club Besiktas.

One of the reasons that many Premier League clubs swerved him in the past was due to his reportedly extortionate wages of over £300,000 per week.

However, European football expert Andy Brassell thinks Chelsea would have been a good move for Vlahovic.

On Vlahovic's future, Brassell told talkSPORT.com's Joe Brophy: "It's very likely to be Besiktas.

"They made an offer for him a while ago, and obviously they're playing with some money that they didn't spend on Mo Salah despite the fact they've done that Trump thing. 'We were never interested in the first place.' Yeah, not sure about that.

"They've definitely got a few euros to spend, a few tax-free euros if you're Dusan Vlahovic. He's gonna get a better salary there than he would get anywhere else.

"It's clear that he would take less money for what he sees as a more exciting sporting project, but I think he's been unpleasantly surprised by the lack of interest or the lack of concrete interest that there has been for a guy who we know has got great ability, we know is a good goal scorer and is as we say, without contract at the moment, I mean the type of speaking.

"He's been technically unemployed for nearly six weeks, so it is a little bit of a surprise to me. I would have thought an Atletico [Madrid] or a Newcastle [United] would have made him an offer.

4 Vlahovic managed seven Serie A goals in 19 games last year Credit: Getty

"Football's a small community and bad news travels fast, but clearly there is a sense that people are either unconvinced by his fitness or his potential to reach that next level.

"It's not been a great time at Juventus for him. He's not met expectations. Although he's been really good at various points, he was sort of saying it wouldn't take a huge pay cut to go back to Juventus.

"They moved on, they went and signed Randal Kolo Muani, that's almost ruled out him going back there on a cut-price deal.

"So he's been left with what he's left with, which is probably Besiktas. But if I was a Premier League team, not necessarily Newcastle, by the way, I wonder if he'd be a decent signing for Chelsea.

"To be honest, I know they've been interested before, but if they could get him for half what he was earning at Juventus... he was earning a fortune at Juventus last season on a sort of short-term deal.

"I would think that's probably quite a good deal all around. Clearly they don't feel the same, but I think he would be a very palatable gamble for a Premier League team because at his best he's really good."

4 Chelsea didn't look at Vlahovic again this summer despite holding previous interest Credit: Getty

What went wrong?

Vlahovic finished his Juventus career with a ratio of over one goal every three games, ending with 68 goals from 168 appearances.

He did suffer from injuries, with abductor problems the main issues across his time in Turin.

In total, he missed nearly a year of action during his spell with the Italian giants.

Vlahovic has also been with Juventus during a lean period for the club.

They won one Coppa Italia in the 2023/24 campaign and nothing else while he was there.

Chelsea's attacking options

Chelsea currently have four strikers on the books ahead of the new season, which they start off against Fulham, live on talkSPORT.

4 Vlahovic still has time to recover his career, but he won't be in a top European league Credit: Getty

Joao Pedro is expected to be the main man leading the line for Xabi Alonso's side. The Brazilian has been in great form in pre-season.

Danny Welbeck has joined from Brighton for a minimal fee having scored 13 goals in the Premier League last term and will bring experience to the forward line.

Then there is the returning Nicolas Jackson, who spent last season on loan with Bayern Munich. The German champions opted against signing him permanently, though.

The Senegalese international has been linked with a move away to reunite with former Villarreal boss Unai Emery at Aston Villa, but he could stay and has looked sharp in pre-season.

Liam Delap is set to head into his second season with the Blues despite scoring just one goal in the Premier League during his first campaign.

He has been told he can leave the club this summer in search for more game time.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca reveals unusual rule that bans Erling Haaland from being Man City captain
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has bizarrely ruled out Erling Haaland becoming his new captain at Manchester City - because he scores too many goals.

As Maresca gears up for the start of his first season as City boss, he is currently weighing up who to appoint as skipper following Bernardo Silva’s departure this summer.



5 Haaland has a leadership role at Man City and has previously captained the side Credit: AFP

Goal machine Haaland is among the lead candidates to take the armband, alongside Ruben Dias and Rodri - with the trio part of the club's leadership group last season, while Phil Foden has also been given an outside chance.

And the Norwegian's hopes of becoming captain might have been boosted recently, with Rodri looking set to depart for Barcelona.

Haaland has certainly led by example in his performances since his arrival at the Etihad in 2022.



He has plundered in a staggering 162 goals in this time, firing the Citizens to three Premier League titles and the 2023 Champions League among his nine major honours with the club.

However, it turns out Haaland's exploits in front of goal could actually prevent him from being handed the City armband.



Strict criteria

Maresca recently addressed the possibility of Haaland leading his team out, and revealed a unique reason which could prevent this.

Asked if Haaland is a leading candidate to become City’s new skipper, he told reporters: "Erling was one of the first to send a message when I joined the club.



“At Leicester and Chelsea, I had a rule that when we scored, the captain had to come to the bench not to celebrate for instructions.

“But if he scores, then he can celebrate.

“So if Erling is the captain, we have a problem. F****** hell, can you imagine?”

5 Enzo Maresca has rather specific requirements for a captain in his team Credit: Getty

5 Ruben Dias is the pick of many to become City's next captain, and has already led the side out in pre-season Credit: Getty



While Maresca seemingly ruled Haaland of contention for the captaincy, defender Dias is expected to get the armband instead.

And the ex-Chelsea boss' system has already been showcased during Man City’s pre-season tour of the Far East, as he pointed to a recent win over a K League All Stars XI where Dias captained the side.

Maresca said: “If you saw the game on Wednesday, when we scored the first goal, Ruben came over to the bench.

“I think even if it is two or three minutes, there is always something to adjust.”



Stick to scoring goals

Maresca's intriguing comments about Haaland and a leadership role sparked a discussion on talkSPORT Breakfast, with Gabby Agbonlahor and Jeff Stelling debating whether he could lead from the front.

And both agreed that while the 26-year-old possesses leadership qualities, they felt his main priority should remain scoring goals.

5 Scoring goals has been the story of Haaland's Man City career, who boasts three Premier League Golden Boot awards

Agbonlahor began: “I think strikers shouldn't be captain, to be honest.



"I think concentrate on scoring goals. I’m old school, centre midfielders or centre-halves can be captain.”

He added: “I look at that Man City side. I wouldn't say Haaland needs to be captain. He's a goal scorer.”

The former Aston Villa striker also said: “When it’s kicking off during the game and the referee needs to speak to you. Haaland's like: 'You sort that out guys, I want to score'.

“He never gets involved when it's pushing and shoving. He's just there concentrating on scoring.”



Stelling then chimed in: “Haaland is, rightly for a striker, totally self-centred, totally self-centred. All it's about is him scoring goals. Nothing else.

5 Elliot Anderson has been named as a contender for the Man City captaincy, despite not yet making a competitive appearance for his new team Credit: Getty

“He's not going to be there trying to drive the rest of the team on. Which I think [you'd get] from, maybe a combative midfield player or a big central defender, somebody who's got more of an overview.”

Anderson a surprise pick for captaincy

Moving on to who could succeed Silva as captain, Agbonlahor named Dias as the standout candidate, before surprisingly suggesting new £116million arrival Elliot Anderson could be considered.



He explained: “The manager will have his idea. I think Ruben Dias is the standout, isn't he?

"He's captain material when he plays the game - very aggressive. He's a leader. He's always cheering his teammates on.

“Elliot Anderson, maybe. He's a new signing. He's going to be in the team.”

“If Rodri stays, obviously it could be Rodri. But I see Elliot Anderson - you know, big money move, [he] looks like captain material to me.”

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho would rank among top three Premier League managers and would win title with this squad
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho would rank among top three Premier League managers and would win title with this squad

Jamie O'Hara believes Jose Mourinho would instantly be among the three best managers in the Premier League, should he return.

Mourinho is back dining at the top table after he returned to Real Madrid earlier this summer.

3 Mourinho is tasked with helping Real win their first league title since 2024 Credit: Getty

The man dubbed the 'Special One' was previously in charge of the Spanish giants for three years and coached the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Kaka and Mesut Ozil.

Although the trio have long since departed Real, Mourinho now has a new generation of Galacticos to work with, including Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior, who recently re-committed his future to the club.

Mourinho's return to Real also marks a curious stage in his managerial career.

The 63-year-old's last three roles were at Roma, Fenerbahce and Benfica, with only one trophy - the Conference League in 2021/22 - scooped up.

Despite his lack of silverware in recent years, O'Hara still holds Mourinho in extremely high regard.

Jamie O'Hara names the Premier League managers Jose Mourinho is better than

"He'd still be in the top three managers in the Premier League, for me," O'Hara said on talkSPORT Drive.

"Unai Emery, I think is a top manager, but he's at Villa.

"In terms of manager, you'd have to put Arteta in the conversation. Not overall, but in terms of what he's done with Arsenal and the Champions League final, winning the league.

"He's (Mourinho) a better manager than (Enzo) Maresca. He's a better manager than (Xabi) Alonso. He's a better manager than (Roberto) De Zerbi. He's a better manager than (Michael) Carrick."

O'Hara added Mourinho would 'relish' the chance to be a Premier League manager because of how influential set pieces have become.

3 During his stints as a Premier League boss, Mourinho won nine trophies Credit: Getty

The ex-Tottenham midfielder even went as far as claiming Manchester City would have 'more chance' of winning the title with Mourinho at the helm instead of Enzo Maresca.

"He knows how to win," O'Hara said.

"If you put City with Mourinho up against Arteta's Arsenal, that's fireworks. I would love to see them go up against each other.

"I think Maresca's not ready to win the league."

Why Manchester City could be Enzo Maresca's most difficult job yet

Maresca has the unenviable task of being Pep Guardiola's replacement following the Spaniard's decision to step away from his post.

Guardiola had held the role since July 2016 and led City to a staggering six Premier League titles in that span.

3 Maresca has won a trophy in his last two roles and will hope to continue the trend at City Credit: Getty

The squad and, in many ways, the entire club, had been moulded to Guardiola's demands.

But it's now Maresca's ship to steer in what is just his fourth senior managerial role, having previously led Parma, Leicester City and Chelsea.

The Maresca era at City gets underway on Sunday as the reigning FA Cup champions take on Premier League winners Arsenal for the Community Shield.

As for Mourinho, he'll look to get off to a winning start on August 22 when Real travel to Espanyol for their LaLiga season opener.

Sports.title: Arsenal told to make immediate Martin Zubimendi decision amid transfer interest from Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Selling Martin Zubimendi to a Premier League rival this summer will 'come back to bite' Arsenal.

That is the view of European football journalist Andy Brassell amid interest in the World Cup winner.



5 Arsenal have been urged not to sell Zubimendi to a Premier League rival this summer Credit: Getty

Chelsea are amongst the clubs to be linked with a move for Zubimendi just a year after he joined the Gunners.

The 27-year-old penned a deal through to the summer of 2030 following his £55million move from Real Sociedad.

In his debut season with Arsenal, Zubimendi scored six goals and provided three assists in 57 appearances across all competitions.



As well as lifting the Premier League title in May, he was part of the Spain squad which won the World Cup earlier this summer.

However, Mikel Arteta's midfield has since been bolstered ahead of the new season in a potential blow to Zubimendi's playing time.



The £75m arrival of Bruno Guimaraes sees him join Declan Rice, Mikel Merino, Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze as options in the centre of the park.

Meanwhile, Ethan Nwaneri and Fabio Vieira have both returned to north London following loan spells elsewhere.



Although Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to clubs, doubts still persist over whether Zubimendi will remain at the Emirates Stadium.

Zubimendi decision

Brassell has backed the midfielder for long-term Premier League success, but admits his current club must make a decision quickly.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, he explained: "I think he could still be a success in the Premier League.

5 Zubimendi joined the Gunners last summer but could see his opportunities reduced this season Credit: Getty



"I think with the amount of games that Arsenal are still hoping to play this coming season and the amount of games you'd expect Arsenal to play in this coming season, they shouldn't be ushering him out the door.

"They should be holding on to him because we've seen that he's a top-level player.

"He's a trusted Rodri replacement for the national team. He's done that well in successive finals in Euro 2024 and in World Cup 2026.

"So I think it would be very short-sighted, especially when you look at the physical condition that Declan Rice finished the World Cup in. I think it'd be really short-sighted for Arsenal to get rid of him now."



Rice battled injuries throughout England's run to the semi-finals of the World Cup.

As with Zubimendi, he has only recently returned to the club for pre-season following a prolonged post-tournament break.

5 Brassell believes Arsenal should keep hold of World Cup winner Zubimendi Credit: Getty

Who could Zubimendi join?

Chelsea are not the only potential destination for Zubimendi if he leaves Arsenal before the transfer window closes.



A return to Spain could also be on the cards, with Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid a possible alternative to the Blues.

Brassell believes selling to a fellow Premier League side is far riskier for Arsenal, although new Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso could persuade Zubimendi to move to Stamford Bridge.

The pair both began their careers with youth club Antiguoko before progressing through the Real Sociedad academy.

Discussing who Zubimendi could join, Brassell added: "With that said if they are going to get rid of him I feel that I wouldn't get rid of him to Chelsea because there would be huge potential for that to bite them on the backside.



"Real Madrid I think makes a lot of sense for the reasons that you've outlined [a return to Spain] or the fact that they've missed out on the aforementioned Rodri or they look like missing out on the aforementioned Rodri.

5 Mourinho's Real Madrid has been named as an ideal landing spot for Zubimendi Credit: AFP

"I think he would add a lot to [Jose] Mourinho's Real Madrid because I think if you look at Mourinho teams in the last few years over the last couple of cycles, you look at Benfica, you look at Fenerbahce, you look at Roma.

"If I could have changed anything about most of those teams, I think: ‘can we have a little bit more mobility in midfield, please?’ And that's what Zubimendi is really good at.



"He's not just a holder who stays. He's someone who's really good at bringing the ball out, really mobile.

"And you think if they're going to get to a point where they play Aurelien Tchouameni either as a third centre-back or just one of two centre-backs, which is a possibility or whether you're going to have him next to Zubimendi.

"Zubimendi works in either of those places, I think, and to have someone who would do that to allow Jude Bellingham the ability to really make those late runs into the penalty box. I think he'd be really good for them.

"Of course, the other connection is he’s a Real Sociedad guy just like Xabi Alonso.



5 Zubimendi's Real Sociedad connections could see him join Alonso at Chelsea Credit: Getty

"So Xabi Alonso is more than aware of him, but I just don't see Arsenal sanctioning that.

"Especially as they know he's a player who has had a tough time rather than a player who's not good enough, so Real Madrid makes the best sense for me, but I think Arsenal should hang onto him."

Sports.title: Newcastle ‘dodged a bullet’ as ‘incredibly average’ player turns down transfer
Sports.content:
Jeff Stelling believes Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg's decision to turn down Newcastle is a blessing in disguise for the club.

The Magpies had made an approach to Marseille for Hojbjerg as they sought to replace Bruno Guimaraes, who completed a switch to Arsenal on Saturday.

3 Hojbjerg moved to Marseille from Tottenham in July 2024 Credit: AFP

Despite Newcastle possessing the funds to meet Marseille's valuation of the midfielder, Hojbjerg chose to remain with the French club.

Yet Stelling believes the Magpies have 'dodged a bullet'.

What was Jeff Stelling's verdict on Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg?

"I know they wanted experience, he's 31 and he's done well at Marseille," Stelling said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"But his last season at Tottenham, he made eight Premier League starts and didn't play successive Premier League games at all.

"I think he's incredibly average."

Co-host Gabby Agbonlahor was equally critical of Hojbjerg and questioned if he would have been the 'fighter' Newcastle needed to help galvanise the squad following Guimaraes' exit.

What was Gabby Agbonlahor's verdict on Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg?

"A strange option," Agbonlahor said.

"When I watched him, you saw he had a bit of an ego, didn't he?

"Is he going to come to Newcastle and really be the player that you want, the character you want, the fighter that wants to be at the football club?

"I think it was a strange player to go for."

3 Hojbjerg has over 250 Premier League games under his belt Credit: Getty

With Hojbjerg off the table, Newcastle could turn to Bayern Munich midfielder Joao Palhinha to fill the void left by Guimaraes.

The 31-year-old, who spent last season on loan at Tottenham, has been put up for sale by the German giants just two years after he joined.

talkSPORT understands Palhinha is on Newcastle's radar, but they face stiff competition for his signature from Premier League rivals Aston Villa.

Which other players have Newcastle missed out on this summer?

It is understood the Villans are advancing in a deal for Palhinha, with their director of football Damian Vidagany previously confirming the clubs were in discussions over the transfer.

And if Villa were to sign the former Fulham ace, Agbonlahor felt those connected to Newcastle will be cursing their luck yet again.

The Magpies have already lost out to Villa once before this window as they swooped in to snap up Johan Manzambi for a club record deal.

3 Palhinha could be set for another season in the Premier League at a new club Credit: Getty

And earlier in the window, Newcastle were beaten to the punch by Liverpool for Spain international Victor Munoz.

"It's getting a bit frustrating, isn't it?" Agbonlahor said.

"If you're involved at Newcastle as a fan or working at the football club, missing out on all these players."

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho in transfer battle with ‘box office’ sensation as European giants weigh up decision
Sports.content:
Jadon Sancho has been told that there is a willingness for Borussia Dortmund to offer him a career lifeline with a third move to the club.

However, the 26-year-old has been warned that he may have to wait until the end of the window despite being available as a free agent.



6 Sancho's immediate future is unclear following mixed success on loan at Aston Villa last season Credit: Getty

Sancho has been on the search for a new permanent home after he was released by Manchester United at the end of his contract in June.

He has spent the last two-and-a-half seasons on loan at Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa - reaching the final of UEFA's three competitions in successive campaigns, and winning the Conference League and Europa League in each of the past two years.

The winger, who has kept himself fit using the facilities at 10th-tier Flixton FC, has been the subject of a surprise enquiry from Qatar.



Sancho has been linked with a third stint at Dortmund since the start of the year, but as of yet, no movement has taken place over a deal.

Sancho back to Dortmund latest

The future of the 23-cap England international was a talking point on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Trans Europe Express podcast.



Andy Brassell asked his fellow European football expert Kevin Hatchard: "What about Jadon Sancho [back to Dortmund]?

"Because he's still without a club. We know they've got lots of people at the club who still rate him, who still like him.



"To me, it feels that a deal might happen if we were to get to the back end of the window and he still hasn't got a club and they could do it more on their terms at a relatively small, risk-free level."

Bundesliga commentator Hatchard replied: "I think there's a willingness to do it at Dortmund. The story wouldn't hang around for as long as it has if there wasn't."

6 Sancho enjoyed a strong loan spell back at Dortmund in the second half of the 2023/24 season Credit: Getty

Realistic wages

"And even though there have been changes at the top in terms of Sebastian Kehl moving on, Nils-Ole Book has gone there as sporting director, I still think within the building there's a willingness to bring him back at some stage.



"Now, as you say, I think they would have to wait until a bit later in the window.

"I think Jadon would have to be realistic about the wages on offer, to be honest, because I think Dortmund don't have the wriggle room that some people might think they do.

"And I think he's somebody that can work in that [Niko] Kovac system because he could actually be one of those interior players that can spark things off. I mean, they've just lost Julian Brandt. Or, I say lost, they let him go, they let his contract lapse, they didn't extend it.

"But there's a really talented player who makes things happen around him, who can be a little bit inconsistent. Well, I'd put Sancho in that bracket.



6 The winger played in the 2024 Champions League final defeat against Real Madrid during his last stint at the club Credit: Getty

"I think he's somebody that could come in, could have an impact, and as long as he was willing to put the work in under Kovac, because there are certain prerequisites there in terms of the work…you have to do it.

"Otherwise you're not going to play. There's no point going there if you're not prepared to put that work in.

Hatchard continued: "He's won things at Chelsea, he's won things at Villa. Was he a central figure in either of those things? Not really.



"I still think there's incredible talent there and Manchester United fans will be apoplectic with rage about me saying that.

"But I still think he's a very talented footballer. But I think he needs the right environment. And I think he needs a lot of things to go his way.

"And I really hope we see that. And if that's at Dortmund, great."

6 Sancho made 39 appearances across all competitions for Villa last season, scoring just once Credit: Getty

Said El Mala transfer

Sancho's potential return to Dortmund may also hinge on the future of Said El Mala, who has been linked with a move to Westfalenstadion.



Brighton were thought to be the leading suitors to win the race for the 19-year-old, who has also attracted interest from Manchester United and Tottenham.

The Seagulls even had a unique plan to steal a march over their rivals by signing El Mala's brother Malek as well.

However, a transfer never materialised, and Brentford's proposed club record deal for the German Under-21 ace collapsed in June.

Hatchard added: "There is a feeling that Jürgen Klopp, the new Germany manager, is a big fan of his and is kind of leaning on Dortmund to try and make that move because he believes El Mala being successful at Dortmund would be a really good thing for Germany.



"I think he's mega raw. I think he's got a lot to recommend him. He moves like a racehorse; he's built like a boxer.

"The physical gifts are there. I just think he needs more consistency."

6 El Mala looked set to become Brentford's most expensive signing Credit: Getty

"He needs better coaching is what he needs," Brassell stated. "I think he would get that off Niko Kovac.



"For Kovac to get hold of him while he was a teenager, make him understand defensive responsibility, working in a structure.

"But the fact is, he is the superstar that Köln fans have wanted ever since Lukas Podolski, because of course they never had the chance for Florian Wirtz to be that because Wirtz was pinched by Leverkusen.

"I saw a lot of El Mala first hand last season. He's box office. He's so great to watch. He really is.

I guess maybe this will be the question for Dortmund come later in the summer. Do you go the extra mile and sign him?



6 Dortmund have been strongly linked with a move for one of the Bundesliga's most exciting talents Credit: Getty

"It will not be mad wages, but a big transfer fee. And that's why it hasn't got done already, right? Because they want 50 million euros.

"Köln are looking at it like we are not prolific producers of players and we've got to replace him and we can only sell him once basically, which I think is a fair point to take.

"But given how poorly he was coached last season, particularly by Lukas Kwasniok, who I don't think looked after him very well at all.



"And the way that he shunted him in and out of the team when he was the player most likely to [to inject the attacking impetus] at all times for Köln.

"I think he needs to get to a good place. He needs to get to a good place, I guess. But for me, that would have a knock-on effect with Sancho. I don't think you sign El Mala and sign Sancho as well.

Sancho vs El Mala

Hatchard agreed, telling talkSPORT: "No, I think you're right. I think it probably is one or the other, unless, as we say, it becomes a situation where Sancho, you know, the well's pretty dry.

"There aren't many options, and he comes in on a reduced deal."

Brassell said: "But I think that's where he is, isn't it? At the moment, he's back up, which with his talent is a is a sad thing to say.



"But I think Dortmund are letting it play out and seeing where they are probably at the back end of the month."

Sports.title: Awkward moment footballer is blanked by his girlfriend dubbed 'Uruguay's Kim Kardashian' after swooping in for a kiss at his transfer unveiling... before hilariously trying to style it out
Sports.content:
A footballer hoping for a smooch on one of the proudest days of his career was left with lonely lips after his girlfriend blanked and abandoned him on stage.

Uruguay striker Luciano Rodriguez was celebrating his loan move to Brazilian giants Cruzeiro alongside his girlfriend Anto Ciavaglia.

But just as he leaned in for a kiss in front of the cameras, Ciavaglia – who has been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian' – turned and left him stone cold.

Rodriguez's smile vanished and he was forced to awkwardly stand on his own for a few seconds before running his hand through his hair.

Footage of the awkward moment has gone viral on social media, and Ciavaglia has had to quell any talk of a rift between them.

The 23-year-old model, who has more than 170,000 Instagram followers, said: 'When I entered, I greeted him and when I left, I was very nervous.

Uruguay striker Luciano Rodriguez was blanked and abaondoned by his girlfriend as he went searching for a kiss upon joining Cruzeiro

The forward, 23, tired to style out the awkward moment by running his hand through his hair

His girlfriend, Anto Ciavaglia, who has been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian,' said she had simply been nervous and did not mean to disrespect him

'The moment overwhelmed me and I preferred to give him space.

'There was no disrespect or anything like what they are trying to make it seem like.'

One clip has been seen more than 4.6 million times.

In more footage from the unveiling, Rodriguez's mother was seen breaking down in tears as she sat next to Ciavaglia, no doubt proud of her son.

Rodriguez, 23, has plenty to celebrate in his career. The striker has been capped five times for his country but narrowly missed out on a place in Uruguay's World Cup squad.

He has also won the Under-20s World Cup and the Uruguayan Premier Division when he was at Liverpool Montevideo in 2023.

After two seasons in Brazil with Bahia, he switched to Neom in the Saudi Pro League last campaign but only scored six goals in 30 games. He has now linked up with Cruzeiro on loan with a reported £14.95million buy option.

At Cruzeiro, he links up with former Leeds forward Luis Sinisterra and ex-West Brom man Matheus Pereira.

His girlfriend, Anto Ciavaglia, was reported by Uruguayan newspaper El Pais to have been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian' in 2021.

Commenting on the comparison, she told the outlet: 'It's super cute because I love her. I'm a huge fan.'

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest complete £36m move for Ousmane Diomande, Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest complete £36m move for Ousmane Diomande, Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Palace teen on Portuguese radar

Portuguese top-flight club Alverca - who are owned by Vinicius Jr - are in talks to sign Mofe Jemide on a permanent deal from Crystal Palace.

The imposing centre-back, who signed his first professional contract at Palace in 2023, has represented England at U20 level and had significant loan and permanent interest across Europe.

The 19-year-old trained with Pierre Sage’s first team squad in pre-season and was given minutes during friendlies against Swindon, Bromley, Famalicao and Al Ula.

He has yet to make his competitive senior debut, though, turning out 44 times for Palace’s U21s.

EXCLUSIVE BY BOBBY MANZI

Another loan for Kalvin Phillips

Midfielder Kalvin Phillips has agreed to join Sheffield United from Manchester City on another loan, as Daily Mail Sport reported in June.

Midfielder Kalvin Phillips has agreed to join Sheffield United from Manchester City on another loan

Chris Wilder was keen to re-sign the 30-year-old, who has two years left on his contract, despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

World Cup star joins Forest

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon.

The 22-year-old centre-back has signed a four-year deal with an option for another year.

Diomande said: 'It is a historic club, and it motivates me to join such a club. I believe we can achieve very good things this season and I am looking forward to meeting the players and head coach.

'I will give my best and all I can to help the team. I cannot wait to meet the supporters at the City Ground and together we can have a good season.'

Forest still want to add a right-back, midfielder and striker.

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon

Patterson completes Wrexham medical

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move to Wrexham.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed yesterday, the 26-year-old has agreed terms on a four-year deal with the Championship club.

Patterson is finalising the paperwork on his contract.

Wrexham are also in talks to sign Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt in a £4.5m deal.

Hull get their Nobel prize

Hull City have finally agreed their protracted negotiations for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

The centre back is heading over for his medical after the clubs settled on a £21million fee plus 12.5per cent sell-on clause, while his former club Real Betis receive 20 percent as part of their sell-on.

The 21-year-old Senegal international can play at centre back and left-back.

Fulham snap up Southampton's Charles

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons.

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year contract, tying him to Craven Cottage until June 2031, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months.

Southampton also retain a 20percent sell-on.

Speaking to FFCtv, Charles, who will wear the number 19 shirt, said: 'It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege.

'I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.

'I’m buzzing to finally get it over the line. The club has got a really good foundation, from the bottom to the top really.'

Palace and Everton complete rare swap deal

Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil have completed their respective swaps to Everton and Crystal Palace and signed four year contracts.

Johnson, who only joined Palace from Tottenham in January for £35m, told evertontv: ‘I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

Brennan Johnson has completed a move to Everton from Crystal Palace in a rare swap deal

As part of the transfer, Dwight McNeil has moved the other way to link up with the Eagles after his transfer to the club on Deadline Day in the winter window collapsed at the last moment

'There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

He becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes’ squad after Merlin Rohl’s loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

Meanwhile, McNeil has signed his four-year contract with Palace and said: 'The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.'

Lukaku agrees Turkey move

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli.

The Belgium international has agreed a two year contract worth around £8.6m a season and has already passed his medical.

The deal includes further add ons based on performances.

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli

Chelsea are understood to have inserted a 40percent sell-on clause when they sold Lukaku for a knockdown £26m to Napoli two years ago.

He scored 14 goals in his first season but injury and the arrival of Rasmus Hojlund from Manchester United restricted him to just seven games last year.

Liverpool starlet wanted in Portugal

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move.

The 18-year-old who has joined the club from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal has stood out for the first team in pre-season friendlies.

But despite the promise he has shown, and Liverpool's dearth of defensive cover, post-Brexit rules mean Austria youth international Ndukwe doesn't have enough points to obtain a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) to obtain a work visa.

He will start against Como in their last friendly but is unable to play a competitive match for the Anfield club.

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move

Now clubs from Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have been calling to take the 6ft 6ins centre back on loan but there is a sense Portugal may be his preferred destination.

After playing alongside him, captain Virgil van Dijk said: 'Big talent, big guy and he wants to learn. I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him, it is just progressing. I know he has to go on loan I think so let's see where he ends up.'

Napoli still in the hunt for Badiashile

Napoli have offered a £2m loan fee for Chelsea's £30million-rated centre-back Benoit Badiashile with obligation to buy.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs and the player's representatives to try and find a full agreement.

Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah to Como and are also looking to sell Axel Disasi who has had interest from Crystal Palace and West Ham.

Napoli are continuing talks to sign Chelsea's £30m-rated centre-back Beniot Badiashile (right)

Mamadou Sarr, who suffered an injury at the weekend, is likely to go on loan to a Premier League side.

Keeper Filip Jorgensen has completed his move to Strasbourg on loan.

Wigan Athletic are closing in on their loan move for Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh while Portsmouth want 17-year-old Chelsea winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen on loan.

Napoli remain keen on Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus also as talks continue. Arsenal want £20m for the Brazilian.

Villa defender wanted in Belgium

Aston Villa right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic is a target for Rangers along with Hugo Siquet of Bruges.

Nedeljkovic has had interest from a number of clubs including Osasuna but Rangers are exploring a £4million deal with initial loan for the Serbia international.

The 20-year-old had a spell with RB Leipzig last season.

Burnley after new keeper

Burnley are showing interest in OH Leuven goalkeeper Tobe Leysen.

The 24-year-old former Belgium U21 international has one year left on contract so Leuven are willing to listen to offers.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...
