Sports.title: Like father, like son! Freddie Flintoff's 18-year-old son, Rocky, blazes stunning maiden hundred for Lancashire in just 65 balls
Sports.content:
Like father, like son! Freddie Flintoff's 18-year-old son, Rocky, blazes stunning maiden hundred for Lancashire in just 65 balls

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rocky Flintoff, son of England legend Freddie, enjoyed a day to remember as he struck his maiden hundred for Lancashire.

Playing against Somerset in the Metro Bank One Day Cup, Flintoff, 18, smashed a stunning 123 off just 76 balls as Lancashire racked up a mammoth 443-6 off their 50 overs.

The 18-year-old struck 10 fours and seven sixes as he shone in the blazing sunshine in Taunton.

Flintoff looked in imperious form and brought up his 100 in just 65 balls as he put on a 214-run fourth wicket partnership with former England opener Keaton Jennings, who hit 156.

The middle-order batter was eventually dismissed off the bowling of South African Migael Pretorius, with Archie Vaughan, son of Ashes 2005-winning captain Michael, a former team-mate of Flintoff Snr, taking the catch.

Flintoff made his First-Class and List A debuts as a 16-year-old during the 2024 season, but after missing much of the 2025 campaign through injury, he has been given an opportunity to shine over recent weeks.

Rocky on the attack! 🚀



Flintoff dispatches a four and a six in consecutive balls as he looks to keep upping our run rate!



🌹 #RedRoseTogether pic.twitter.com/dITNQwguZx — Lancashire Cricket (@lancscricket) August 11, 2026

Freddie Flintoff's son Rocky, 18, struck his maiden hundred for Lancashire on Tuesday

Flintoff brought up his century off just 65 balls and hit seven sixes in his incredible innings

With several of Lancashire's more senior batters away at The Hundred, Flintoff has featured in seven of their eight group matches in the One Day Cup and impressed.

After his knock on Tuesday, Flintoff had scored 293 runs across seven innings at an average of 73.25.

That makes him Lancashire's third top run scorer in the competition behind Jennings and their Australian overseas batter Marcus Harris.

Given his age, Flintoff continues to feature regularly for England's Under 19 side, while he also struck a century for the England Lions against a Cricket Australia XI in early 2025, highlighting his prestigious talent.

He is one of a number of famous sons of England's 2005 generation making their way in the cricketing world.

Vaughan, a top-order batter and off-spin bowler, is slightly older than Flintoff at 20, yet he is a regular in Somerset's One Day and First-Class team.

Charlie Harmison, son of former England fast-bowler Steve, is on the books at Durham and featured alongside Flintoff for England's Under 19 side earlier this summer.

Rocky's older brother Corey also enjoyed a short stint with Kent last summer.

Flintoff's feat came against Archie Vaughan, son of his dad's former England captain Michael

When making his debut in the One Day Cup in 2024, Flintoff became Lancashire's youngest ever player at 16 years and 113 days, and he signed a new two-year contract with the club earlier this year.

His father is one of England's most popular and iconic cricketers of all-time, featuring in 79 Tests - including the 2005 and 2009 Ashes series victories - 141 ODIs and seven T20Is.

He was in charge of the England Lions, the team Rocky had featured for, until he stepped down from the role last week.

Sports.title: Players go to WAR with the English Football League as trade union pursues legal action over new third-tier wage bill rules
Sports.content:
Players go to WAR with the English Football League as trade union pursues legal action over new third-tier wage bill rules

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The PFA have taken the extraordinary step of pursuing legal action in a bid to block changes to financial controls in League One.

In a move that has triggered outrage within the EFL, the trade union has filed a case with the High Court over a proposal to drop the amount a third tier club can spend on wages from 60 per cent of revenue to 50 per cent.

As Daily Mail Sport previously revealed, League One sides lost a staggering average of £7.3m last year, and the aim of the plans is to reduce an overwhelming reliance on ownership funding.

However, the PFA – clearly concerned over the impact that the changes would have on wages – has now taken the legal route and is claiming that due process has not been followed.

In a lengthy statement, the EFL said it was ‘concerned and disappointed’ at the move.

They say the changes had been discussed at length ahead of their planned introduction, with PFA feedback taken on board.

The players' union have taken the extraordinary step of pursuing legal action against the EFL

The PFA have begun High Court proceedings in relation to new wage restriction rules brought in by the EFL this season in League One. pic.twitter.com/Ulls1afkSX — PFA (@PFA) August 11, 2026

In 2021, the PFA successfully challenged the introduction of a salary cap however, the EFL believe the current proposal is not a major change and so should not be judged in the same manner.

A spokesperson added: ‘The PFA’s decision to oppose these reforms, and to pursue legal action, diverts limited resources and adds further cost to a game already under financial pressure. League One clubs have made it clear that change is needed.

'Costs are rising, losses are increasing and many clubs are relying more heavily on owner funding to meet their commitments. That model is not sustainable for clubs, players or the wider game. The approved changes are intended to support responsible financial management, encourage sensible squad planning and reduce the risk of clubs spending beyond their means.

'This is not about undermining players’ interests. It is about creating a stable environment in which clubs can meet their obligations and continue to invest in football.’

Trevor Birch, EFL chief executive, added: ‘Put simply, these reforms are designed to make clubs more sustainable. Stable clubs are better placed to honour contracts, pay wages on time, invest in facilities and create long-term opportunities for players. But a rising tide of losses and growing reliance on owner funding increase risk for everyone. That is why delaying reform is a risk. Clubs need rules that help them plan responsibly and avoid spending beyond their means.’

EFL chief executive Trevor Birch hit out at the decision, insisting that the new wage bill structure coming to League One is designed to help keep football clubs 'sustainable'

Average losses in League One have skyrocketed from £2.3m in 2021-22 to £7.3m last season. Many players in League One are now paid in excess of £10,000 per week.

A PFA spokesperson said: ‘The PFA have begun High Court action against the EFL in relation to new wage restriction rules adopted by clubs in League One and introduced this season.

‘We believe that the process through which clubs have voted to bring in these new measures, which will artificially restrict and tighten what clubs can spend on player wages, was not in line with the consultation and agreement process required by the EFL’s membership (alongside the PFA, FA and Premier League) of the Professional Football Negotiating and Consultative Committee (PFNCC).’

Sports.title: Paul Scholes urges Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for 'nutcase' Cristian Romero - despite calling him 'an absolute clown' who 'does stupid things'
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes urges Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for 'nutcase' Cristian Romero - despite calling him 'an absolute clown' who 'does stupid things'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has urged his former club to gazump Atletico Madrid's £34million move for Cristian Romero, despite branding the Tottenham captain a 'nutcase' and 'absolute clown' in his sales pitch.

The Argentina defender, 28, is expected to leave Spurs this summer after being given the green light to join LaLiga heavyweights Atletico Madrid, who are deep in talks with the north London outfit and only a few million apart in negotiations.

Meanwhile, the Red Devils are eagerly exploring options to bolster Michael Carrick's squad ahead of the new campaign, which will see United compete in the Champions League after finishing third in the Premier League last season.

Scholes, who has previously criticised Romero's rash and ill-disciplined approach to defending at Spurs, has surprisingly called for United to hijack Atletico's pursuit.

'This is one you might laugh at. Cristian Romero from Tottenham,' he said while discussing United's potential transfer targets on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast, powered by Midnite.

'I know it might sound stupid, but I just think... I like him. I think he's a nutcase. He's a very good defender that does some stupid things. He is an absolute clown.

Paul Scholes has urged Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for Cristian Romero

Scholes branded the defender a 'nutcase' but still thinks he would bring something to United

'But I think if someone could get hold of him, like Michael Carrick, who is very calm and relaxed, he might be able to [help him].

'He seems like a bit of a cult hero defender, really. I know it might sound strange, but I think the fans at Old Trafford would like him.

'There's a bit of something about him. He's won the Europa League with Spurs, he's won a World Cup, two Copa Americas. There's definitely something about him and he's cheap, £30-40million.'

Carrick has a string of defensive options at centre-half heading into the season, with Harry Maguire, Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt, Ayden Heaven and Romero's international team-mate Lisandro Martinez among those who operate at the heart of defence.

Scholes believes, despite the options available, that United need to bolster that department in particular if they plan to kick on in the future.

'I think centre-half is probably the biggest [area that needs addressing],' he added. 'You need to have centre-halves that are reliable for the Premier League. You’d like to have them [fit enough to play] in most games.

'Harry Maguire not so much, but Martinez picks up a lot of injuries. They’ve got the young lad Ayden Heaven, who I think is a really bright prospect, but he’s still going to make mistakes. He’s young.

'Centre-half is a position they need to address if they are going to be challenging towards the top end [of the league].'

Manchester United's first test in the Premier League is a trip to newly-promoted Hull City on Saturday, August 22.

Sports.title: Revealed: Shocking food and drink prices at European Championships in Birmingham - with a pork roll costing £18.50 - as Stan Collymore hits out at bosses for pricing fans out
Sports.content:
Revealed: Shocking food and drink prices at European Championships in Birmingham - with a pork roll costing £18.50 - as Stan Collymore hits out at bosses for pricing fans out

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The European Athletics Championships have come under fire with fans being 'gouged' with 'disgusting' ticket and refreshment prices in Birmingham.

Star names such as Keely Hodgkinson, Katarina Johnson-Thompson, Dina Asher-Smith and Amy Hunt are competing in the first Championships to be held on these shores.

But seats are being flogged for up to £150 while a barbecue pork roll costs a piggish £18.50 at the Alexander Stadium.

Ticket prices are decided by European Athletics in collaboration with the Local Organising Committee.

The fees have been met with half-empty stands, with one supporter branding it a 'disgrace'.

Even former England footballer Stan Collymore has come out of the woodwork to criticise the pricing, writing on X: 'No wonder crowds yesterday were poor. Woeful optics.

'£18+ for a pork roll, £150 for a Cat A ticket. Could have got a £20 ticket for this morning's session but how many can go on a Tuesday in the school holidays?

The European Athletics Championships have seen tickets priced up to £150 - and have struggled to get bums on seats

The likes of Keely Hodgkinson (pictured), Katarina Johnson-Thompson, Dina Asher-Smith and Amy Hunt are competing

'Weather is amazing and the sport needs as many eyeballs as possible so kids for a quid!!

'£150/£100/£70 for the three categories at the weekend is aimed at who? Not families and kids who may want to be athletes!'

It's not just fans being priced out - athletes' families and friends are struggling to meet the costs too.

Athletes are not being given any complementary tickets for the events, but UK Athletics are not offering any discounts on this occasion.

At the 2024 Paris Olympics, athletes were given at least one free ticket and that is the case at the majority of major championships.

One anonymous athlete told The Times: 'They could have even offered a discounted rate, so it is a little bit of a surprise, a bit of a shame. It’s a home championships, it would be good to have more family and friends there but it’s sort of the hands we’ve been dealt really.'

Another said: 'We thought it was maybe a mistake at first.'

The extortionate food and drink prices include £15 for a bratwurst dog, £12 for barbecue loaded fries, and £3.95 for a bottle of water.

An X user wrote: 'Sorry but this is disgusting and a sure-fire way to turn people off a sport that gets only a couple of opportunities to show itself off each year. European Athletics Championships organisers in Birmingham need to be called out for this price gouging.'

Another said: 'Such a shame to see so many empty seats. Have watched those temporary stands go up in recent weeks, and yet so few people attending.'

One said: 'I was there. Half-empty stands were a disgrace. They knew ticket sales were dire, so where was the dynamic pricing model to drop prices, supported by marketing? And where was the back-up of giving tickets to youngsters in athletics clubs and other sports clubs? Embarrassing.'

Another replied to Collymore's post, saying: 'That's a joke. Country is on its knees as it is, how are they getting away with charging those prices expecting to attract families etc.? Ridiculous!'

Organisers said: 'Birmingham 2026 is delighted with ticket sales for the championships, which have far surpassed our targets.

'Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening sessions are approaching sell-out, with several other sessions close to capacity.

'There are still opportunities to be part of the championships at incredibly good value, including the ‘Mondo’ £6.31 children’s ticket for Friday morning - named in honour of his world record - while a family of four can attend for as little as £30.'

The European Athletics Championships are taking place from August 10 to 16, with Great Britain putting out a team of 96 competitors.

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Chelsea and Man United with Arsenal looking to sell after £75m Bruno Guimaraes capture
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Chelsea and Man United with Arsenal looking to sell after £75m Bruno Guimaraes capture

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arsenal midfielder Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both Chelsea and Manchester United following the Gunners' capture of Bruno Guimaraes.

The 19-year-old signed a new deal last year following his breakout season, but after limited minutes in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign, there is belief the champions may be willing to move the Hale End product on.

There has been fresh contact with both the Blues and United, among other Premier League clubs, who are assessing whether to make a move for the versatile player.

Lewis-Skelly's minutes at Arsenal could be further limited in the upcoming season, with Guimaraes completing a £75million move from Newcastle last week.

Chelsea are understood to have long held an interest in Lewis-Skelly, but it is unclear whether they will put down an offer.

The academy product only managed 19 starts in all competitions last season, with Arteta giving him a rebirth in the middle of the park toward the end of the campaign, which led to a start in the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both Chelsea and Manchester United

Chelsea and United could both test Arsenal's resolve with a high enough offer for Lewis-Skelly

But with the Brazilian now expected to leapfrog Lewis-Skelly in the midfield pecking order, and opportunities already limited at left-back, there is a feeling that a move could be on the cards.

Guimaraes has signed a four-year deal with the option of a further 12 months. He adds serious talent and depth to Arsenal's midfield, which already contains names such as Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

A move to Chelsea would also see Lewis-Skelly face competition for minutes, with the Blues boasting a contingent of Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez – who has been linked with a move away – Romeo Lavia, Dario Essugo, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with new boss Xabi Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light.

The Blues have already made a series of statements in the transfer market, with Maxence Lacroix joining from Crystal Palace. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Teenager Lewis-Skelly has already made 75 senior appearances for Arsenal, securing a Premier League winner's medal last campaign.

He predominantly started his career at left-back, making a name for himself in Arsenal's Champions League quarter-final demolition of Real Madrid in 2025, but has since returned to his preferred position in central midfield.

The youngster has started every pre-season game for Arsenal, of which they have lost two, but is expected to be moved in place of Rice and Guimaraes once they return to action.

Sports.title: Defiant James McClean turns up for training at Derry City after poppy protestor's hometown club tried to rip up his contract
Sports.content:
James McClean rocked up for training at Derry City on Tuesday morning - despite the Northern Irish club reportedly trying to rip up his contract.

The 37-year-old rolled up in a black Range Rover despite a report in the Irish Independent claiming that Derry want to cancel his deal due to his supposed lack of 'physical capacity'.

Asked by reporters whether he was still a player with the club, McClean simply replied: 'Clearly.'

He was all smiles as he posed for photographs with young fans after the team's open training session.

McClean signed for his hometown club at the start of the 2026 season and has two years left on his deal, but has only started 12 of their 27 league games after leaving Wrexham.

The club reportedly claim that he is unable to fulfil his contract's terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

However the star - who has regularly made headlines for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations - is expected to insist that a contract cannot be cancelled unilaterally and that an independent physician must determine his fitness.

James McClean in Derry City training gear on Brandywell pitch meeting young fans at an open training session #jamesmcclean @UTVNews pic.twitter.com/Jd4jiqYrx1 — Gareth Wilkinson (@Gwilkinson_utv) August 11, 2026

WATCH. James McClean arrives at Brandywell Stadium for training amid reports Derry City has terminated his contract pic.twitter.com/db454kWy7U — Simon Collins (@SimonCollins82) August 11, 2026

James McClean has turned up for Derry City training despite them reportedly trying to rip up his contract

Derry sit sixth out of 10 teams in the League of Ireland Premier Division, a disappointing campaign after finishing runners-up in 2023 and 2025.

In June, McClean hinted at his unhappiness following his return home after a 15-year spell in English football.

'Family (are) enjoying being home – probably not so much myself, if I’m being honest,' McClean said during a punditry appearance on RTE.

'You know, you have a lot of conversations on the phone, and then you come home and you quickly realise that what you hear on the phone is not what you see in reality.

'There’s a lot of factors that’s contributed to that, but we’ll leave them for another day.'

McClean has previously spoken out about his reasons for not wearing the poppy, a decision he first made while playing for Sunderland in 2012. He maintained that stance throughout his career in England, despite being regularly targeted with abuse.

'The poppy which originally stood for World War 1 and 2 has now been adopted into honouring and remembering British soldiers that have served in all conflicts throughout the world including those who opened fire and murdered 14 innocent civilians on Bloody Sunday Jan 1972, in my home city, as well many other brutal crimes throughout Ireland,' McClean said in 2024.

'That is why I never have and never will wear a poppy. If the poppy’s sole purpose was to honour World War 1 and 2 then I would have no issue wearing it, but that’s not the case.

McClean has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations

'I respect those who do as I am fully aware we have different beliefs and upbringings, I would never force my beliefs on others, I’m not naive or stupid enough to expect the matter to be reciprocated, especially as the poppy is forced now on everyone in the UK and god forbid someone doesn’t wear it, the abuse they have to endure. The irony of all of this is that the poppy originally stood to honour those who fought for the right of freedom in both World Wars.

'Some people, no matter what, will not educate themselves or want to educate themselves, so to those who throw abuse about (matters they know nothing about), with insults like ‘hates our country’ – well I don’t. Some of my best relationships I’ve made through the years are with people born and raised in England and have completely different beliefs to me ... One thing I never have and never will do, is bend the knee to compromise my convictions.'

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland whom he represented in the Under 21s, said he had received 'death threats' for his stance over the poppy.

Last October, speaking during an episode of Virgin Media's Living with Lucy, he told presenter Lucy Kennedy how his family feared he would be shot while away on international duty after he first refused to wear a poppy on his shirt in 2012.

'I was getting death threats, people were saying I should be shot,' he said. 'I was getting bullets in the post, bullets sent to the club.

'That night, I met up with Ireland. The club had received threats that basically I was going to be shot. The game was on TV. I was going to be shot, this and that. (My wife, Erin) is back up in Newcastle, she’s panicking, she’s s*****g herself. They had to put security outside my hotel room door the whole night.

'Then, obviously, we’re playing the game, Erin’s watching the game, she’s panicking, she’s thinking, "He’s going to be shot on TV". Thankfully, nothing happened or nothing ever has happened.'

He added: 'I was getting death threats, people were saying he should be shot and dragged across the Cenotaph.

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland, said he has received 'death threats' for his poppy stance

'I could have easily just said, "I'll wear a poppy," and sold myself out and be known for my football or "I'll not wear a poppy" and be known as that but I've stayed true to myself.

'Six or seven people from the Creggan estate (where he grew up) died on Bloody Sunday that day so for me to wear a poppy in support of the people who carried out those atrocities...

'It frustrates me how people can’t see that. How is it even a debate of why I should wear the poppy?'

Sports.title: Amy Hunt hails 'coming of age' moment as she turns silver into gold at European Championships
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt hails 'coming of age' moment as she turns silver into gold at European Championships

Amy Hunt hailed a “coming of age” moment after storming to European 100m gold in Birmingham for the first major individual title of her career.

View 2 Images Novuna GB & NI Team athlete Amy Hunt celebrates her victory in the Women’s 100m at the European Athletics Championships Birmingham 2026.

Amy Hunt hailed a ‘coming of age’ triumph after scorching to European 100m gold in Birmingham.

‌



The 24-year-old landed her first major individual success by coming home in 11.00s, two-hundredths of a second clear of Ewa Swoboda, to upgrade the silver she won at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow 13 days ago.

‌



It is the start of what she hopes will be a historic week as she targets gold on four fronts, with the 200m - in which she won World Championship silver last year - and a pair of relays to come.

‌



“I thought it was time to upgrade and I think this was definitely a coming of age night for me,” she said. “Now I am kind of fully established. I have two 100m medals in the last two weeks and one more sub-11 to boot, so I’m very happy.

“I want to be the best. I don't shy away from that. I train incredibly hard, and I back myself so incredibly hard. I'm not saying that I'm the best right now, but that's something I aspire to be.”

View 2 Images Gold medalist, Amy Hunt of Team Great Britain (Image: 2026 British Athletics)

‌



Hunt set the tone in the semi-finals, clocking 10.99s to ease into the showpiece. Reigning champion Dina Asher-Smith also made it through but could only manage fifth in the final on this occasion in the latest sign of a shift in the balance of power within British sprinting.

“The stage of a final doesn’t intimidate me and I just knew I had to stay calm and not overthink myself into the goal,” Hunt said. “That was why the Commonwealths really came in handy for me. That’s why I really wanted to do it, to have that experience of being in front of a home crowd, having that medal expectation, because I've never had that before.”

Hunt credited the unlikely trio of Megan Thee Stallion, High School Musical and Mamma Mia as key to keeping her calm in the build-up, along with keeping her brain active on Wordle. As in the Commonwealth Games final in Glasgow, her start left her with catching up to do but she never had cause to press the panic button.

‌



“One of my biggest skills in terms of championships is I know I'm so strong in the end and I always have that kind of extra magic in the last 40," she said. “It can definitely rescue me in situations that I've got myself into but I kind of know the distance I can be away from the girls in order to be able to come back.

“I did leave it a little bit last minute this time but in championships, it's all about crossing the line first. When I look back at this race in ten years, I'm not going to think about how far back I was after 30 metres.”

Hunt returns to action on Wednesday in her ‘favourite event’, the 200m. Her plans before that are refreshingly simple.

Article continues below

“Try and get as much sleep as possible and a big fat lie-in.”

After this, she has earned it.

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson's BBC interview gatecrashed moments after run as Brit caught by surprise
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson's BBC interview gatecrashed moments after run as Brit caught by surprise

British athletics star Keely Hodgkinson was left stunned after her BBC interview was interrupted by a rival following her 800m heat at the European Athletics Championships

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson saw her BBC interview gatecrashed by Italy's Eloisa Coiro (Image: BBC)

Keely Hodgkinson was caught by surprise just moments into her BBC interview after reaching the semi-finals of the women's 800m at the European Athletics Championships. The Brit won her heat on Tuesday morning and clocked a time of 1.57 with Italy's Eloisa Coiro, who finished second, quick to congratulate her.

‌



While the duo embraced on the track, Coiro also ensured she got her point across in front of the cameras as she interrupted Hodgkinson's interview just as she was about to give her first answer to Sarah Mulkerrins.

‌



She said: "She is such an inspiration. Such a cool girl. Such an inspiration, on and off the track, really." Coiro then turned to Hodgkinson and added: "You're the champion for me," with the Atherton-born runner giggling at her rival's remarks.

‌



Keely Hodgkinson has point to prove as she faces Birmingham showdown with new rival READ MORE :

How to watch European Athletics Championships for free - TV channels and full schedule READ MORE :

"Aw, bless her," Hodgkinson replied. "We grew up competing against each other, so it's nice. She just got a PB as well there."

The 24-year-old then returned back to her interview and spoke about feeling "comfortable" on the track after taking the first step towards another European crown.

She did, however, confess to being surprised by the level of competition in the opening heat and revealed why her rivals are always improving

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Relieved isn't the word I would use at all," she said. "I've worked so hard and the shape has been there all year, it's just been an unfortunate couple of ends that have led to me being a little bit off.

"But, who cares? The championship is a fresh start, that felt very good, very comfortable. It was a little windy. The standard has gone up - 1.57, in the heats!

‌



"They were pushing me on the shoulder and I was like 'Guys? !'. But it's good, it brings out the best in me and I was just excited to get through this round."

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson won her 800m heat at the European Athletics Championships

Hodgkinson will return to the track on Thursday afternoon when the semi-finals get under way, and as the standout name in women's 800m racing in recent years, she will be hoping to secure her place in Friday night's final.

Article continues below

However, her bid for a third successive European title faces a stern test, with Switzerland's Audrey Werro widely regarded as her most formidable challenger for top honours.

Two-time 400m hurdles world champion Femke Broeders-Bol adds yet another threat to the mix, having made the switch to 800m this season.

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow

Manchester United are ready to move for Club Brugge left-back Joaquin Seys after seeing their advances for two other targets, including Lewis Hall, knocked back

View 2 Images Joaquin Seys has impressed for Club Brugge with Man Utd now keen

Manchester United are ready to open talks with Club Brugge about a £30million deal for left-back Joaquin Seys after being knocked back by two of their targets.

‌



The Red Devils have added two new faces in midfield but left-back is another area where they are looking to bring in reinforcements. It has proved challenging throughout the summer however with the club onto their third different target.

‌



The Belgian side are in no hurry to sell and have Seys under contract for another three years. They will not ease off their £30m price tag, but it Mirror Football understands United are strongly considering an opening bid.

‌



The 21-year-old is a regular for Club Brugge and forced his way into Belgium‘s World Cup squad, featuring in his country’s quarter-final defeat to winners Spain last month.

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

United did have Newcastle's Lewis Hall on their radar after the ex-Chelsea man had enjoyed the best season of his career to date, but the Magpies are refusing to sell up.

Already this summer Newcastle have lost marquee players in Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes. Hall is one of the leading lights and St James' Park bosses have refused to entertain his departure. United had ultimately been priced out whilst another target, young Spaniard Jorge Salinas, is poised to remain in La Liga.

‌



He reportedly remains fully committed to Racing Santander and "doesn’t want to leave" despite interest from Manchester and Barcelona. His manager Jose Alberto has grown tired with the incessant speculation regarding Salinas’ future during the summer window.

View 2 Images Lewis Hall had been a target for Man Utd (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

The left-back could be available for just €16m (£13.7m) due to a release clause in his contract at Racing, but his boss maintained that he and another of his in-demand team-mates want to remain. "They don’t want him to leave. And they show every day that they don’t either," he said.

‌



"But we know how this world works and there are release clauses. If a team comes along and pays the clause, they cease to be our players."

United currently have Luke Shaw as their first choice left-back, but he has struggled to remain fit throughout his career and, now into his 30s, the club are looking to future proof the position.

Sports.title: Golfer hits staggering 411-yard hole-in-one and is so shocked he can't find the ball
Sports.content:
Golfer hits staggering 411-yard hole-in-one and is so shocked he can't find the ball

An incredible new national record could have been set by an amateur golfer who hit an incredible 411-yard shot, which has estimated odds of six million-to-one

View 4 Images Matt Vigurs hit an incredible 411 yards hole-in-one (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

A golfer has incredibly set what is thought to be Britain's longest hole-in-one shot, at an incredible 411 yards (376 metres).

‌



Matt Vigurs, from Droitwich in Worcestershire, narrowly missed out on setting a new Guinness World Record when he aced the third hole during a recent match, but he could be in store for a national record. The 32-year-old made the incredible shot during a recent league match at Great Barr Golf Club in Sandwell, near Birmingham.

‌



The golfer hit his driver off the tee but could not find his shot when he reached the green. After a few minutes searching, Matt decided to have a quick look in the hole and saw his ball.

‌



Golf star punished after fish eats his ball during round leaving pundits gobsmacked READ MORE :

View 4 Images The shot was hit at Great Barr Golf Club (Image: Google Maps / SWNS)

Matt said: "It was really surreal. I just froze to start with. The lads ran over and we all belly slammed and high fived. It was a moment I will never forget for sure. It was brilliant. I think we were all shocked. Typically, the ball wouldn't go that far. It is just unheard of to get a hole-in-one really let alone on a par-four."

The golfer revealed that his average drive is around 300 yards but the wind and hard ground helped him stretch out to 411 yards. The incredible shot however was just 36 yards (33 metres) short of all-time record of a 447 yards (408 metres) hole-in-one, set by Robert Mitera in Nebraska, USA.

‌



View 4 Images Matt hit the hole-in-one on his third (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

Despite this, England Golf - the national governing body for amateur golf - believe Matt could have achieved a national record, but this has not yet been confirmed. It is thought the golfer beat the previous national effort by three yards. Peter Vickerman aced the 408-yard par-four seventh hole at Littlestone Golf Club in Kent, in 2014.

Matt's hole-in-one - also known as an albatross - came in a scratch match at the Walsall golf club, playing with a friend against two others. The four-ball found three balls when they got to the green of the hole, named Twin Oaks - but Matt's was missing.

‌



They searched the bushes, around the fairway and over the back of the green but it was nowhere to be seen. On a whim, Matt, who plays off a handicap of +1, decided to check the hole and says his friends gave him strange looks for even checking.

View 4 Images Matt Vigurs after winning the Worcestershire County Championship (Image: Matt Vigurs / SWNS)

Matt said: "At that point I looked a bit silly, so I thought I might as well check the hole - and there it was, nestled in the bottom. I had to take two or three looks. I couldn't believe it. They didn't believe me till I pulled it out of the hole and we just went mad! It was so weird - I couldn't concentrate for the next hole!"

‌



Matt, who only returned to regular golf in February after eight years abroad, went on to win his match. Droitwich Golf Club as a result sealed promotion by winning the league on the same day.

The odds of getting an albatross - a score of three-under-par - are estimated to be odds of six million-to-one, according to England Golf. However, the odds of a hole-in-one from this distance even likely even slimmer.

Matt, who works as a product and training manager at McLaren, added: "We think it might be the longest which is quite cool actually. I think it might even be the longest in Europe. I have absolutely no chance of ever doing it again. It truly was a once in six-million shot."

Article continues below

The golfer, who started playing the sport aged 11, said he kept the ball and hopes his golf club might help him commemorate the achievement.

James Crampton, championships director at England Golf, said: "We hear of holes-in-one all the time, but a 411-yard one - it's the stuff of golfers' dreams! It sounds like Matt is in the purple patch of his golfing life - and you have to enjoy these moments."

Sports.title: Man Utd 'ready to trigger release clause' and forced to act quick after £20m agreement
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'ready to trigger release clause' and forced to act quick after £20m agreement

Manchester United continue to be linked with a host of names, even though they have added six new faces to Michael Carrick's squad this summer

View 2 Images Michael Carrick could be getting a new left back before the season gets underway (Image: (Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United are ready to trigger Jorge Salinas’ release clause - but face competition from Atletico Madrid for his signature. Salinas came through the ranks at Real Racing Club de Santander and went on to make his first-team debut back in 2024.

‌



The left-back has since impressed in Spain, and, as a result, has been linked with a move away. As well as Atletico and United, Salinas has also been linked with a move to Barcelona.

‌



However, according to Spanish publication Sport, Barca have no intention of paying Salinas’ €16m (£13.6m) release clause. United, though, are ready to trigger it to snap up the 19-year-old this summer.

‌



But in a twist, the report also claims that Atletico are waiting for Matteo Ruggeri to complete a move to Aston Villa before making a move for Salinas. It is claimed that Villa have agreed a €18m plus €6m bonuses (£20m) deal with Los Rojiblancos for Ruggeri, meaning United may have to act quickly.

Despite the continued speculation around Salinas’ future, Racing boss Jose Alberto Lopez claimed earlier this week that the defender, along with Gustavo Puerta, don’t want to leave the club this summer. He said: "Their professionalism doesn't surprise me.

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UNITED FB PAGE! Latest news and analysis via the MEN’s Manchester United Facebook page

‌



“What surprises me is that people are constantly talking about the departure of two of our players [Salinas and Puerta], when they have contracts and are our players."

Before he added: "They're very important to us. I don't want them to leave. And they show every day that they don't either.

“But we know how this world works and there are release clauses. If a team comes along and pays the clause, they cease to be our players."

‌



View 2 Images Jorge Salinas is a key target with United said to be ready to meet his release clause

Speaking last week, Racing sporting director Chema Aragon made similar comments, but he did admit that his club would be powerless if a 'giant' such as United and Barca came in with a significant bid for Salinas.

"There's little you can do if a giant appears," Aragan said. "We value the assets we have, we consider them important.

‌



“For the club, at this time, there is no other option than to try to strengthen the team and not weaken it by losing stars. The reality is that the club that wants him has to come along with an offer."

United are in the market for a left back and are considering alternatives for Lewis Hall, who Newcastle do not want to sell. Salinas has already represented Spain's under-19 side nine times and registered seven assists from 34 matches last season as Racing were promoted back to La Liga.

Sports.title: Golf news: Scottie Scheffler banks £7.4m bonus as star hits back after being disqualified
Sports.content:
Golf news: Scottie Scheffler banks £7.4m bonus as star hits back after being disqualified

Golf round-up as Scottie Scheffler secures a massive bonus ahead of the FedEx Cup Playoffs

View 3 Images Scottie Scheffler is the man to beat heading into the FedEx Cup playoffs (Image: Getty Images)

With the 2026 majors in the rearview mirror, attention in the golf world has switched to the FedEx Cup Playoffs. The majors were shared, with Rory McIlroy defending his Masters title in typically dramatic fashion.

‌



Englishman Aaron Rai then secured a breakthrough triumph at the US PGA Championship before Wyndham Clark landed his second US Open crown.

‌



The final major of the year produced a surprise winner in the shape of New Zealander Ryan Fox, whose final-hole birdie saw him hold off Cameron Young at Royal Birkdale.

‌



Next up on the PGA Tour schedule is the first FedEx Cup Playoff event, the St Jude Championship, which begins on Thursday. That is followed by the BMW Championship and the big one, the Tour Championship, which was memorably won by Tommy Fleetwood last year. Here's a round-up of the latest golf news…

Golf star punished after fish eats his ball during round leaving pundits gobsmacked READ MORE :

Scottie Scheffler defended after microphones picked up row with his caddie READ MORE :

Scheffler banks £7.4m

He may have missed out on a major title this year, but Scottie Scheffler goes into the FedEx Cup play-offs as the man to beat.

For the fourth season out of five, the world number one has topped the regular-season standings, earning him a handy £7.4m bonus. While money is 'unofficial' and doesn't count towards his season's earnings, it will soon reside in his bank account.

‌



That is half of the bonus prize pool, worth almost £15m, which is shared among the top 10 at the end of the regular season. Scheffler was joined in the top 10 by Matt Fitzpatrick, Young, Clark, Chris Gotterup, Collin Morikawa, Si Woo Kim, Sam Burns, Fleetwood and Ludvig Aberg.

View 3 Images Scheffler has again topped the regular-season standings (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

Star hits back

Michael Block has insisted he didn't deserve to be disqualified from the PGA Seniors Championship.

‌



The 50-year-old, who stole the show with a shock top-15 finish at the 2023 US PGA Championship, walked off the course 12 holes into his final round at Trump International Golf Links in Scotland.

Block had already been docked two shots for turning up late to his tee time. He admitted that particular sanction was fair, telling Golf Digest: "First time in my career [that's happened] and it's completely my fault."

View 3 Images Michael Block wasn't happy about being disqualified (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But he wasn't happy to have the word 'disqualified' next to his name after claiming he tried to withdraw correctly, having been given a lift to the tournament office by someone he thought was an official. He also denied he was unhappy with course conditions.

He said: "I walked into the championship office to thank them for the week, but no one was there. I thought nothing of it, thinking that I had withdrawn correctly.

"But I guess the gentleman who gave me the ride [to the office] was not an official, so I was disqualified. To hear these accusations that I just walked off the course and that I was upset about the course conditions is absurd."

Sports.title: What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season
Sports.content:
What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season

Marcus Rashford is planning on holding talks with United boss Michael Carrick following the Red Devils friendly with Leeds United in Dublin on Wednesday night

View Image Marcus Rashford of Manchester United in action during a first team training session at Carton Hotel on August 10, 2026 in Dublin, Ireland. (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

Marcus Rashford is still keen to find an escape route from Manchester United. But Rashford might have to go abroad again - because his hopes of remaining in the Premier League look slim.

‌



Rashford has returned to pre-season training at Carrington following his summer break after the World Cup. He is planning to hold talks with manager Michael Carrick once the squad returns from its commitments in Dublin. But Rashford’s immediate future remains unclear and complicated.

‌



Co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe remains keen to get Rashford off the club’s wage bill. But he is not willing to sell the England forward to main rivals Arsenal, Liverpool or Manchester City.

‌



While loan deals with the likes of Chelsea, Aston Villa and Tottenham have been ruled out. Because if Rashford was to help any of these clubs finish in the Champions League places this coming season, it would prove embarrassing to United bosses.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

It’s understood Rashford would prefer to find a new club - and continue to revive his career elsewhere. He has the option of running down the remaining 24 months of his United deal, and leaving Old Trafford for nothing in 2028.

He could also use the next campaign to put himself in the shop window in the hope of securing a dream move in 2027 - assuming someone will pay.

‌



He believes there has been too much bad blood between him and his hometown club. And he knows there is still time in the summer window for him to negotiate a deal with someone else which suits him.

Rashford, 28, had been hoping to make his loan deal with Barcelona permanent, but the Spanish giants rejected the option to sign him for £24m, opting to sign Anthony Gordon instead.

United, meanwhile are considering opening talks with Club Brugge about a potential £30m deal for left back Joaquin Seys.

United have been priced out of a move for England and Newcastle defender Lewis Hall, and could turn their attentions to Seys instead.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
