World.title: Tonse-Pamodzi accuses security agencies of seizing campaign funds, denies kidnapping reports
World.content:
Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance spokesperson George Chisanga has denied reports that he and two senior colleagues were kidnapped on Monday, saying instead that a joint team from the Drug Enforcement Commission, police and the Anti-Corruption Commission raided his Lusaka law chambers and seized more than seven million dollars intended for polling agents and campaign logistics.

Addressing journalists alongside NRPUP presidential candidate Brian Mundubile, Chisanga said he wanted to correct what he described as a well-meaning but inaccurate rumour that he, Japhen Mwakalombe and senior alliance member Sebastian Kopulande had been abducted. He said Kopulande remained in custody at the time of the briefing.

Chisanga said officers arrived at his chambers, which the alliance sometimes uses for campaign business, and held him and his colleagues incommunicado for roughly twelve hours. He said officials told him the operation targeted funds being prepared for distribution to polling agents and election monitors ahead of Thursday’s vote.

“We explained exactly what we were doing and what we intended to achieve with the exercise that we put in place. We even gave them documents that showed clearly how the money has been earmarked and what it’s supposed to be utilised for,” Chisanga said.

He said the funds, contributed by well-wishers, had been earmarked mainly to resource polling agents and monitors countrywide, with a smaller portion set aside for final campaign rallies in Mazabuka, Livingstone and Choma. He said officers proceeded to seize the money despite receiving that explanation.

“That money, like I said, most of it was intended to be utilised for logistics, for people who are going to monitor elections, polling agents who have already been appointed and accredited,” he said.

Chisanga said staff at his chambers who had no connection to the alliance’s campaign work were also searched, and described the operation as an attempt to weaken the alliance’s ability to organise in the campaign’s final days rather than a genuine law-enforcement exercise.

“The intention clearly is to paralyse the Tonse alliance in the work that they’re doing,” he said, adding that those involved had since been asked to report to the Commission’s offices later the same day.

He appealed to authorities to return the funds without delay, arguing that the money carried no element of criminality and was needed to ensure polling agents could reach stations, some of them in remote rural areas, on polling day.

Chisanga said the alliance remained determined to contest the election despite the setback, and thanked supporters who had continued sending messages of solidarity after news of the raid spread. He said the alliance was still weighing whether a scaled-back visit to Southern Province remained possible before Thursday.

World.title: Zesco Utd confirm Mwenya Chipepo appointment
World.content:
Super Division side Zesco United have officially confirmed the appointment of Mwenya Chipepo as the club’s new Head Coach.

In a statement issued Tuesday afternoon, Zesco did not disclose the duration of Chipepo’s contract.

Chipepo recently seperated with Nkana just months after being sent on forced leave.

The former Nkana and Power Dynamos coach will be assisted by Tenant Chembo, who returns to the club as First Assistant Coach.

“ZESCO United Football Club officially announces the appointment of Mwenya Chipepo as the Club’s new Head Coach. Coach Chipepo will be supported by Tenant Chembo, who joins the technical bench as First Assistant Coach.”

Chipepo had already joined the team in training over a week ago and led the side in a friendly match against Kabwe Warriors on Monday.

The club has also made changes to the rest of the technical bench. Interim coach Winston Kalengo has been dropped to the role of Physical Trainer, while Mwape Mwelwa has been appointed Second Assistant Coach.

“Mwenya Chipepo brings a wealth of experience and a proven winning record to the ZESCO United FC technical bench. A CAF Licence holder, Chipepo has coached several top-flight Zambian football clubs.

Chipepo launched his coaching career at Young Power before stints as head coach at Prison Leopards, Indeni and Forest Rangers.

On Chembo, Zesco said: “Tenant Chembo returns to ZESCO United FC bringing extensive experience both as a player and coach. Chembo has built a distinguished coaching career with ZESCO United, Mufulira Wanderers, Lumwana Radiants, Forest Rangers, Indeni and Ndola United.”

Zesco United are seeking improved performance after struggling in the 2025/2026 campaign.

FULL TECHNICAL AND SUPPORT TEAM

• Mwenya Chipepo – Head Coach

• Tenant Chembo – First Assistant Coach

• Mwape Mwelwa – Second Assistant Coach

• Winston Kalengo – Physical Trainer

• Kondwani Mtonga – Physical Trainer

• Jacob Banda – Goalkeeper Trainer

• Simon Silwimba – Equipment Manager

• Kabamba Kalande – Team Manager

• Abidan Chansa – Team Doctor

• Stephen Mbewe – Team Clinician

World.title: ECZ Intensifies Poll Preparations in Sioma
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia has intensified preparations for the forthcoming general elections slated for 13th August, 2026, with the verification of ballot papers successfully conducted in Sioma District.

District Electoral Officer, Nsama Chiti, described the exercise as successful and thanked all stakeholders for the professionalism exhibited during the process.

Ms Chiti said the Commission will commence the deployment of poll staff to four wards of the district, with the exercise expected to continue up to Wednesday, 12th August, 2026.

She further pledged the Commission’s continued transparency to ensure the delivery of free, fair, and credible elections.

Meanwhile, representatives of political parties and independent candidates expressed satisfaction with the verification process.

Liswaniso Mutomena, representing an independent candidate, said he was happy with the transparency shown throughout the exercise and urged the Commission to maintain the same standard as it distributes ballot papers to all polling stations.

And United Party for National Development (UPND) Representative, Ilukena Mwindwa, called on all electorates to turn out in large numbers and vote peacefully on 13th August.

World.title: Former Kafulafuta MP endorses President Hichilema
World.content:
Former Kafulafuta Member of parliament Brian Chitafu has endorsed President Hakainde Hichilema for the upcoming August 13 presidential election and UPND candidate Elen Grigoraki for Kafulafuta Member of Parliament.

Mr Chitafu says his decision follows what he describes as careful reflection on the leadership provided by President Hichilema and the UPND government.

In a statement made available to the media in Ndola, the former lawmaker said President Hichilema has demonstrated economic leadership and has positioned the country on what he calls a path of economic recovery and development.

Mr Chitafu has also endorsed Elen Grigoraki for the Kafulafuta Parliamentary seat saying she has leadership qualities needed in the area.

“She brings the leadership qualities needed to move the constituency forward,” Mr Chitafu said.

He added that Ms Grigoraki has the vision and ability to address issues affecting residents, including jobs, improved economic opportunities and development.

The former MP has since called on voters to participate peacefully in the electoral process, because every citizen has the democratic right to choose their preferred candidate.

Mr Chitafu further appealed to the public for unity and responsible political participation, urging citizens to avoid what he describes as petty political discourse.

And he noted that his endorsement was aimed at supporting continued development in Kafulafuta, the Copperbelt and Zambia as a whole, and has called on kafulafuta residents to unite for a stronger and more developed constituency and country.

World.title: Katele turns on HH, accuses President of failing to protect political opponents
World.content:
Former Finance Minister Dr Katele Kalumba has launched a blistering attack on President Hakainde Hichilema, accusing him of failing in his constitutional responsibility to protect Zambians holding opposing political views and alleging that the political environment ahead of Thursday’s general election has deteriorated dangerously.

In a direct address to President Hichilema, Dr Kalumba said he was speaking only days before the August 13 election because he had become deeply concerned about what he described as abductions, deaths and attacks involving people expressing political opinions different from those of the government.

“Mr President, my name is Katele Kalumba. I’m speaking to you directly from the election day,” he said, before referring to his past relationship with the President. “I’m thankful for everything you did to me, and I’m sure you should be thankful for everything I did to you.”

Dr Kalumba said he would not publicly explain everything that had previously transpired between the two men, saying President Hichilema already knew what he was referring to. He instead turned his attention to the current political environment, placing responsibility for the protection of citizens directly on the President.

“What is happening now is not in the interest of our country, and I believe that you are at the helm of it. You are responsible as the President of the Republic of Zambia. You are responsible to protect the lives of every Zambian under the Constitution of the Republic of Zambia,” he said.

He questioned what the presidency meant if the Head of State could not guarantee the safety of citizens expressing political opinions different from his own or seeking to provide alternative leadership.

“I don’t know what your job is if you cannot protect the lives of Zambians who are expressing a different opinion from you, and to provide leadership different from you,” Dr Kalumba said.

The former minister then delivered one of his strongest personal attacks against President Hichilema, saying his previous perception of the President had changed considerably.

“I’m disappointed, because I thought you were a good man,” he said. “What I have found out now is a man who was pretentious, a man who pretended to be a good man.”

Dr Kalumba went further, using extremely strong language to characterise the President and alleging that the country had witnessed “abductions, death, strangulation” and other acts in the political environment surrounding the election.

He did not, in the recorded statement, provide specific cases or evidence directly linking President Hichilema to the alleged incidents. His allegations therefore remain claims made by the former minister and are not established facts.

Dr Kalumba also compared President Hichilema’s leadership with that of late former President Edgar Lungu, arguing that his experience of both men had left him with a harsher assessment of the incumbent.

“You are worse than Edgar Lungu,” he said.

He said he had at different times been close to both political leaders and claimed he understood former President Lungu from both a family and political perspective.

“I was close to Edgar Lungu at some point, as I was close to you. In fact, closer to him. I understand him better, from the family level to the political level,” Dr Kalumba said.

The veteran politician then revisited his involvement with President Hichilema during the 2015 presidential election campaign, saying he had worked as a campaign strategist for him and had believed at the time that he was making sacrifices in support of a man he considered a gentleman and a civilised political leader.

“But as a campaign strategist for you in 2015, which goes to be my business, my family’s business, I expected you to… I thought I was sacrificing for you, a gentleman, a civilised human being,” he said.

Dr Kalumba then made an extraordinary personal accusation against President Hichilema, claiming that allegations he had previously been accused of making about the President were now words he was prepared to state directly.

“Now I’m going to say it to your face,” he said, before accusing President Hichilema of believing in “nothing else than satanism.”

No evidence supporting that allegation was presented in the recording, and the claim represents Dr Kalumba’s own accusation against the President.

The former minister also claimed he had previously defended President Hichilema when there were attempts to arrest him in connection with what he referred to as “San International Hotel.”

“I was trying to defend you. I defended you when he said he wanted to arrest you over San International Hotel. I knew much, and I still do, but I defended you,” Dr Kalumba said.

He claimed that his intervention had helped President Hichilema avoid what he described as a “trap”, although he did not provide further details about the circumstances or identify precisely who he said was behind the alleged attempt.

“I made sure you got out of the trap and nobody exactly knew what I was saying,” he said.

Towards the end of the recording, Dr Kalumba also referred cryptically to Cape Town, saying: “I knew what had happened in Cape Town. I knew…”

The recording ends at that point without Dr Kalumba explaining what event he was referring to or providing further details.

The intervention represents a sharp change in tone from Dr Kalumba’s public assessment of President Hichilema earlier in the election campaign. In May, the former minister said President Hichilema remained politically ahead going into the August 13 general election, although he believed the contest was becoming increasingly competitive.

His latest remarks, however, move beyond an assessment of the electoral contest and amount to a direct personal and political attack on the President just days before Zambians vote.

The allegations concerning violence, abductions and other criminal acts contained in Dr Kalumba’s statement have not been independently substantiated in the recording, while President Hichilema and the UPND were not heard responding to the specific accusations made by the former minister.

With Zambia heading to the polls on Thursday, Dr Kalumba’s intervention adds another forceful voice to the increasingly charged final stages of the campaign, while leaving several of his most serious claims unexplained and unsupported by specific evidence in the statement itself.

World.title: Nakonde election preps advance
World.content:
Electoral stakeholders in Nakonde district in Muchinga Province have commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) for promoting transparency and ensuring peace during the preparations for Thursday’s general elections.

Nakonde Forum for Persons with Disabilities Chairperson, Martin Gondwe, thanked ECZ for exhibiting transparency and hoped this would be maintained throughout the electoral process.

Speaking in an interview with the Zambia News and Information Services (ZANIS), Mr Gondwe called on all political parties to preach peace in communities ahead of the polls.

Mr Gondwe further appealed for inclusion of persons with disabilities in the voting process and asked if braille tactile jackets will also be available during the verification exercise.

“Make sure you preach peace wherever you are going, in our camps. Persons with disabilities and women inclusive, we want to participate in a violence-free election this year,” he said.

And United Party for National Development (UPND) Chairperson for Nakonde District, Derick Banda, said the process had been peaceful.

He expressed optimism that the same peaceful mood will prevail as poll staff are deployed and dispatched to polling stations tomorrow.

He also expressed gratitude to other stakeholders who have been available from inception, to ensure transparency.

“So far so good, the process has been peaceful for us. The most important thing we always preach is peace. Even from the time we received the ballot papers it has been peaceful,” he said.

And National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) Mwenzo Constituency Chairperson, Frederick Siame, called for continued transparency during the dispatch of poll staff and verification of election material.

Mr Siame also expressed satisfaction with how the election preparations have been conducted in the district.

“So far so good. As we do the verification exercise when dispatching poll staff, we need to verify what the contents are. What we are asking for is the same transparency that has prevailed to continue,” Mr Siame said.

World.title: Liberia: Boakai Names Retired Army General to Head Anti-Drug Agency
World.content:
The Executive Mansion says Ziankahn's appointment reflects the President's confidence in his "leadership, integrity, and operational experience."

President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has made perhaps his most consequential national security appointment since assuming office, naming former Defense Minister, retired Major General Daniel Dee Ziankahn, as Director General of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) in a move that signals a fundamental shift in the government's strategy against transnational narcotics trafficking.

The appointment comes at a defining moment for Liberia's anti-drug campaign -- one marked by record cocaine seizures, allegations of institutional infiltration by organized crime, dismissals of senior security officials, and mounting international scrutiny over whether Liberia has become an emerging transit and storage hub for global narcotics syndicates.

Rather than selecting another career drug enforcement officer, President Boakai has entrusted the agency to one of the country's most experienced military minds, suggesting that the administration increasingly views narcotics trafficking not merely as a law enforcement problem but as a national security emergency.

Ziankahn's appointment follows months of extraordinary anti-narcotics operations that have transformed Liberia's security landscape.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The crisis reached international prominence after authorities intercepted approximately 237.6 kilograms of cocaine valued at about US$19 million at Roberts International Airport earlier this year. That operation exposed what investigators described as sophisticated trafficking methods involving airport operations and triggered an extensive criminal investigation.

Only weeks later, authorities executed an even more dramatic operation in Duazon, Margibi County, where investigators seized nearly 3.97 metric tons of suspected cocaine with an estimated international street value exceeding US$370 million -- one of the largest narcotics seizures ever recorded in Liberia and among the most significant in West Africa.

The scale of both seizures fundamentally altered perceptions of Liberia's role in international narcotics trafficking.

For years, security analysts had warned that West Africa was increasingly serving as a bridge between cocaine-producing regions in Latin America and lucrative consumer markets in Europe.

The Liberian seizures appeared to reinforce those concerns, suggesting that international trafficking organizations may have established increasingly sophisticated logistical networks within the country.

The investigations that followed produced consequences extending far beyond the drug seizures themselves.

As investigators traced the alleged trafficking operations, allegations emerged suggesting that elements within the security architecture may have been compromised.

President Boakai responded with an unprecedented series of administrative actions, dismissing, suspending and ordering investigations into officials from several security institutions, including the Liberia National Police (LNP), National Security Agency (NSA), Roberts International Airport (RIA), and the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency itself.

Those measures reflected the administration's determination to demonstrate that no institution would be insulated from accountability if credible evidence of misconduct emerged.

The actions also exposed what many analysts consider the greatest institutional threat confronting the country's anti-drug campaign: the possibility that sophisticated international criminal organizations may seek to infiltrate state institutions responsible for combating them.

Such concerns are not unique to Liberia.

Across the world, transnational narcotics organizations have historically relied not only on logistical sophistication but also on corruption, insider facilitation and institutional compromise.

Why Ziankahn?

Against that backdrop, President Boakai's choice of Daniel Dee Ziankahn appears highly strategic.

Unlike many previous leaders of the LDEA, Ziankahn arrives with decades of experience in military command, institutional reform and national security planning.

During his tenure as Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of Liberia (AFL), he became widely associated with efforts to professionalize Liberia's post-war military following years of civil conflict.

Working alongside international partners, including the United States, he helped oversee reforms aimed at transforming the AFL into a disciplined, professional institution operating under democratic civilian control.

His subsequent service as Minister of National Defense further expanded his experience managing complex security institutions and coordinating with regional and international partners.

More recently, Ziankahn has served as Military Adviser to President Boakai, providing strategic advice on national and regional security matters.

His appointment therefore brings together operational military leadership, institutional reform experience and direct presidential confidence.

Unlike a conventional law enforcement appointment, it places a seasoned strategic commander at the helm of the country's principal anti-narcotics agency.

The Executive Mansion emphasized that Ziankahn's appointment reflects the President's confidence in his "leadership, integrity, and operational experience," while assigning him direct responsibility for intensifying Liberia's campaign against illicit drugs and organized crime.

The President has also appointed to the LDEA Precious Rue as Deputy Director General for Operations and Prince Mulbah as Deputy Director General for Administration, pending Senate confirmation.

All three officials have been instructed to assume their responsibilities immediately in acting capacities.

The restructuring also returns Ernest Tarpeh to the National Security Agency, while former Officer-in-Charge Fitzgerald Biago has been indefinitely suspended from the Liberia National Police over ethical concerns pending further investigation.

Although the Ministry of Justice reportedly found no evidence directly linking Biago to narcotics trafficking, President Boakai concluded that ethical issues identified in the investigation warranted additional scrutiny.

That distinction reflects the administration's emerging message: legal innocence does not necessarily preclude administrative accountability where questions of institutional integrity arise.

Ziankahn's appointment inevitably raises broader questions about the evolving character of Liberia's anti-drug campaign.

Drug enforcement agencies traditionally operate as civilian law enforcement institutions emphasizing criminal investigations, prosecutions and intelligence gathering.

By selecting a retired four-star military officer to lead the LDEA, President Boakai appears to be elevating narcotics trafficking to the level of a national security threat.

That does not necessarily imply militarization of policing.

Rather, it suggests greater emphasis on intelligence coordination, operational discipline, inter-agency cooperation and strategic planning.

The President has directed the new leadership to work closely with the Ministry of Justice, Joint Security and international partners to dismantle trafficking networks, strengthen border controls and improve intelligence capabilities.

Such coordination will likely become increasingly important as investigations continue across multiple jurisdictions.

Liberia's response carries significance beyond its borders.

International partners -- including the United States, the European Union, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), ECOWAS and INTERPOL -- closely monitor countries serving as potential transit points for narcotics trafficking.

Major cocaine seizures often become tests of institutional credibility.

Foreign governments generally assess not only whether drugs are intercepted but also whether investigations reach the criminal networks responsible and whether compromised public officials are held accountable.

Close 

Boakai's successive dismissals, suspensions and institutional reforms therefore appear designed partly to reassure international partners that Liberia remains committed to confronting organized crime despite the scale of recent challenges.

Yet appointments alone cannot dismantle sophisticated international trafficking networks.

Experts note that sustainable success will depend on broader institutional reforms, including stronger financial investigations, improved border surveillance, enhanced intelligence-sharing, witness protection mechanisms, prosecutorial capacity and judicial efficiency.

Liberia must also continue strengthening airport security, maritime surveillance and anti-money laundering systems if it hopes to disrupt the financial infrastructure sustaining organized criminal enterprises.

Equally important will be restoring public confidence in institutions that recent investigations have exposed to allegations of misconduct.

Announcing the appointments, President Boakai reaffirmed that narcotics trafficking represents one of Liberia's gravest threats to national security, public health and national development.

"Our fight against drugs is a fight for the future of Liberia," the President declared. "We will continue to strengthen our institutions, hold public officials to the highest ethical standards, and pursue those who seek to poison our communities. There will be no safe haven for drug traffickers or those who aid and abet them."

Those remarks reinforce an earlier pledge made after the first major cocaine seizure that his administration would dismantle the criminal networks operating within Liberia rather than merely seize narcotics shipments.

The assignment, for Ziankahn, may become the most demanding chapter of a career spanning military leadership, defense policy and national security.

It also represents, for the President, a high-stakes bet that disciplined leadership, institutional credibility and strategic coordination can restore confidence in an agency whose reputation has been shaken by allegations of internal compromise.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Zambia Election Set for Closely Fought Opposition Battle

Zambia's 13 August election has become a closely contested battle between the ruling United Party for National Development and the Tonse-Pamodzi opposition alliance, led by newcomer Brian Mundubile and backed by former Patriotic Front structures. The election is expected to test the opposition's strength and serve as a referendum on President Hakainde Hichilema's record. The government has made progress on debt restructuring, economic growth and inflation. But the high cost of living remains a big concern for voters. The poll is also taking place amid concerns over alleged state interference, restrictions on opposition activity and controversial legislative changes, making it a key test for Zambia's democracy.

WHO Warns DR Congo Ebola Response Falling Behind

More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak. 60-70% of deaths occur in communities before patients reach treatment centres. The WHO said that the concentration of healthcare services in Bunia, Ituri province, is forcing patients to travel long distances and seek care too late. Poor transport systems may also increase transmission. The agency plans to expand treatment facilities closer to communities, add 400 Ebola beds and strengthen public awareness and early referrals. WHO is also looking to the town of Aru, where no new cases have been reported for two weeks after authorities expanded surveillance and response beyond individual patients to surrounding communities.



Nigeria Lassa Fever Cases Reach 1,000 in 2026

Nigeria has reported 1,000 confirmed cases of Lassa fever and 237 deaths in 2026, with cases reported in 23 states and 116 local government areas. Five states, Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue, account for 86% of confirmed cases. At least 53 healthcare workers have also been infected, prompting the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention to introduce a 30-day protection plan for frontline staff. The agency has said that late presentation, high treatment costs, poor sanitation and limited awareness are contributing to the outbreak and high fatality rate. Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic disease transmitted primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rodents.

Malawi Land Audit Flags Irregular Plot Allocations

Malawi's Ministry of Lands is set to release findings from a pilot land ownership audit in Lilongwe that reportedly uncovered irregularities in the allocation of plots in the affluent Area 3 and Area 10. The audit was launched in February 2026 to improve transparency and accountability in land administration. It is said to have identified politically exposed individuals, including current and former ministers, judges and MPs, among those allegedly linked to irregular land acquisitions. The findings could trigger political controversy, with questions remaining over whether those implicated will be publicly named or face legal or disciplinary action.

UN Somalia Auction Raises Security Concerns

The UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has opened a tender to auction vehicles, generators, IT equipment, medical supplies, construction machinery and other assets. This comes as Washington moves to end funding for the mission's logistical support by the end of 2026. UNSOS provides critical transport, fuel, food and other supplies to about 12,000 African troops and police serving under AUSSOM in the fight against al-Shabab. The auction has raised concerns among civil society groups over transparency and oversight. Regional leaders have warned that any premature reduction in international support could create a security vacuum as al-Shabab continues to operate in parts of Somalia.

Close 

Climate Change Shifts Africa's Malaria Risk

Climate change is reshaping malaria risk across Africa, with rising temperatures making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for transmission, according to a new Nature study. Some parts of West and Central Africa may have become too hot for optimal malaria transmission. The region still bears about 95% of the global malaria burden. But experts warn that climate change is only part of the equation, with funding gaps, drug and insecticide resistance, and weak health systems still major threats. They are urging countries in emerging risk areas to step up malaria prevention and surveillance while maintaining elimination efforts in high-burden areas.

World.title: South Africa: Immigrant Traders See Their Livelihoods Destroyed By March and March
World.content:
Traders with documents and permits chased away, leaving Bellville bus terminus market almost empty

Dozens of immigrant traders who usually traded at the Golden Arrow terminus in Bellville are staying away because of anti-immigrant protests.

When we visited the once bustling site last week, it was quiet with only a handful of traders. Many stalls were deserted.

Some traders we spoke to said they had tried to set up shop in other areas but were stopped. They have not traded at the bus site since the March and March 30 June "deadline" demanding "illegal immigrants" leave South Africa.



"I need to pay rent, put food on the table, and pay the bills," a Zimbabwean man who asked to remain anonymous told GroundUp.

He said he has been selling clothes in Bellville for about five years. He left Zimbabwe in 2008 when its economy collapsed.

While he has not been directly threatened, he has witnessed others being harassed.

"They will take your stuff and throw it on the ground," he said.

"It hurts, but as much as it hurts, it's their country, and they're also marginalised people."

Another trader, who introduced herself as Meye, said she has had a permit to trade since 2010. She fled the DRC in 2003.

"We are legal; everything is correct. But they say we are foreigners and we need to go back to our country."

A single mother of three, she says she is now struggling to feed and school her children.

Another single mother, Safia, says she has been unable to trade despite having refugee status and a trading permit. She came from Somalia in 2010.

She said law enforcement needs to protect the traders better.

"I can't sleep at night because of what is happening. I can't even pay my rent. I can't support my children," she said.

Abdulhakim Husein, Western Cape director of the Somalia Association of South Africa, told GroundUp that he had been assisting traders since the start of July.

He said many asylum seekers and refugees are traders as they have to rely on being self-employed. They came from Somalia, DRC, Zimbabwe, Angola and Burundi.

He said that at a meeting on 13 July (which the City confirmed), it was agreed that traders with valid permits should be allowed to trade. But on 14 July, they received a message warning them about a March and March protest in the area.

Husein said they have approached a legal NGO for assistance.

City spokesperson Luthando Tyhalibongo said foreign nationals whose immigration status has been verified by Home Affairs are permitted to trade with a valid permit. These cost R78 per month.

Close 

"It is a concern whenever permitted traders, whether South African citizens or foreign nationals lawfully permitted to trade, are prevented from engaging in legal economic activity," he said.

He said intimidation and threats should be reported to SAPS.

World.title: Pittsburgh Steelers set at 8.5 wins as Mike McCarthy takes over and Aaron Rodgers nears 43
World.content:

There is typically just one thing that I truly root for in almost every sport: a winning bet. However, there are times that I see a team or player I love or dislike and feel like I am at least somewhat rooting for their success or downfall. The Pittsburgh Steelers are a team that I kind of want to see fall apart for a variety of reasons, but will this be the year they do stumble?

Last year

It was a year of high expectations for the Steelers, and thanks to a bit of luck, they at least still made it to the postseason. Aaron Rodgers came in and increased their potential before the year began, and honestly, he had a pretty good season. Rodgers can be criticized for a lot of off-field oddities, but when he is between the lines, he is still pretty damn good. The problem with the Steelers last year was a lack of consistency. They had only two winning streaks; both were three games. They had some questionable losses — losing to the Bengals without Joe Burrow and the Browns led by Shedeur Sanders. They were incredibly lucky to beat the Ravens in the last game of the season, and then didn’t bother showing up against the Texans.

DEBUT OF FORMER STEELERS COACH MIKE TOMLIN ON NBC SNF HAD HIGHLIGHT MOMENTS BUT WAS TOO CAREFUL AND REHEARSED

Offseason additions and subtractions

That loss to the Texans seems to have led to the resignation of Mike Tomlin. After 19 seasons at the helm, none with a losing record, the team has turned to Mike McCarthy. How McCarthy continues to get jobs is a bit beyond me. He had success with Rodgers years ago, and is 174-112, but I feel like everywhere he goes comes up short of expectations. Maybe the problem is the expectations. He is trying to reshape a team that turned out 10+ wins basically every season. The team is banking that Rodgers can play well in his final season and added Michael Pittman Jr. as well as Germie Bernard to the receiving room. They also added a cornerback, Jamel Dean, who should help boost their defense.

Roster

World.title: Medicaid ends funding for child sex-change procedures as Trump admin slams 'experimental' treatments
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

FIRST ON FOX: American taxpayers will no longer be on the hook for child sex-change hormones or surgeries, as a key Trump administration agency announced Tuesday that Medicaid will stop funding such procedures and therapies.

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz tells Fox News Digital that the decision to implement a rule pulling the funding is "consistent with [the Trump administration's] commitment to protect children from experimental and life-altering sex-rejecting procedures that carry serious long-term health risks and lack sufficiently reliable evidence of clinical benefit."

CMS, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), says taxpayer-funded Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) will also cease coverage of sex-change hormones and surgeries.

SEN HAWLEY WARNS IT WOULD BE 'UNCONSCIONABLE' IF BILLIONS OF TAXPAYER FUNDS FLOW TO TRANS KIDS’ SEX CHANGES

The rule will not affect mental health treatments for gender dysmorphia and other conditions, which will continue to be covered under Medicaid and CHIP.

The move comes after years of what conservatives called 'woke' policies that opened avenues for federal funding of therapies and procedures to allow children to physically — and oftentimes permanently — transition from their biological sex before they could legally drive, get a tattoo or enlist in the U.S. Military.

"Children deserve our protection, not experimental interventions that pose serious risks and convey no proven benefits," Oz said. "By cutting off federal funds for these sex-rejecting procedures, we’re following the science, saving taxpayer dollars, and, most importantly, protecting children from potentially irreversible harm so they can truly flourish."

Specifically, the "sex-rejecting" treatments that will no longer be covered include cross-sex hormones, puberty blockers and sex-change surgical operations.

CMS and HHS say such procedures "can result in irreversible damage, including infertility, impaired sexual function, diminished bone density, altered brain development, and other lasting physiological effects."

HHS, under Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., reviewed national and international research on sex-change procedures in minors, which ultimately informed CMS' decision to reverse federal taxpayer-funded procedures.

COLORADO SUPREME COURT ORDERS CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL TO RESUME GENDER TRANSITION TREATMENTS FOR MINORS

"Today, we are ending federal taxpayer funding for sex-rejecting procedures on children," Secretary Kennedy said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "These interventions carry serious risks and can cause irreversible harm. The federal government will no longer use Medicaid and CHIP dollars to fund procedures that fail to meet the evidentiary standard our children deserve."

That research "identified significant evidence gaps" and "documented serious safety concerns," eventually leading to the conclusion that taxpayer funding for such procedures could not be justified comparative to the risks.

Specifically, CMS pointed to the United Kingdom's Cass Review as one of the cornerstone pieces of research informing the decision.

That review, conducted by Dr. Hilary Cass, concluded in 2024 that research on medical interventions like cross-sex hormones and puberty blockers was limited and not definitive. The report also said that medical interventions had developed significantly faster than evidence proving those interventions were safe.

LARGEST CHILDREN’S HOSPITAL IN US TO OPEN ‘DETRANSITION CLINIC’ AFTER $10M SETTLEMENT WITH TRUMP DOJ, STATE

"The Trump Administration is drawing a clear line: America’s children will not be subjected to life-altering interventions on the taxpayer’s dime without reliable evidence of safety and clinical benefit," HHS Press Secretary Emily Hilliard told Fox News Digital.

"Under the leadership of Secretary Kennedy, federal health care dollars will support evidence-based care that protects children and puts their long-term health first," she added. "American taxpayers should never be forced to finance interventions when the evidence of benefit is insufficient and the potential consequences for children can be serious and irreversible."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

What follows is a tapering-off period where the Medicaid and CHIP funding will slowly phase out and allow children who are currently getting hormone treatments to receive funding for six months from the date the new rule takes effect.

World.title: I lost my wife on 9/11. Please let this 25th anniversary belong to the families
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Twenty-five years ago, on September 11, 2001, my wife Grace was at her desk on the 105th floor of the North Tower. She was 29 years old. She will always be 29 years old.

Twenty-five years is long enough to learn that grief doesn't end. It learns your calendar. Somewhere in early August it starts: the tightening, the bracing, the counting down to the morning I return to the place where Grace was taken from us.

It’s there that I, along with every other family at Ground Zero, remember our own Grace. We remember how she was the kind of person the rest of us build our lives around without ever realizing it. We remember how her last summer, her sister told us another baby was coming, and Grace hoped out loud for a girl. It was a girl, they named her Grace. That little girl is twenty-four now, and everything she knows about her aunt is a story someone told her. In Grace's memorial guest book, a friend called her a brilliant light to everyone who knew her. She was, and the world lost nearly three thousand lights that morning. Every one of them was somebody's Grace.

9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

The ceremony itself is the one mercy in it all. The bell at 8:46. The silence. The names, all 2,983 of them, read out loud by loved ones, for hours, until every single person is remembered. No speeches, no politicians at the microphone, just the names. Whoever built it that way understood something: for one morning a year, the most famous piece of ground in America belongs to ordinary grieving people, and to no one else.

That morning is getting harder to protect. Every year there are more cameras, more commentary, more people with something to say standing near people who came to mourn. And this year, the twenty-fifth, the year it should be most sacred, the story is already not about the victims. It's about the mayor.

For weeks now, the coverage of this anniversary has been an argument about the Mayor of New York City. Whether he'll attend, what his presence means, what he said, what he meant, who's offended, who's defending him. Every one of those stories is a story that is not about the 2,983 people who were murdered, and every day of it, asks grieving families to spend the season we need for remembering on a political argument instead.

TUNNEL TO TOWERS ANNOUNCES 'STEEL ACROSS AMERICA' TOUR TO MARK 25 YEARS SINCE 9/11 ATTACKS

We are one month from the 25th anniversary of the worst day of most of our lives. So I will be plain about why so many of us cannot treat this mayor as just another dignitary in the crowd. In 2020, he called the NYPD "racist, anti-queer & a major threat to public safety" and demanded it be defunded. Twenty-three NYPD officers died saving people in those towers, and their names are cut into the memorial he would stand beside. When New Yorkers asked him, again and again, to condemn the phrase "globalize the intifada," a phrase many of us hear as a call for more mornings like the one that took Grace, he said it means different things to different people. He has praised a Brooklyn imam who served as a character witness for the Blind Sheikh, the man convicted of plotting terror attacks against this city. To the families in that plaza, these are wounds.

The anniversary of September 11th asks one thing of everyone who stands on that ground: an unambiguous rejection of the violence and the ideology that caused it, without hesitation and without ambiguity. The families should not have to wonder where their mayor stands.

When the cameras find him, and they will find him, the day stops belonging to the families and starts belonging to the fight.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That's why I started a petition on Change.org asking that this year's ceremony stay focused on the victims and their families. More than 83,000 people have joined me by signing the petition at change.org/911Ceremony. Not because they hate anyone, because they want one morning free of political controversy.

So this is my ask of the mayor, and it's a simple one: on the morning of September 11th, let the families have the plaza. Removing a distraction isn't a punishment, it's a kindness.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Grief doesn't have a party. It doesn't care who you voted for. Somewhere in those hours of names next month, a voice will say "Grace Catherine Galante," and for a few seconds the whole world will hold just her. That is what the morning is for.

Twenty-five years. One morning. Let us have it.

World.title: College football coaches on hot seat: Bill Belichick, Mike Norvell and others facing make-or-break 2026
World.content:
We are just three weeks away from the college football season getting underway, which means that it's time to start discussing which coaches are fighting for their jobs in 2026.

In case you weren’t paying attention to the chaos that transpired during the 2025 season, schools are no longer hesitating when it comes to pulling the trigger on what could be a very expensive decision to restart their football programs with a new coach.

Right now, the stakes couldn’t get any higher from a financial standpoint. The insane amount of money being spent on rosters through revenue-sharing, NIL payouts and these third-party deals with athletes are at an all-time high.

UNC WANTED THE DEION SANDERS EFFECT WITH BILL BELICHICK, ALONG WITH WINS. SO FAR, IT'S GOTTEN SOMETHING MUCH DIFFERENT

So, that obviously means athletic departments across the country are looking for a return on investment not only for their financial future, but also staying relevant in the ever changing world of college athletics.

There are teams spending upwards of $50 million on their rosters this season, while others are hovering around the $30 million area depending on the buy-in from each athletic department. No, not every school can afford a roster like LSU, Texas Tech, Ohio State or Oregon, but that's no longer an excuse that can be used by those programs that are outside the spectrum.

Since we are living in a different era, this has become a further cut-throat sport where athletic departments can no longer give coaches four to five years to rebuild a program.

'HOT SEAT RANKINGS' FOR ALL 16 SEC COACHES AS BEGINNING OF 2026 COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON DRAWS NEARER

Which coaches are sitting on scolding hot seats?

If the 2025 season was any indication, schools are no longer waiting until December to make a move on firing their head coach. Now, with the transfer portal and insane spending on rosters, the clock is ticking for a number of coaches in 2026.

INSIDE CFP EXPANSION BATTLE AS SEC, BIG TEN AND TV NETWORKS FIGHT FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S NEXT BIG MOVE

Mike Norvell (Florida State)

Coming off the Seminoles' fourth losing season in Norvell's six years as head coach at Florida State, the pressure is on for this once powerful ACC program to make some noise in 2026. No, I don't mean beating Alabama and grabbing the attention of the college football world for a few weeks. It's time for Mike Norvell to get FSU back into the CFP conversation. If he doesn’t, then the FSU administration will have to make the tough financial decision to pay the $46 million buyout and make their next hire, like they quietly tried to do last season according to Lane Kiffin.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS FINALLY BACK AFTER MONTHS OF NCAA LAWSUITS, NIL DRAMA AND CONGRESSIONAL FIGHTS

Luke Fickell (Wisconsin)

Enough with the games, Wisconsin. If Fickell puts up a third straight losing season, he might not even make it to the final weekend for the Badgers to make the move in ousting the Wisconsin coach. When athletic director Chris McIntosh decided he would retain the Badgers head coach following an abysmal 2025 season and provide Luke with additional NIL funds to piece together a roster that could put up a stronger fight, he did so just months before Shawn Eichorst took over for him. That means Fickell is already facing the realization that his new boss will not be providing a long leash in Madison, Wisconsin, this year. Could we see another James Franklin type firing just two months into season?

This experiment is already off to a rocky start, coming off a 4-8 season last year. Now, with multiple off-field storylines overtaking the front pages of the Chapel Hill newspapers, led by the awkward presence of girlfriend Jordon Hudson, the ongoing HR investigation into general manager Michael Lombardi and the tension within the athletic department, the legendary NFL coach is one bad loss in Ireland to TCU from potentially seeing the ship sink. North Carolina board of trustee members did not initiate this hire for Belichick to turn the Tar Heels into the laughing stock of college football with his "33rd NFL team." But, here we are, with two more years of $10 million per season guaranteed. If this gets ugly early in the season, does UNC pull the trigger and appoint offensive coordinator Bobby Petrino as interim head coach? Yep, you read that right.

DABO SWINNEY IS RIGHT: COACHES OPINIONS DON’T MATTER IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF EXPANSION FIGHT

Mike Locksley (Maryland)

Even though the Maryland head coach mentioned that his program is turning the corner and the bad days are behind the Terrapins, words only go so far with a fan base looking to see their team in the Big Ten conversation. Back-to-back 4-8 seasons have donors and the athletic department wondering how much longer they can afford to see their beloved Terrapins meddle around in the highly-competitive Big Ten, even though Locksley has a very talented quarterback in Malik Washington that will be entertaining to watch this season. It's time for Mike to back up his words in 2026.

Honorable Mention (Keep an eye out, in no particular order)

Shane Beamer (South Carolina. The Gamecocks could be a sleeper-team in the SEC. But, if not..) Lincoln Riley (USC. Just pay attention if things get rough) Bill O’Brien (Boston College) Scott Satterfield (Cincinnati) Dabo Swinney (Clemson. Just pay attention if things get rough)

OK, so there ya have it. Don't worry, there will be a number of names that could pop up out of nowhere this season that we don't see coming as we get going later this month.

World.title: Michigan rescuers find family stranded for 3 days after tubing trip in dramatic video
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Heart-pounding new video shows the moment a family of three stranded in the wilderness for three days were rescued after getting lost while tubing on a Michigan river.

Video shows members of the Michigan Department of Natural Resources and a Michigan State Police K-9 unit successfully locating Jazman Hock, her cousin Sarah Vida, and Sarah's 9-year-old son, Kayden Kovalcik on Aug. 8 after the trio had been stranded while water tubing on the Muskegon River

The footage also reveals the moment state troopers and the resource workers locating the stranded wayfarers, with one rescuer instructing them to "Make some noise... Yell!" as the officials closed in on the family.

Rescuers waded through thick forest grass as they called out to the group before finally reaching the family.

MONTANA TEEN THROWS LASSO TO MAN IN YELLOWSTONE RIVER IN SPLIT-SECOND RESCUE

One of the women was cut up and wearing a bathing suit while Kovalick was shirtless. The group had been water tubing on the Muskegon River when their rafts, which were only meant to be used in a pool, broke apart and left them stranded, Jazman's mother Teresa Hock told WWMT.

The family can be heard telling their rescue team what happened.

"We got lost on the river," the shirtless Kovalcik explained.

FIREFIGHTERS, POLICE PULL YOUNG WOMAN FROM SEWAGE-FILLED RAVINE AFTER DAYS TRAPPED IN 104-DEGREE HEAT

"We went to the river and we were on the river for four hours," he continued.

The rescuers appeared audibly shaken, as one exasperated "oh my God" multiple times. Another hugged one of the two women, repeatedly telling her "good job, good job."

It's unclear which of the two women he's speaking to, but one rescuer tells her "let's have you sit down, you are cut up. You're not going to be able to walk very good, are you?"

"I'm forcing myself," she replies.

TERRIFIED HIKERS FACE NIGHTMARE SURVIVAL SCENARIO AFTER HEART-POUNDING GRIZZLY BEAR ENCOUNTER

While the trio had packed protein bars and water, they gave all the food to the young Kovalcik, Hock told WWMT, while the two women survived on flowers, bark and ants.

"We are relieved to report that Jazman Hock, Sarah Vida, and Kayden Kovalcik have been located alive and safe. This is the outcome everyone involved had hoped for. We are incredibly grateful for the tireless efforts of the many law enforcement agencies, fire departments, emergency responders, search and rescue teams, and volunteers who dedicated countless hours to this search," Michigan State Police said in a post on X.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Jazman, Sarah, and Kayden were located safe by an MSP K-9 team and Michigan DNR Conservation Officers approximately three-quarters of a mile northeast of the Mill Iron Rd Boat Launch at 4:36 pm. It was truly remarkable to see so many highly trained professionals from multiple agencies come together by establishing a Unified Command, share resources, and work as one team toward a common goal," the post concluded.

Fox News Digital contacted Michigan State Police and Michigan Department of Natural Resources for further comment.

World.title: Blue Jays-Red Sox game thrown into chaos by 17-minute 'rules check,' massive scoreboard mistake
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Everything seems to be going right for the Boston Red Sox.

OK, not everything, as they have now lost three games in a row, but not before going on an insane stretch that saw them win 32 of their previous 37 games.

After losing their final two games against the Athletics over the weekend, the Sox traveled to Toronto to take on the lowly Blue Jays, where they found themselves trailing 2-1 in the seventh inning with runners on the corners and one out.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Yet on a fly ball to center field, both runners took off because they believed there were two outs. Taking advantage of the situation, the Jays turned a double play to end the inning. However, chaos, including a 17-minute delay, ensued when a run was actually awarded to the Sox despite the costly mistake.

Center fielder Brett Bateman made the catch and threw the ball into the infield. Once the ball was thrown to first before Nick Sogard could return, the inning appeared to be over. However, a wild MLB rule states that since the runner was out at first after Anthony Siegler crossed home plate, and the Blue Jays did not appeal Siegler as the "fourth out," the run scored.

It turns out Siegler and Sogard had a justifiable reason to believe there were two outs because the main scoreboard at Rogers Centre actually showed two outs.

"We kind of got a break there," Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy admitted.

MIKE TROUT GOLF OUTING GOES FROM TEAM-BONDING EVENT TO AWKWARD MLB TRADE DEADLINE MESS FOR ANGELS

Blue Jays manager John Schneider, though, claimed that his team was never given the chance to appeal at third, because plate umpire Charlie Ramos "waved off the run."

"After consulting with MLB, they told me that all of my players were across the third base line before Charlie waved off the run, which I 100% disagree with," Schneider said. "I don’t know if [Vladimir Guerrero Jr.] is that fast after he got the ball at first."

"We felt like it was our obligation to correct the error for not scoring the run originally," crew chief Chris Guccione said after the game.

"The rule is the rule. ... So if the run scores from third, no matter what he did tagging up, or not, before the out is recorded at first, the run counts," Schneider said. "Now, if we had just thrown the ball to third instead of first, obviously different story."

Despite the lucky break, the Sox's red-hot offense was stalled, as they lost a third consecutive game for the first time since June 16-18.

World.title: Barred Little League team from Tulsa gets reinstated for chance to play in World Series
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Little League Baseball is on fire even before the big days in Williamsport, Pennsylvania.

Little League on Monday ruled that Tulsa National Little League's 12U team had an ineligible player on the roster and booted it from the Southwest Region Tournament, the final stop before the Little League World Series.

However, a Texas judge reinstated the team just hours later through a temporary restraining order, despite Little League saying its decision was "final and binding."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Thus, Tulsa National Little League is set to face Boerne Little League, representing Texas West, on Tuesday at 6 p.m. ET in Waco, with a trip to Williamsport on the line.

Little League initially ruled that Boerne Little League's Monday game against Louisiana (Ascension Parish Little League) would be for the Southwest championship — Boerne won 4-1 and celebrated on the field, thinking it had just earned a trip to every child's dream.

However, it now must play one more game against a team with an ineligible player.

Little League did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

"Judge [Ryan] Luna made the right decision to give the boys an opportunity to play the game and decide everything on the field," Tulsa National's attorney, Christian Dennie, said, via News on 6. "These boys are ball players and ball players do just that — play ball.

MIKE TROUT GOLF OUTING GOES FROM TEAM-BONDING EVENT TO AWKWARD MLB TRADE DEADLINE MESS FOR ANGELS

"Legally, I find it surprising that an esteemed organization would withhold the protest documentation from this ball club and decide their fate in a cloak of darkness. Simply put, the law does not allow for arbitrary and capricious actions."

Little League said its decision came after "a recent protest related to the eligibility of players on the Tulsa National Little League Baseball team." It is not clear which player is ineligible, nor is the reason. Tulsa National Little League's softball team was recently removed from the Little League Softball Southwest Region Tournament for a separate eligibility case.

"To uphold the integrity of the International Tournament and provide an opportunity for every team, community, and, most importantly, child, to have a fair and equitable experience, Little League International relies on adult volunteers and parents to adhere to our Rules, Regulations, and Operating Policies," Little League said in its announcement.

World.title: Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs chooses former Republican as running mate in re-election bid
World.content:
Arizona’s Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs has chosen a former Republican as her running mate for her re-election bid this November.

On Tuesday, Hobbs named John Giles, who served as a GOP mayor of Mesa, Arizona, from 2014 to 2025, as her pick for lieutenant governor.

In a joint video announcement with Giles, Hobbs said she has fought for Arizonans as governor by cutting taxes, securing the border and supporting public safety.

“Now, for the first time in our state’s history, we are electing a governor and lieutenant governor on the same ticket. And the first thing I looked for in a running mate was someone who shares that value of putting Arizonans ahead of partisan politics,” Hobbs said.

Giles said, “I was a lifelong Republican before becoming an independent because extremists shouldn’t stand in the way of getting things done.”

Giles changed his party affiliation to independent in May and voted in the Democratic primary last month, Hobbs’ communications director Michael Beyer confirmed to NBC News.

Voters will elect a lieutenant governor for the first time this fall after a ballot measure creating the position was approved in the 2022 election.

The New York Times was first to report on Hobbs’ plans.

Hobbs faces a competitive race against Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., who previously chaired the conservative House Freedom Caucus and has served in Congress since 2017. Biggs has selected former state lawmaker Sine Kerr as his running mate. Biggs won the Republican primary last month, beating fellow Rep. David Schweikert and businessmen Scott Neely and Ken Miceli.

While mayor of Mesa, Giles endorsed then-Vice President Kamala Harris for president in the 2024 election and spoke at the Democratic National Convention in Chicago that year about his disappointment with the Republican Party.

“I’m a lifelong Republican, so I feel a little out of place tonight. But I feel more at home here than in today’s Republican Party,” Giles said in his remarks. “The Grand Old Party has been kidnapped by extremists and devolved into a cult — the cult of Donald Trump.”

He added, “I have an urgent message for the majority of Americans who, like me, are in the political middle. John McCain’s Republican Party is gone, and we don’t owe a damn thing to what’s been left behind.”

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rated the governor’s race as leaning Democratic in the battleground state, which President Donald Trump carried in 2016 and 2024 and Joe Biden won in 2020.

In 2022, Hobbs defeated Republican Kari Lake in the gubernatorial election by less than 1 percentage point. Before serving as governor, Hobbs was Arizona’s secretary of state and was also the minority leader in the state Senate and a member of the state House.

Hobbs recently formed a coalition of former and current Republican and independent leaders who support her re-election, which included Giles and more than 50 other business leaders and officials.

The Democratic incumbent has touted her record of working across the aisle, including signing more than 900 pieces of bipartisan legislation into law, according to her campaign. She has also highlighted her efforts to expand affordable housing, secure the border and her repeal of the state’s 1864 total abortion ban

Biggs, meanwhile, has promoted his relationship with Trump and has run on a campaign touting his support for lowering taxes and border security.

World.title: Jury in Luigi Mangione’s state trial will be anonymous, judge rules
World.content:
Luigi Mangione appeared in a New York courtroom Tuesday where plans were nearly finalized for his state murder trial next month, including the judge’s ruling that the jury of Manhattan residents will be anonymous.

Mangione, 28, has pleaded not guilty to several state charges in connection with the December 2024 fatal shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson outside the New York Hilton Midtown.

At Tuesday’s hearing, Justice Gregory Carro ordered the parties to team up on crafting a jury questionnaire — a task that could prove challenging given the case’s notoriety. Jury selection is set to begin Sept. 8.

Luigi Mangione attends a court hearing on May 18, 2026. Jeenah Moon / Pool via AFP-Getty Images

If convicted, Mangione faces up to life in prison.

It was unclear when the jury questionnaire would be finalized, but Mangione’s side told NBC News that they expect to have a proposed draft this week. The parties are expected to coordinate on a survey that will address the concerns of each side identify out potential jurors who may be biased.

Jurors who make it past the initial screening process will then face additional vetting in a process known as voir dire. Questionnaires are designed for the parties and judge to get a preliminary sense of a jury candidate’s background and beliefs.

On Tuesday, the courtroom was filled with journalists and some Mangione proponents, who were wearing green, a color that appeared to reference the Luigi character from the iconic Nintendo Super Mario games and subsequent movies.

Mangione entered the courtroom from a holding area wearing a gray suit. He glanced around the room before taking his seat next to his attorneys Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Marc Agnifilo and Jacob Kaplan.

Carro ruled at the start of the hearing that the jury would be anonymous, a designation that is becoming increasingly common in high-profile cases in New York.

Carro also said there would be expanded media and public access to the trial. After fielding complaints from Mangione’s defense team about potential space limitations, court administrators arranged for an overflow room.

“It has always been under consideration. They had to find the physical place, and it had to be staffed,” Carro said.

Prior to the conference, the defense and prosecution sparred over how much space would be available for members of the media and public to view the trial.

The defense accused the Manhattan district attorney’s office of unfairly trying to limit the number of attendees, which they argued would also shape the type of coverage that the trial received.

Prosecutors objected to those characterizations but also raised concerns about witness exposure.

“We are particularly concerned about the possibility that a spectator in an overflow room will clandestinely record the proceedings and share any such recordings with others,” prosecutor Joel Seidemann wrote in an Aug. 10 letter.

Marc Agnifilo, one of Mangione’s lawyers, said outside the courthouse that he was glad the court arranged for extra space.

“I think it actually changed the complexion of the coverage of the trial. ... I think there should be two overflow rooms, but I’ll take one,” Agnifilo said.

Mangione’s case has garnered international headlines, with mostly female supporters who have appeared in court throughout the pretrial hearings and argue that the killing was justified.

Prosecutors allege Mangione was motivated by an animus toward the health insurance industry, but he was never a UnitedHealthcare customer. He had no connection to Thompson, a father of two from Minnesota.

Prosecutors say Mangione trailed Thompson and identified his movements in New York, where the prominent healthcare executive was attending his company’s investors conference.

Prosecutors allege that Mangione shot Thompson from behind outside the hotel, then fled the city. He was apprehended several days later in Altoona, Pennsylvania, after a McDonald’s employee called the police.

Former Manhattan prosecutor Rebecca Roiphe told NBC News that during jury selection, prosecutors will likely want to scrutinize potential jurors’ experiences in the healthcare system to weed out those who might sympathize with Mangione.

“I think the prosecution is clearly going to want to keep off people who have some kind of ax to grind about healthcare,” Roiphe said.

Roiphe, who is a criminal law and ethics professor at New York Law School, believes the defense will seek panelists with a “healthcare-for-all mindset.”

Roiphe said attorneys will also pay close attention to jurors’ attitudes toward law enforcement and politics, even though aspects of Mangione’s case do not seem to strictly apply to a partisan viewpoint.

Mangione separately faces federal stalking-related charges in New York and has pleaded not guilty. The Justice Department was seeking the death penalty in the federal case, but that option was taken off the table earlier this year.

U.S. District Judge Margaret Garnett issued a ruling in January that effectively blocks New York federal prosecutors from pursuing a capital case.

The son of Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., was arrested on charges of sexual exploitation of a child, authorities said Monday.

Tyler Boebert did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

“I love my son,” Lauren Boebert said in a statement Monday. “We take allegations very seriously and pray for everyone affected during this challenging time.”

It was not immediately clear whether Tyler Boebert has a lawyer to speak on his behalf. An attorney who previously represented him in a separate case did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The charges are linked to a 2024 video Tyler Boebert allegedly recorded with a 17-year-old, according to an affidavit in support of an arrest warrant. He was 18 at the time.

The 17-year-old’s mother later alerted authorities that a video showing her daughter and Tyler Boebert having sex was posted on Instagram, the affidavit says. The affidavit does not say who is alleged to have posted the video.

Tyler Boebert was charged with three counts of sexual exploitation of a child and two counts of contributing to the delinquency of a minor, court records show.

He was previously arrested on charges police described as a string of vehicle trespass and property thefts.

That case continues, according to Colorado Public Radio.

After her son was arrested in 2024, Lauren Boebert said he had been through “some very difficult, public challenges for a young man and the subject of attention that he didn’t ask for.”

“It breaks my heart to see my child struggling and, in this situation, especially when he has been provided multiple opportunities to get his life on track,” she said. “I will never give up on him, and I will continue to be there for him.”
