Kerala Health Minister K Muraleedharan on Tuesday said right-wing political commentator TG Mohandas secured bail due to a âloopholeâ after his arrest over alleged remarks on a student protest in New Delhi, while BJP MLA V Muraleedharan described the action against him as âselective retaliationâ by the state government.Mohandas was arrested by Kerala Police on Monday morning over remarks allegedly made in a YouTube video about a protest by students in the national capital over the NEET paper leak. He was released on bail later the same day.Muraleedharan said he had been informed that the prosecution's case was not presented effectively and that the government would examine the reasons for it and take appropriate action.âHe was booked for offences for which it was not easy to get bail, as that was the kind of statements he made. He got bail on a loophole. Nevertheless, the government will take stringent steps in the matter,â the minister told reporters.BJP leader V Muraleedharan, however, questioned the government's decision to act against Mohandas, saying there may be differing views on his remarks but alleged that no action had been taken against people who made âheinousâ comments about Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his mother.He said the action against Mohandas indicated that the government was selectively targeting individuals while protecting others.Mohandas has been charged under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Information Technology Act and the Kerala Police Act. The case was registered following a complaint alleging that videos uploaded on his YouTube channel, 'Pathrika', were intended to disturb public order and create fear and unrest.In the video, Mohandas allegedly said the student protest in Delhi could lead to incidents of gang rape and made derogatory remarks about women participating in the demonstration. He also allegedly claimed that some people could be killed or permanently injured during the protest and that their bodies would subsequently be taken to hospitals.

World.title: 'Taking matter seriously': Aviation minister as turbulence-hit Air India flight pilot fails 2nd dope test
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu on Tuesday said the ministry is taking the matter seriously and has sought an update from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) on the existing regulations, after the confirmatory dope test of the pilot-in-command of an Air India Phuket-Delhi flight returned positive.

When asked about possible changes to the rules, Naidu said, âThat issue we are continuously studying. We have also asked DGCA for updates on that. We are taking it very seriously. If we feel that the present regulation is not up to the mark, we will respond to it very seriously and improve whatever needs to be done.â

The development comes after the August 4 Phuket-Delhi Air India flight AI 2379 experienced a sudden loss of altitude of around 300 feet during cruise, leaving several passengers and crew members injured.

The Airbus A320 later landed safely in Delhi, while 17 people were subsequently hospitalised.

The pilot-in-command's initial psychoactive substance screening test conducted after the aircraft landed in Delhi was reported as ânon-negativeâ, following which a confirmatory test was carried out as per procedure.

DGCA working on stricter testing requirements

The DGCA is now working on stricter dope-testing requirements for flight crew, with the aim of creating a stronger deterrent against substance abuse among pilots.





Under the existing rules, a crew member whose screening test is non-negative is immediately removed from safety-sensitive duties until the confirmatory report is received. If the first confirmatory test is positive, the employee is referred for de-addiction and rehabilitation.

A pilot can return to active flying after rehabilitation and a subsequent negative dope test. However, if the pilot tests positive again after resuming flying, the licence can be suspended for three years.

A third positive test can lead to cancellation of the flying licence.

AAIB begins probe

The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has taken up the investigation into the August 4 Air India AI 2379 Phuket-Delhi incident under applicable provisions and ICAO protocols.

This includes examination of the aircraft and its systems, recorded flight data, relevant operational and maintenance records, medical information, and interviews with persons concerned.

The objective is to determine the circumstances and contributing factors behind the incident and identify safety measures to prevent a recurrence. It also cautioned against drawing conclusions from isolated or incomplete information before the investigation is complete, it reads further.

World.title: Centre likely to send FCRA Bill to JPC amid opposition
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre is likely to send the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) Amendment Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) for detailed scrutiny, amid objections from Christian representatives and opposition parties, news agency ANI reported citing sources.The Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, seeks to amend the FCRA, 2010, which regulates the acceptance and utilisation of foreign contributions by individuals, associations and companies in India.Although the Bill has not yet been listed for consideration and passage in the Lok Sabha, the government had earlier indicated that it could be taken up on August 12.According to sources, Christian representatives met Union home minister Amit Shah and sought either withdrawal of the Bill or its referral to a JPC, citing concerns over its provisions.The development follows a meeting between Mizoram chief minister Lalduhoma and Shah, during which the chief minister raised regional concerns and submitted recommendations on the proposed legislation. Lalduhoma was accompanied by Reverend John Raldosanga, chairman of the Mizoram Kohhran Hruaitu Committee (MKHC), and Reverend Lalhmangaiha, general secretary of the Council of Churches in Mizoram (CCM)."The only thing that is very clearly mentioned to us is that it's not going to be retrospective.That assurance was given to us, and the rest of the points will be given a paragraph-wise comment by him... the discussion on the 12th of this month in Parliament," Lalduhoma had said.Separately, a delegation led by DMK leader P Wilson met Shah and submitted a memorandum raising concerns that the proposed legislation "impacts religious minorities and civil society".The delegation also flagged provisions including Section 14B and Chapter IIIA, arguing that delays on the FCRA Online Portal or minor technical non-compliances could lead to automatic cessation of registration and trigger the provisional or permanent vesting of assets with a state-notified Designated Authority.A major proposed change is the creation of a Designated Authority to oversee foreign contributions and assets belonging to organisations whose FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases to remain valid.Under the proposed provisions, an organisation losing its FCRA registration would initially have its foreign contributions and assets vested provisionally with the Designated Authority. If its registration is restored or renewed within the prescribed period, the assets and unused foreign funds would be returned. Otherwise, the assets could vest permanently with the authority.The Bill also provides for cessation of an FCRA certificate following its expiry, non-renewal or refusal of renewal, including in cases where an organisation becomes defunct or its registration ceases.For assets such as places of worship, the proposed law requires the Designated Authority to preserve their religious character. It also provides for revision and judicial appeal against orders issued by the authority.The Bill proposes changes to the penalty framework as well, including reducing the maximum imprisonment for violations from five years to one year. It further proposes that state agencies obtain prior approval from the Centre before launching investigations under the FCRA.Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu assembly adopted a state government sponsored resolution urging the Centre to withdraw the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill, alleging it may adversely affect the autonomy of charitable organisations and functioning of institutions run by minorities.The monsoon session of Parliament began on July 20 and is scheduled to conclude on August 13. Proceedings have repeatedly been disrupted by opposition protests over several issues, including Delhi Police action against protesters on July 20. Several Bills have been passed in the Lok Sabha amid opposition protests and limited debate.

World.title: Phuket-Delhi AI flight captain's confirmatory test also positive for : Sources
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The confirmatory dope test of the pilot-in-command (PIC) operating Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight last Tuesday has also come positive, say sources. His screening test done on arrival was "non negative" and then as per procedure, a confirmatory test was conducted whose report came Tuesday.

Sources say the plot has tested positive for marijuana, which is commonly known as weed. The DGCA is now working for more strict dope test requirements to act as an effective deterrent.

Meanwhile, aviation secretary Samir Sinha called Air India's outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson where officials of the DGCA and AAIB were present. The officials asked AI to ensure safety of operations from all aspects and asked what steps is the airline taking to the effect.

Also read |

The pilots of Air Indiaâs August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight, which had experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet during cruise, were subjected to psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival at the destination. The pilot-in-command or captainâs screening test report was ânot negativeâ and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said Sunday.

The ministry has classified the incident, which led to 17 people being hospitalised, as a serious one and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will probe it.





âFurther action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,â government said.

Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) rules stipulate that âin case the screening test (for psychoactive substances) is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received. In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisationâ for de-addiction.

Multiple passengers and cabin crew members on board the Airbus A320 operating as AI 2379 were injured when it suddenly lost altitude. The plane later landed safely in Delhi. âAs standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing.

Samples have accordingly been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,â the ministry statement added.

Both the pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA pending investigation.ââ¦ firmly committed to highest standards of aviation safety and ensuring that all such occurrences are thoroughly investigated and appropriate action is taken in accordance with the prescribed regulations and procedures,â the statement added.

Authorities are probing this case from all angles including what caused the sudden of altitude, weather or something else; the handling of this event; impact on the aircraft like did it suffer hydraulic failure due to impact and whether it should have flown all the way to Delhi after the episode and not diverted to some nearby airport like Varanasi or Lucknow.
